signals.title: Azure OpenAI Cognitive Services endpoint: Responses API does not append ?api-version=, cannot use gpt-5.x-codex models
signals.text: ### Description **Summary:** When using OpenCode with Azure OpenAI Cognitive Services endpoints (i.e. `https://<resource>.cognitiveservices.azure.com/openai`), the Responses API (`/responses`) requests are missing the required `?api-version=...` query parameter. This causes all requests to `/openai/responses` to return 404, even though the same endpoint works with tools like `curl`. **Impact:** - Cannot use models that require the Responses API (e.g. `gpt-5.2-codex`) on Azure Cognitive Services endpoints. - Azure returns `404 Resource not found` when `?api-version=` is missing from the request URL. - The same request succeeds via `curl` when `?api-version=2025-04-01-preview` is included manually. **Working curl example:** ```bash curl -X POST "https://<resource>.cognitiveservices.azure.com/openai/responses?api-version=2025-04-01-preview" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $AZURE_API_KEY" \ -d '{ "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hello"}], "max_completion_tokens": 16384, "model": "gpt-5.2-codex" }' ``` --- **Config attempts and results:** **Attempt 1: Standard `@ai-sdk/azure` with `resourceName`** ```json { "provider": { "azure": { "npm": "@ai-sdk/azure", "options": { "apiKey": "<REDACTED>", "resourceName": "<REDACTED>", "apiVersion": "2025-04-01-preview" }, "models": { "gpt-5.2-codex": { "name": "GPT 5.2 Codex", "provider": { "npm": "@ai-sdk/azure" } } } } } } ``` **Result:** SDK constructs URL with `.openai.azure.com` hostname (wrong — Cognitive Services uses `.cognitiveservices.azure.com`), and hits `/v1/chat/completions` instead of `/responses`. Error: `The chatCompletion operation does not work with the specified model, gpt-5.2-codex`. **Attempt 2: `@ai-sdk/azure` with `baseURL` override** ```json { "provider": { "azure": { "npm": "@ai-sdk/azure", "options": { "apiKey": "<REDACTED>", "baseURL": "https://<resource>.cognitiveservices.azure.com/openai", "apiVersion": "2025-04-01-preview" }, "models": { "gpt-5.2-codex": { "name": "GPT 5.2 Codex", "provider": { "npm": "@ai-sdk/azure" } } } } } } ``` **Result:** URL hits `/openai/responses` (correct path) but `?api-version=` query parameter is **dropped**. Error: `404 Resource not found`. **Attempt 3: `@ai-sdk/openai` with `api` URL including query param** ```json { "provider": { "azure": { "api": "https://<resource>.cognitiveservices.azure.com/openai?api-version=2025-04-01-preview", "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai", "options": { "apiKey": "<REDACTED>", "headers": { "api-key": "<REDACTED>" } }, "models": { "gpt-5.2-codex": { "name": "GPT 5.2 Codex" } } } } } ``` **Result:** SDK appends `/responses` **after** the query string, producing a malformed URL: `https://<resource>.cognitiveservices.azure.com/openai/responses?api-version=2025-04-01-preview/responses`. Error: `404`. **Attempt 4: `@ai-sdk/openai` with clean `api` URL (no query param)** ```json { "provider": { "openai": { "api": "https://<resource>.cognitiveservices.azure.com/openai", "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai", "options": { "apiKey": "<REDACTED>", "headers": { "api-key": "<REDACTED>" } }, "models": { "gpt-5.2-codex": { "name": "GPT 5.2 Codex" } } } } } ``` **Result:** URL hits `/openai/responses` (correct path) but `?api-version=` is missing. Error: `404 Resource not found`. **Attempt 5: Custom provider ID to bypass Azure custom loader** ```json { "provider": { "azure-responses": { "name": "Azure OpenAI", "npm": "@ai-sdk/azure", "options": { "apiKey": "<REDACTED>", "baseURL": "https://<resource>.cognitiveservices.azure.com/openai", "apiVersion": "2025-04-01-preview" }, "models": { "gpt-5.2-codex": { "name": "GPT 5.2 Codex" } } } } } ``` **Result:** Same as Attempt 2 — `?api-version=` is dropped when `baseURL` is provided. Error: `404 Resource not found`. --- **Root cause analysis:** The issue is an architectural mismatch across three layers: 1. **`@ai-sdk/azure` URL construction:** When using `resourceName`, the SDK hardcodes the hostname as `{resourceName}.openai.azure.com`. Cognitive Services endpoints use `{resourceName}.cognitiveservices.azure.com` instead. When `baseURL` is provided to bypass this, the SDK stops appending `?api-version=` to requests — this is a [known limitation](https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/2312). 2. **OpenCode's Azure custom loader** ([`provider.ts` L178-191](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/7ed449974864361bad2c1f1405769fd2c2fcdf42/packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts#L178-L191)): Correctly calls `sdk.responses(modelID)` by default, but has no mechanism to handle the Cognitive Services endpoint variant. 3. **OpenCode's `getSDK`** ([`provider.ts` L1041-1117](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/7ed449974864361bad2c1f1405769fd2c2fcdf42/packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts#L1041-L1117)): Passes config options through to `createAzure()`, but there's no way for users to configure both a custom base hostname AND retain the `?api-version=` query parameter behavior. **Note:** The bundled `@ai-sdk/azure` version (`2.0.91`) is not obsolete — it does support the Responses API. The issue is specifically about how it constructs URLs when `baseURL` is overridden. **Suggested fix:** - Allow OpenCode's Azure provider to accept a full custom base URL while preserving `?api-version=` injection (e.g. via a custom fetch wrapper, or by patching URL construction in the Azure loader). - Alternatively, add explicit support for the `cognitiveservices.azure.com` hostname pattern in the `azure-cognitive-services` custom loader. **References:** - [Azure OpenAI Responses API docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/openai/how-to/responses) - [Vercel AI SDK: Add baseURL and apiVersion to Azure provider (issue #2312)](https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/2312) - [Vercel AI SDK: Azure calling wrong URL path (issue #4797)](https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/4797) ### Plugins None ### OpenCode version Latest stable (2026-02-17) ### Steps to reproduce 1. Deploy a model requiring the Responses API (e.g. `gpt-5.2-codex`) on an Azure Cognitive Services resource 2. Configure `opencode.json` with provider `azure`, pointing at `https://<resource>.cognitiveservices.azure.com/openai` 3. Set `"model": "azure/gpt-5.2-codex"` and provide your API key 4. Launch opencode and send any message 5. Observe error: `404 Resource not found` — the request URL is `/openai/responses` without `?api-version=` 6. Verify the same request works via curl with `?api-version=2025-04-01-preview` appended ### Screenshot and/or share link **Error from OpenCode logs:** ``` AI_APICallError: Resource not found url: "https://<resource>.cognitiveservices.azure.com/openai/responses" statusCode: 404 responseBody: {"error":{"code":"404","message": "Resource not found"}} ``` **Expected URL (works via curl):** ``` https://<resource>.cognitiveservices.azure.com/openai/responses?api-version=2025-04-01-preview ``` ### Operating System Windows 11 ### Terminal Windows Terminal

signals.title: [QOL]:  Treat directories with .git or opencode.json as local projects (not global)
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request ## Description: OpenCode currently only promotes a directory from “global” to a distinct project when Git has at least one commit. This forces users to make an initial commit even when they only want project-scoped config or agents. We should treat a directory as a local project if either (a) a `.git` directory exists (even without commits) or (b) an `opencode.json` file is present at the root. ### Current behavior - `git init` alone (no commits) → `project.id === "global"` [1](#2-0) - Adding `opencode.json` does not affect project ID detection [2](#2-1) - Tests confirm: repo with only `git init` yields global; repo with commits yields non-global [3](#2-2) ### Expected behavior - Presence of `.git` directory OR `opencode.json` should cause OpenCode to assign a non-global project ID and enable project-scoped features (e.g., `.opencode/` directories, project config precedence). ### Why this matters - Users often create a project to set up agents or project-specific config before committing. - Requiring an initial commit is unnecessary friction for configuration-only workflows. - `opencode.json` already signals intent to be a project; it should influence project detection. ### Suggested implementation hints - In `Project.fromDirectory`, after the existing Git toplevel/common-dir checks, add a fallback: - If `existsSync(path.join(directory, ".git"))` OR `Filesystem.findUp("opencode.json", directory)` succeeds, generate a non-global project ID (e.g., hash of the absolute path) and set `vcs: "git"` if `.git` exists, else `vcs: undefined`. - Ensure `migrateFromGlobal` runs for these newly-recognized projects [4](#2-3) . - Update tests to cover both cases. ### Acceptance criteria - [ ] Directory with only `.git` (no commits) opens as a local project. - [ ] Directory with `opencode.json` (no Git) opens as a local project. - [ ] Existing behavior with committed Git repos is unchanged. - [ ] Sessions migrate from global to the new local project when applicable. ## Notes - The UI determines “global” status by checking `projectID === "global"` or when metadata lacks an ID but has local overrides [5](#2-4) . - Project configs already override global configs in the merge order, but they don’t affect the initial project ID assignment [6](#2-5) . Wiki pages you might want to explore: - [Architecture (anomalyco/opencode)](/wiki/anomalyco/opencode#2) - [Agent System (anomalyco/opencode)](/wiki/anomalyco/opencode#3.3) ### Citations **File:** packages/opencode/src/project/project.ts (L143-192) ```typescript const top = await git(["rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"], { cwd: sandbox, }) .then(async (result) => path.resolve(sandbox, (await result.text()).trim())) .catch(() => undefined) if (!top) { return { id, sandbox, worktree: sandbox, vcs: Info.shape.vcs.parse(Flag.OPENCODE_FAKE_VCS), } } sandbox = top const worktree = await git(["rev-parse", "--git-common-dir"], { cwd: sandbox, }) .then(async (result) => { const dirname = path.dirname((await result.text()).trim()) if (dirname === ".") return sandbox return dirname }) .catch(() => undefined) if (!worktree) { return { id, sandbox, worktree: sandbox, vcs: Info.shape.vcs.parse(Flag.OPENCODE_FAKE_VCS), } } return { id, sandbox, worktree, vcs: "git", } } return { id: "global", worktree: "/", sandbox: "/", vcs: Info.shape.vcs.parse(Flag.OPENCODE_FAKE_VCS), } ``` **File:** packages/opencode/src/project/project.ts (L294-314) ```typescript async function migrateFromGlobal(id: string, worktree: string) { const row = Database.use((db) => db.select().from(ProjectTable).where(eq(ProjectTable.id, "global")).get()) if (!row) return const sessions = Database.use((db) => db.select().from(SessionTable).where(eq(SessionTable.project_id, "global")).all(), ) if (sessions.length === 0) return log.info("migrating sessions from global", { newProjectID: id, worktree, count: sessions.length }) await work(10, sessions, async (row) => { // Skip sessions that belong to a different directory if (row.directory && row.directory !== worktree) return log.info("migrating session", { sessionID: row.id, from: "global", to: id }) Database.use((db) => db.update(SessionTable).set({ project_id: id }).where(eq(SessionTable.id, row.id)).run()) }).catch((error) => { log.error("failed to migrate sessions from global to project", { error, projectId: id }) }) } ``` **File:** packages/web/src/content/docs/config.mdx (L41-52) ```text ### Precedence order Config sources are loaded in this order (later sources override earlier ones): 1. **Remote config** (from `.well-known/opencode`) - organizational defaults 2. **Global config** (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`) - user preferences 3. **Custom config** (`OPENCODE_CONFIG` env var) - custom overrides 4. **Project config** (`opencode.json` in project) - project-specific settings 5. **`.opencode` directories** - agents, commands, plugins 6. **Inline config** (`OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` env var) - runtime overrides This means project configs can override global defaults, and global configs can override remote organizational defaults. ``` **File:** packages/web/src/content/docs/config.mdx (L104-114) ```text ### Per project Add `opencode.json` in your project root. Project config has the highest precedence among standard config files - it overrides both global and remote configs. :::tip Place project specific config in the root of your project. ::: When OpenCode starts up, it looks for a config file in the current directory or traverse up to the nearest Git directory. This is also safe to be checked into Git and uses the same schema as the global one. ``` **File:** packages/app/src/context/layout.tsx (L343-356) ```typescript const isGlobal = projectID === "global" || (metadata?.id === undefined && localOverride) if (!isGlobal) return base return { ...base, id: base.id ?? "global", name: local?.name, commands: local?.commands, icon: { url: base.icon?.url, override: local?.icon?.override, color: local?.icon?.color, }, } ```

signals.title: ANSI escape codes displayed as literal text on Windows with wezterm + PowerShell 7
signals.text: ### Description Environment - OS: Windows 10 - Terminal: wezterm - Shell: PowerShell 7.4.7 - Bun version: 1.3.10 - Node.js: Works correctly Problem When running opencode-cli on Windows with wezterm terminal, ANSI escape codes are displayed as literal text instead of being rendered as colors/styles. Example of corrupted output: m┃H Build [ 38; ssion - 2026-03-09T02:30:38.791Z █ 2 0m 8 ;238m续 3 8;2 55m [ 12;4H ; 30m█ 3 0;30;30m█ 4 8;2;3 m█ The escape sequences like [38;2;255;255;255m, [30m, [48;2;30;30;30m should render colors, but are shown as plain text. Reproduction Steps # 1. Install Bun on Windows # 2. Use wezterm as terminal # 3. Run any Bun-based CLI with colored output bun -e "console.log('\x1b[31mRed\x1b[0m')" # Expected: "Red" in red color # Actual: "[31mRed[0m" as literal text What I've Tried 1. ✅ Node.js works correctly: node -e "console.log('\x1b[31mRed\x1b[0m')" # Output: Red (in red color) 2. ❌ Setting FORCE_COLOR: $env:FORCE_COLOR = "1" # No effect 3. ❌ Setting TERM variables: $env:TERM = "xterm-256color" $env:COLORTERM = "truecolor" # No effect 4. ❌ UTF-8 encoding: chcp 65001 # No effect 5. ❌ Modified wezterm.lua: config.set_environment_variables = { TERM = 'xterm-256color', COLORTERM = 'truecolor', } No improvement. 6. ✅ PowerShell native colors work: Write-Host "Red" -ForegroundColor Red # Works correctly 7. ❌ Both opencode versions affected: - npx opencode - same issue - npx oh-my-opencode - same issue Environment Variables Check $env:TERM # xterm-256color ✓ $env:COLORTERM # truecolor ✓ $env:TERM_PROGRAM # WezTerm ✓ chcp # 65001 (UTF-8) ✓ All settings appear correct. Root Cause Analysis - Node.js correctly detects the terminal as TTY and renders ANSI codes - Bun appears to not properly handle ANSI escape sequences on Windows + wezterm - The issue is specific to Bun on Windows with wezterm (not reproducible with Node.js) Expected Behavior ANSI escape codes should render as colors/styles, matching Node.js behavior. Actual Behavior ANSI escape codes are printed as literal text, making the UI unreadable. Suggested Fix Bun should properly detect Windows terminals (wezterm, Windows Terminal, etc.) and pass ANSI escape codes through correctly, similar to how Node.js handles them. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signals.title: Windows ARM64 native: OpenTUI fails to initialize with bun:ffi dlopen TinyCC error
signals.text:
### Description On Windows 11 ARM64, the native ARM64 OpenCode binary works for non-interactive commands, but the TUI fails to initialize. The native binary successfully runs commands like: - `opencode.exe --version` - `opencode.exe --help` - `opencode.exe debug --help` - `opencode.exe debug paths` However, starting the interactive TUI does not start correctly and logs this error: ```text Failed to initialize OpenTUI render library: bun:ffi dlopen() is not available in this build (TinyCC is disabled) ``` ### Environment - OS: Windows 11 ARM64 - Architecture: native ARM64 - Installation method: npm global install - Native binary path: `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming
pm
ode_modules\opencode-ai
ode_modules\opencode-windows-arm64 in\opencode.exe` ### OpenCode version Observed from direct ARM64 binary: - `1.3.0` Also noting that `opencode` from PATH reported `1.3.2` in my environment, so there may be version/path inconsistency locally. If needed, I can provide more details, but the native ARM64 binary issue below was reproduced directly from the ARM64 executable path. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Install OpenCode on Windows ARM64 via npm 2. Run the native ARM64 binary directly: ```powershell C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming
pm
ode_modules\opencode-ai
ode_modules\opencode-windows-arm64 in\opencode.exe ``` 3. Alternatively run: ```powershell C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming
pm
ode_modules\opencode-ai
ode_modules\opencode-windows-arm64 in\opencode.exe --print-logs --log-level DEBUG ``` 4. Observe startup behavior ### Expected behavior The OpenCode TUI should initialize and start normally on the native Windows ARM64 build. ### Actual behavior The process does not start the TUI correctly and logs: ```text ERROR ... Failed to initialize OpenTUI render library: bun:ffi dlopen() is not available in this build (TinyCC is disabled) ERROR ... Error: Failed to initialize OpenTUI render library: bun:ffi dlopen() is not available in this build (TinyCC is disabled) ``` In my testing, the process stayed alive until manually terminated / timed out, rather than exiting cleanly. ### Additional notes - This seems different from the existing Windows OpenTUI DLL/path issues that fail with `LoadLibrary` / DLL error codes. - This also seems different from the existing Windows ARM64 x64-emulation crash report, since this was reproduced against the native ARM64 binary directly. - Non-interactive commands work, so the problem appears specific to OpenTUI initialization on Windows ARM64 native. - Related but possibly separate: I have also seen instability when using the x64 build under emulation on Windows ARM64, but this report is specifically about the native ARM64 binary failing to initialize OpenTUI. If useful, I can provide the exact command output and more environment details.
signals.author: Carliquiss

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Recursive skill discovery + multi-skill selection in TUI
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request ## Feature Request: Recursive skill discovery and multi-skill selection ### Problem - The `skills` command only discovers skills at the root level (no recursive lookup). - Only a single skill can be selected per request. --- ### Use Case Projects with structured skill directories: project-a/skills/backend/auth.md project-a/skills/backend/database.md project-b/skills/frontend/ui.md - Nested skills are not detected - It is not possible to combine skills (e.g. `auth` + `database`) --- ### Proposal 1. **Recursive discovery** - Load skills using recursive directory scanning (`/skills/**/*.md`) 2. **Multi-skill selection** - Allow selecting multiple skills in a single request: /use auth,database --- ### Expected Behavior - `skills` lists all skills recursively - Multiple skills can be selected and applied in one request --- ### Considerations - Context/token limits when combining skills - Conflict resolution between skills --- ### Question Would you accept: 1. Recursive skill loading as a first step 2. Multi-skill support as a follow-up (separate PRs)
signals.author: Flussen

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Azure AI Foundry Microsoft Entra (OAuth) authentication
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request It appears Microsoft Entra authentication with the Azure AI Foundry is not supported yet (or I can't find anything about it 😉). A customer of ours deployed Anthropic models in an Azure AI Foundry with a custom base URL and provided instructions only for Anthropic CLI. The existing provider relies on an API key, but the customer expressly does not want to provide one to strengthen security and enforces Entra authentication using the Azure CLI instead. These are the steps they document (not using OpenCode): 1. `export ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL=https://their-custom-domain.azure-api.net/ai/anthropic` 2. `export CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY="1"` 3. `az login` to sign in to Azure using Entra Authentication (OAuth). 4. `claude run` Steps 1, 2 and 4 appear already possible with OpenCode (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/4474#issuecomment-3560959500), but for 3 an API key is expected by OpenCode instead. They also mention the Azure CLI session can expire every so often (10 hours in their case), in which case `az logout` followed by `az login` is required - mentioning it as reauthenticating might be relevant for OpenCode also.

signals.title: macOS notifications show as 'Script Editor' instead of terminal app — no click-to-focus
signals.text: ## Problem On macOS, desktop notifications from OpenCode appear to come from **"Script Editor"** (AppleScript) instead of the terminal emulator (iTerm2, Terminal.app, etc.). Clicking the notification opens Script Editor instead of focusing the correct terminal tab. This happens because OpenCode uses `osascript -e 'display notification...'` as a fallback, and macOS attributes the notification to the osascript process (Script Editor) rather than the terminal. ## Expected Behavior - Notifications should be attributed to the terminal emulator (iTerm2, Terminal.app, etc.) - Clicking a notification should focus the correct terminal tab/window - On iTerm2 specifically, notifications should use OSC 9 escape sequences for native integration ## Current State I found **PR #23212** (`feat(tui): add terminal notifications` by @kitlangton) which addresses this by adding: - OSC 9 escape sequences (`\x1b]9;message\x07`) for iTerm2, Ghostty, Apple Terminal, Warp - OSC 777 for Kitty, WezTerm, VTE-based terminals - Bell (`\x07`) as fallback - Auto-detection based on `TERM_PROGRAM` However, this PR is: - **Draft** status - Has **merge conflicts** - Open since April 18 ## Suggested Fix The notification resolution logic from PR #23212 looks correct: ```typescript // For iTerm2 if (env.TERM_PROGRAM === "iTerm.app") return "osc9" // \x1b]9;title:body\x07 // For Kitty/WezTerm if (env.KITTY_WINDOW_ID || env.TERM === "xterm-kitty") return "osc777" // \x1b]777;notify;title;body\x07 // Fallback return "bell" // \x07 ``` Additionally, for terminals that don't support OSC sequences, consider using `terminal-notifier` with `-activate <bundle-id>`: - iTerm2: `com.googlecode.iterm2` - Terminal.app: `com.apple.Terminal` - Warp: `dev.warp.Warp-Stable` ⚠️ **Do NOT use `-sender` flag** — it conflicts with `-activate` on macOS Sequoia 15.x+ and breaks click-to-focus. ## Environment - macOS (Sequoia/Tahoe) - iTerm2 - OpenCode v1.14.18 - Installed via Homebrew ## Related - Draft PR: #23212
signals.author: dexion

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Add unarchive/restore for archived sessions
signals.text: - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request **Problem:** Archiving a session is currently a one-way operation. Once archived, sessions disappear from the sidebar and the only place they're visible is dimmed in the command palette file picker. There's no way to restore them without directly hitting the API. signals.title: TUI hangs in tmux after opentui 0.1.103 upgrade (theme detection)
signals.text: ## Description After the opentui upgrade from 0.1.99 to 0.1.103 in commit 3a5507de9, the TUI becomes unresponsive when running inside tmux. Every keystroke lags significantly, making the app unusable. ## Root Cause `0.1.103` introduced `renderer.waitForThemeMode(timeout)` which sends OSC escape sequences to detect the terminal's background color. tmux doesn't forward these properly, so the call blocks for the full timeout duration on each render cycle — not just once at startup. The call site is in `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/app.tsx:133`: ```ts const mode = (await renderer.waitForThemeMode(1000)) ?? "dark" ``` ## Reproduction 1. Open a tmux session 2. Run `opencode` (built from dev branch with opentui >= 0.1.103) 3. Try typing — keystrokes are delayed by ~1 second each 4. Exit tmux, run `opencode` directly — works fine ## Workaround Pin opentui back to 0.1.99 in `package.json` and replace the `waitForThemeMode` call with a hardcoded `"dark"`. ## Environment - Linux (WSL2) - tmux 3.5a - Terminal: Windows Terminal / wezterm - TERM: xterm-256color

signals.title: Web prompts can stop after the first reply when client and server clocks differ
signals.text: ### Description I ran into a behavior when using `opencode serve` with the Web UI: the first message received a normal assistant response, but subsequent messages were persisted as user messages without triggering another assistant response. The same model and configuration worked normally in the terminal/TUI. After some debugging, this seems related to Web client-generated `messageID`s and clock skew between the browser/client device and the server. ### What I observed 1. Start opencode with `opencode serve`. 2. Open the Web UI from a browser. 3. Send the first message. 4. The assistant responds normally. 5. Send additional messages. 6. The later user messages are persisted in the database. 7. No new assistant message is created. 8. The server log shows: ```text session.prompt ... exiting loop ``` ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start `opencode serve`. 2. Open the Web UI from a browser/device whose clock differs from the server clock. 3. Send a first message. 4. Wait for the assistant response. 5. Send another message. 6. Observe that the later user message is persisted, but no new assistant response is generated. ### Debugging notes In the database, the later user messages had later `time_created` values, but their `messageID`s sorted before the first assistant message. In my environment, the server clock was about 170 seconds ahead of the client/browser device that was accessing the Web UI. After decoding the timestamp portion of the message IDs, the sequence looked roughly like this: ```text user1 09:38:26 assistant1 09:41:16 user2 09:38:37 user3 09:38:38 user4 09:38:39 ``` So `user2`, `user3`, and `user4` were sent after `assistant1`, but their IDs still sorted before `assistant1`. I noticed this condition in `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts`: ```ts if ( lastAssistant?.finish && !["tool-calls"].includes(lastAssistant.finish) && !hasToolCalls && lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id ) { yield* slog.info("exiting loop") break } ``` My understanding is that, in the Web UI case, the user message ID can be generated using the browser/client device clock, while the assistant message ID is generated using the server clock. If those clocks differ enough, the ID ordering may not match the actual conversation order, and the prompt loop may conclude that the latest user message has already been answered. ### Additional check I also tested sending a prompt directly to the server API without providing a client-generated `messageID`, allowing the server to generate the user message ID. In that case, the subsequent assistant response was triggered correctly. ### Impact This may be more likely to happen when using the Web UI from another device, for example: - accessing `opencode serve` from a phone or another computer - the browser/client device clock differs from the server clock - the server clock itself is not synchronized The user-facing behavior is a little confusing because the message appears to be sent successfully, but no assistant response appears. ### Question Would it make sense to avoid relying on ordering between client-generated user message IDs and server-generated assistant message IDs in this path? For example, perhaps Web prompts could have their final user message IDs generated or normalized on the server, or this loop condition could use a server-trusted ordering mechanism instead. ### Plugins None ### OpenCode version 1.14.25 ### Operating System Ubuntu 24.04 ### Terminal zsh

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Progress indicator for MCP calls
signals.text:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [X] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ← Note: suggested but abandoned, see section *Prior art* ### Describe the enhancement you want to request ## Motivation While an MCP call is running, OpenCode’s TUI currently doesn’t show progress info, even if the MCP server sends progress updates. Especially with longer-running services (which are common in MCP, e.g. on-demand embedding runs), this is awkward from the user’s point of view because the conversation can seem stuck for minutes. That effect is about to get even more noticeable when [#24964]() is merged, which (correctly) fixes an issue with `resetTimeoutOnProgress`, causing the “user is waiting for anything to happen” time to become potentially unbounded. ## Suggestion If an MCP server sends progress messages, then the text in the TUI should reflect that progress message. Depending of whether the MCP progress message includes the optional `total` and `message` fields, I suggest that instead of the current message: ```plain ⚙ mcp_service_name [query=very long running call] ``` I suggest that the TUI render one of the following: ```plain ⚙ mcp_service_name [query=very long running call] · In progress [42] ``` or, if the server includes a `total`: ```plain ⚙ mcp_service_name [query=very long running call] · In progress [42/800] ``` or, if the server includes both a `total` and a custom `message`: ```plain ⚙ mcp_service_name [query=very long running call] · Calculating embeddings [42/800] ``` ## Prior art Here’s what has been done so far: * @fahreddinozcan’s PR [#24964]() ← this is the foundation that actually triggers the MCP server to send progress messages (and fixes the timeout issue). Needs to be merged first. * @wangguodong-f’s report anomalyco/opencode#22153 ← related but different focus (subagents). Pinging them anyway for ideas and to keep them in the loop. Related but abandoned: * @rfhold’s report [#11821]() ← very related, also abandoned. A bit more focused (it mentions only the SDK plumbing, not the TUI changes.) However, doing both plumbing and TUI at once might give the user more immediate value (and the developer a closer feedback loop). * @xhuw’s report [#2101]() ← very similar to this report, abandoned * @CagierAsh123’s report [#5472]() ← related but broader (not just focused on MCP), abandoned * @ravshansbox’s report [#3742]() ← related but broader, abandoned * @Becktor’s report anomalyco/opencode#9655 ← related, different proposal (sidebar), broader, abandoned ## Technical design (draft/proposal) *Note: I started out entirely unfamiliar with the code base, and there’s no way I could have possibly come up with a design draft by myself. The following is the gist of a few days of back-and-forth with Opus 4.7 and includes insights from a PoC implementation.*
Design draft MCP client Accepts a new optional `onProgress` callback and passes that to the MCP SDK’s `callTool` options. If none is supplied, passes an empty callback (that same empty callback as in PR [#24964](), which tickles the MCP SDK to include a progress token in the request so the server can send progress messages and the timeout is properly reset.) Session runner (prompt.ts) Gets to own a small adapter (in form of an `onProgress` callback) that it injects into the MCP client. The adapter consumes progress reports and converts them into a v1 bus event and a v2 sync event (dual-write, just like the rest of the codebase does). Bus Needs a new v1 event type `.tool.progress.report`. v2 sync-event registry Gets a new v2 event type `.next.tool.progress.report`. A similar event type named `.next.tool.progress` already exists but handles unrelated stuff, i.e. partial tool output, which arrives entirely separate from progress reports. We can’t rename the existing `….progress` type lest we’d break existing consumers. Hence, `….progress.report`. Session projector Receives the progress report as a v2 sync event, updates the database, and updates the `ToolStateRunning` model in the v2 `SessionMessage`. TUI v1 client Receives the progress report from the bus and updates its `store.part[messageID][idx].state.progress`. TUI v2 client Receives the progress report from the bus and updates the `ToolStateRunning` model. TUI v1/v2 renderer Presents the progress info in its `InlineTool` and `BlockTool` components when a tool is `running`.
## Commitment If the core team decides that this is worth doing, I’ll be happy to implement this end to end.

signals.title: fix(session): inherit parent directory + workspaceID in subagent sessions
signals.text: ### Description When opencode is run in HTTP server mode, the directory is always set to ctx.directory, which is the daemon's process.cwd(), NOT the parent session's context. For subagent sessions (parentID set), this is wrong: they should inherit the parent's directory to maintain workspace coherence. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce **Evidence (Session IDs from live observation, port 4096):** - Parent session: `ses_17cdba9cfffeC5A6FQLkMAFYtM` - Created in headless client project root - Correct: `directory=/path/to/headless/client/project/directory` - `workspaceID=wsv2_6uN7E5rF1I0rJy2qL` - Child Planner session: `ses_17cb08557ffe8G2ucNG1fi1F0c` - Created by Brain task tool for subagent execution - Incorrect: `directory=/path/to/opencode/daemon/home` (daemon's $HOME) - Should have been: `directory=/path/to/headless/client/project/directory` (inherited from parent) **Call trace:** - `headless client` makes HTTP POST to daemon's task endpoint with parent session context - Daemon's `task.ts` creates child session via `Session.create({ parentID })` - `session.ts` `Session.create()` previously did NOT inherit parent's directory - Result: child receives `ctx.directory` = daemon `process.cwd()` = `/path/to/opencode/daemon/home` ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Linux Debian/testing ### Terminal xterm ## Resolution See #32807 (supersedes #30650). The new PR is a fresh PR from the feature branch with improved scope: it adds structural projectID inheritance (so project_id can't drift from directory) on top of the original directory/workspaceID inheritance, includes a dedicated regression test, and excludes the unrelated bin/opencode ESM-shim change. Result is a conflict-free branch upstream can merge directly. Note: cross-project fork directory divergence is a separate deferred concern.

signals.title: MCP schema warnings: non-standard "format" values (uint32/uint64) from schemars pollute TUI
signals.text: ## Problem MCP servers that derive their JSON Schemas from Rust types via `schemars` emit non-standard `format` values like `uint32`, `uint64`, `uint8`, and `uint`. When opencode registers these tools, AJV (the JSON Schema validator) outputs warnings for each unknown format: ``` unknown format "uint64" ignored in schema for path "/properties/pid" unknown format "uint32" ignored in schema for path "/properties/width" ... ``` These warnings cannot be suppressed — `--log-level ERROR` does not help because they come from AJV's `console.warn()` bypassing opencode's logger. ## Affected MCP servers - `computer-use-linux` (schemars-derived schemas for Rust u32/u64/u8 types) - BigQuery MCP (previously reported in #8581) - Any other MCP server built with Rust + schemars ## Previous attempt PR #12815 ("fix(mcp): strip non-standard JSON Schema formats to suppress AJV warnings") was closed without merging. ## Request Either: 1. Strip non-standard format values before AJV validation (resurrect #12815 approach) 2. Provide a mechanism to suppress/silence schema validation warnings from MCP tool registration 3. Both ## Why upstream fixes aren't enough While individual MCP servers can (and should) configure schemars to use `SchemaSettings::draft07()` to avoid emitting these formats, this is a systemic issue that will keep appearing for any Rust MCP server using default schemars config.

signals.title: [BUG] TUI session view doesn't reflect external updates to an active session
signals.text: ### Description ### Describe the bug When a session is being driven by an **external** process — another opencode client, a remote agent or `opencode serve` running the session elsewhere — the TUI session view goes stale. New messages and parts produced outside this TUI's own event stream never appear until you manually switch away and back. The root cause is in the `useSync` hook: `sync.session.sync(sessionID)` short-circuits once a session has been fully hydrated: ```ts async sync(sessionID: string) { if (fullSyncedSessions.has(sessionID)) return // <- never re-fetches ... } ``` So after the first hydration the TUI relies entirely on live SSE events. Any update that doesn't arrive over that stream (external writer, dropped/missed event, a session being advanced by a different process) leaves the view permanently out of date. ### Expected behavior While a session is active, the TUI should periodically reconcile with the server so externally-produced updates appear, instead of trusting the initial hydration plus the local event stream alone. ### Proposed fix - Add a `{ force?: boolean }` option to `useSync().session.sync()` that bypasses the `fullSyncedSessions` cache and re-fetches. - In the session route, poll every 2s with `{ force: true }` only while the session status is working or compacting, and stop polling (clearInterval via `onCleanup`) once it goes idle. - Covered by a new test asserting that a normal `sync()` is a no-op on an already- hydrated session while `sync(id, { force: true })` re-fetches and picks up new messages. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version 1.15.13 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start a session and let it hydrate in the TUI. 2. 2. Drive that same session from an external source (e.g. opencode-remote, a second client, or the server directly) so new assistant messages are appended. 3. Observe the TUI session view — it does not show the new messages/parts. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System macOS 26.3 ### Terminal iTerm2

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Add markup disclosure column to Go pricing table — V4 Flash parity vs V4 Pro 4x markup is invisible to users
signals.text: - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. **Describe the enhancement you want to request** The Go pricing table at https://opencode.ai/docs/go/ displays per-token costs uniformly, but the markup model is inconsistent: - **V4 Flash**: $0.14/$0.28 — at parity with official DeepSeek ($0.14/$0.28) - **V4 Pro**: $1.74/$3.48 — 4x markup vs official DeepSeek ($0.435/$0.87) Both sit in the same table with identical formatting. V4 Flash at exact parity creates a false baseline — users have no reason to suspect V4 Pro carries a 300% service fee. The only way to discover this is to cross-reference DeepSeek's official pricing. The problem is reinforced by the request estimates: the "1,350 req/5h" for V4 Pro is calculated against the 4x inflated per-token price. At actual DeepSeek rates ($0.435/$0.87), that same $12/5h limit would yield ~5,400 requests. The estimates silently penalize V4 Pro users. **Request**: Add a disclosure column to the pricing table showing markup vs official provider pricing, e.g.: | Model | Input | Output | Cached Read | vs Official | |---|---|---|---|---| | V4 Flash | $0.14 | $0.28 | $0.0028 | Parity | | V4 Pro | $1.74 | $3.48 | $0.0145 | 4x markup | This isn't asking for a price cut — it's asking for transparency so users can make informed decisions about which models to use through Go vs bringing their own key.

signals.title: `opencode run --format json --session` hangs after final answer is persisted
signals.text: ### Description ### Summary `opencode run --format json --session <session_id>` can hang even after the model has completed and the final assistant answer has been persisted to OpenCode’s session DB. In our repro, the process stayed alive, stdout remained empty, but the SQLite session DB contained both the completed tool result and final answer. ### What We Tried We tested PR #31505, which flushes missed parts after the stream loop finishes: ```ts await finish() if (!args.attach) await flushParts(result.data?.parts) ``` That did not fix our case because `finish()` itself can hang waiting for the event stream to observe `session.status: idle`. Since `flushParts()` runs after `finish()`, the fallback is never reached. ### Custom Patch We changed JSON mode to flush returned prompt/command parts before waiting for stream completion: ```ts async function finishBestEffort() { if (args.format !== "json") { await finish() return } await Promise.race([ finish(), new Promise<void>((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1000)), ]) } ``` Then changed both `session.command` and `session.prompt` paths from: ```ts await finish() if (!args.attach) await flushParts(result.data?.parts) ``` to: ```ts if (!args.attach) await flushParts(result.data?.parts) await finishBestEffort() ``` ### Why This Works Once `client.session.prompt()` or `client.session.command()` returns, `result.data.parts` contains the completed assistant parts. For `--format json`, emitting those parts immediately avoids depending on the event stream’s idle signal. The stream is still given a short best-effort drain window, but output delivery no longer blocks forever on it. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version 0.17.7 ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signals.text: ## Summary Azure GPT-5.x deployments routed through the built-in **`cloudflare-ai-gateway`** provider fail in OpenCode because requests use `max_tokens` instead of `max_completion_tokens`. This is distinct from #25096 (custom `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` providers) and #22623 (native Azure provider). Here the failure is in the **built-in** `cloudflare-ai-gateway` path backed by `@earendil-works/pi-ai`. ## Environment - OpenCode: **1.17.8** - Provider: `cloudflare-ai-gateway` (connected via `/connect`, Azure keys in gateway BYOK) - Gateway compat endpoint: `https://gateway.ai.cloudflare.com/v1/{account}/{gateway}/compat` - Model IDs: `azure-openai/gpt-5.4-nano`, `azure-openai/gpt-5.4`, `azure-openai/gpt-5.4-mini`, `azure-openai/gpt-5.5` - Other Azure deployments on the same provider (e.g. `grok-4-20-non-reasoning`, `kimi-k2.6`) work fine ## Reproduce `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`: ```jsonc { "provider": { "cloudflare-ai-gateway": { "models": { "azure-openai/gpt-5.4-nano": { "name": "GPT 5.4 Nano (Azure)" } } } } } ``` ```bash opencode run -m cloudflare-ai-gateway/azure-openai/gpt-5.4-nano "Reply with exactly: OK" ``` **Error:** ``` Unsupported parameter: 'max_tokens' is not supported with this model. Use 'max_completion_tokens' instead. ``` ## Root cause (pi-ai) In `@earendil-works/pi-ai` `openai-completions.js`, `detectCompat()` treats all `cloudflare-ai-gateway` URLs as non-standard and sets: ```js maxTokensField: useMaxTokens ? "max_tokens" : "max_completion_tokens" // where useMaxTokens includes isCloudflareAiGateway ``` So every gateway request sends `max_tokens`, which newer Azure GPT-5 deployments reject. `getCompat()` can override via `model.compat.maxTokensField`, but that override is not reachable from normal OpenCode config for custom models added in `opencode.jsonc`. ## Workarounds attempted (none worked) 1. Per-model `options.compat.maxTokensField` in `opencode.jsonc` 2. `modelOverrides` / full model entries in `~/.config/opencode/models.json` 3. Full model entries in `~/.pi/agent/models.json` (pi docs path) 4. Separate custom provider using `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` pointed at the same compat `baseURL` (still sends `max_tokens` — same class of bug as #25096) ## Expected behavior At least one of these should work: - `options.compat.maxTokensField: "max_completion_tokens"` per model in `opencode.jsonc` - `modelOverrides` / `models.json` compat for config-defined `cloudflare-ai-gateway` models - Smarter defaults: `azure-openai/gpt-5*` routes use `max_completion_tokens` while other gateway models keep `max_tokens` ## Suggested fix 1. **OpenCode:** Map `provider.models.*.options.compat` (or top-level model `compat`) into pi `model.compat` when registering config models. 2. **pi-ai:** Do not blanket-force `max_tokens` for all `cloudflare-ai-gateway` traffic; either per-model override or prefix-based detection for `azure-openai/gpt-5*`. ## Notes - Gateway + Azure deployment itself is healthy; this is a client parameter naming issue. - Switching to the native Azure provider **without** pointing `baseURL` at the gateway would bypass Cloudflare AI Gateway observability/BYOK routing. Related: #22623, #25096

signals.title: fix(session): unhandled PlatformError when binary file attachment does not exist
signals.text: ## Bug Description Attaching a binary file (image, PDF, HTML, etc.) that does not exist crashes the TUI with an unhandled \PlatformError\. Text file and directory attachments handle this gracefully — only the binary file path is missing error handling. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Start opencode in any project 2. Attach a non-existent binary file (e.g. \@missing_file.html\ or drag in a file that has been deleted) 3. Send the message ## Error \\\ PlatformError: NotFound: FileNotFoundError: W:\\path\\to\\missing_file.html at SessionPrompt.resolveUserPart ... at SessionPrompt.createUserMessage at SessionPrompt.prompt at SessionHttpApi.prompt \\\ The TUI becomes broken/unresponsive after this error. ## Root Cause In \packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts\, the \ esolveUserPart\ function handles file attachments differently depending on mime type: - **Text files** (lines 931-972): Uses \Effect.exit\ + \Exit.isFailure\ — catches errors gracefully, publishes to bus, returns error text part - **Directories** (lines 976-999): Same graceful pattern - **Binary files** (lines 1022-1043): Uses \Effect.catch(Effect.die)\ which converts any error (including \PlatformError.NotFound\) into an unrecoverable defect that crashes the session The problematic line is: \\\ s Buffer.from(yield* fsys.readFile(filepath).pipe(Effect.catch(Effect.die))) \\\ ## Expected Behavior Binary file read failures should be caught and surfaced to the user as an error message (same as text files), not crash the TUI. ## Suggested Fix Replace \Effect.catch(Effect.die)\ at line 1038 with \Effect.exit\ and add \Exit.isFailure\ handling that mirrors the text file pattern (lines 957-972): log the error, publish to bus, and return a synthetic text part with the error message.

signals.title: Desktop app redirects to wrong directory when multiple clones of same repo exist
signals.text: ### Description opencode Desktop identifies projects by Git repository identity (VCS), not by filesystem path. When multiple clones of the same Git repository exist at different paths (e.g., ~/Desktop/WorkSpaceA/ProjectA and ~/Desktop/WorkSpaceB/ProjectB both cloned from the same upstream), they are assigned the same project ID (e7dc3c41... in SQLite project table). Opening the non-main clone always redirects to the main worktree directory. Expected: Each local directory should be treated as an independent workspace. Workaround: Temporarily change one repo's origin remote to a different URL, open it in opencode (creates separate project), then revert the remote. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version 1.17.8 ### Steps to reproduce 1. signals.title: [Bug] Kimi K2.6 reasoning content leaks into main response instead of being rendered as thinking block
signals.text: **Description:** When using **Kimi K2.6** through the **direct Moonshot AI** provider, the model's reasoning content is not separated into a thinking/rationale block. Instead, it is streamed as part of the main assistant response, making it look like the model is "talking to itself" in the answer. This does **not** happen with **Kimi K2.7** under the same setup — reasoning is correctly handled there. **Environment:** - OpenCode version: `1.17.7` - Provider: Moonshot AI (direct, via `/connect`) - Model: `Kimi K2.6` - OS: Windows 11 + WSL - Terminal: WezTerm **Steps to reproduce:** 1. Run `opencode`. 2. Connect Moonshot AI provider via `/connect`. 3. Select `Kimi K2.6` model via `/models`. 4. Send any prompt. 5. Observe that reasoning text appears inline in the assistant response rather than in a separate thinking block. **Expected behavior:** Reasoning should be rendered as a collapsible `Thought:` block (when `/thinking` is enabled) or hidden from the response entirely (when `/thinking` is disabled). **Actual behavior:** Reasoning text is mixed into the normal response text, as if it were part of the answer. The `/thinking` command has no effect on this behavior — the reasoning content is never recognized as a separate block. **Additional context:** - `/thinking` command state does not affect this behavior. - The issue appears specific to Kimi K2.6; Kimi K2.7 works correctly. - Possibly related to open issues around `reasoning_content` handling for Kimi K2.6: #29690, #29619, #27852, #32545.

signals.title: OpenCode overwrites data in a different directory without any notification
signals.text: ### Description I work in a single repository but with multiple branches simultaneously. The branches are checked out into different directories (pkb, pkb_develop, pkb_gateway, pkb_checker, etc.). When opening the pkb_develop directory, OpenCode opened the pkb directory and started making changes there, without any notifications, warnings, or informational windows, and with no way to know that writing was happening to a different directory. I only found out after noticing the data discrepancy. The same thing happens with the other directories — OpenCode silently redirects everything to the first one. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version 1.17.7 ### Steps to reproduce **Steps to Reproduce** 1. **Prepare the environment:** - Clone a single Git repository into several different directories, for example: - `pkb` (main branch) - `pkb_develop` (develop branch) - `pkb_gateway` (gateway branch) - `pkb_checker` (checker branch) - In each directory, switch to its respective branch so that the file states differ across directories. 2. **Open and use the `pkb` directory first:** - Launch OpenCode and open the `pkb` directory as the working directory. - Make some changes to files there (this establishes it as the initially opened directory). 3. **Close and try to open a different directory:** - Close the `pkb` directory (or close OpenCode entirely and relaunch it). - Attempt to open any other directory, for example `pkb_develop`. 4. **Observe which directory is actually opened and where changes land:** - Check which directory OpenCode actually opens – it will be `pkb`, not `pkb_develop`. - Without receiving any notification, make file-modifying operations (edit code, create new files, modify existing ones). 5. **Verify where changes were written:** - After making changes, check which directory actually received those changes. **Actual Result:** - Once the `pkb` directory has been opened first, closing it and then trying to open any other directory (e.g. `pkb_develop`) causes OpenCode to silently open the `pkb` directory again instead of the selected one. - All subsequent file modifications are applied inside `pkb`, not in the directory the user intended to work in. - No notifications, warnings, or indicators appear to inform the user that writing is happening in a different directory. The behavior repeats for all other directories: OpenCode always silently redirects to `pkb`. **Expected Result:** - OpenCode should open the directory explicitly selected by the user, regardless of previous sessions. - File changes should be written to the currently opened and actively worked‑in directory. - Any fallback or redirect to a different directory must be clearly communicated to the user, with a warning and the option to abort. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Windows 10 ### Terminal _No response_

signals.title: MCP session recovery does not trigger on HTTP 400 (only 404) — breaks servers that return 400 for expired sessions
signals.text: PR #32088 (closes #25137) added MCP Streamable HTTP session recovery, but it only reinitializes when a POST receives **HTTP 404**. Some MCP servers return **HTTP 400** for an expired/missing session, so recovery never fires and every tool call fails until opencode is restarted. Reopening as a separate issue because #25137 is closed and may not be re-triaged. ## Description When the remote MCP server invalidates a Streamable HTTP session via idle timeout, the Atlassian/Jira MCP server (uvicorn, Atlassian MCP 1.12.4) responds to the stale `mcp-session-id` with **HTTP 400**, not 404. The recovery logic from #32088 only handles 404, so the session is never reinitialized and all subsequent tool calls fail with `Bad Request: No valid session ID provided` until a full restart. Reproducible every ~15-30 min of inactivity. The PR description for #32088 explicitly scopes the fix to the 404 POST failure, so this is a known gap rather than a regression. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Configure a remote Streamable HTTP MCP server that returns 400 for an unknown/expired session id (e.g. Atlassian MCP 1.12.4). 2. Use it normally; a few tool calls succeed. 3. Wait for the server-side idle timeout (~15-30 min). 4. Call any tool again → fails permanently with `Bad Request: No valid session ID provided`. Only a restart fixes it. Reproduced directly against the live server with a stale session id: ``` $ curl -si <server>/mcp/ -X POST \ -H "Authorization: Token ***" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \ -H "mcp-session-id: 00000000000000000000000000000000" \ -d "{\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"id\":1,\"method\":\"tools/list\",\"params\":{}}" HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request server: uvicorn content-length: 41 Bad Request: No valid session ID provided ``` Handshake without a session also returns a structured JSON-RPC error (code -32600): ```json {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"server-error","error":{"code":-32600,"message":"Bad Request: Missing session ID"}} ``` ## Suggested fix Extend the recovery trigger (currently 404-only, see #32088) to also cover a **400** that indicates a missing/expired session — e.g. body matching `No valid session ID` / `Missing session ID`, or JSON-RPC error code `-32600` with `session` in the message. Keep the same bounded single-retry behavior already implemented. ## OpenCode version 1.17.8 (desktop) ## Operating System macOS Related: #25137, #28567

signals.title: perf(plugin): O(N) dispatch overhead on every trigger call — pre-index hooks by name
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request ## Performance: eliminate O(N) plugin dispatch overhead on every trigger call `packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts` has two hot paths that scale linearly with the number of loaded plugins on **every single message, tool call, and config change**. With 10+ plugins loaded these add measurable latency to the session loop — especially `trigger()`, which fires multiple times per assistant turn. Both fixes are purely internal (no public API change, no behaviour change, no new dependencies), and together they reduced our measured plugin-dispatch overhead to near-zero on a 12-plugin workload. --- ### Problem 1: `events.listen(...)` always subscribes even when no plugin uses `event` The current code unconditionally subscribes to the global event bus: ```ts // current upstream const unsubscribe = yield* events.listen((event) => { if (event.location?.directory !== ctx.directory) return Effect.void return Effect.sync(() => { for (const hook of hooks) { void hook["event"]?.({ event: { id: event.id, type: event.type, properties: event.data } as any }) } }) }) yield* Effect.addFinalizer(() => unsubscribe) ``` **Cost**: On every emitted event — even when zero plugins implement `event` — this allocates an `Effect.sync`, does a directory equality check, then linearly scans all hooks hitting `?.` on each. For a typical session producing hundreds of events/sec during streaming, this is pure waste. **Fix**: Pre-filter once at startup; skip the subscription entirely when the filtered set is empty: ```ts const eventListeners = hooks.filter((h) => typeof h.event === "function") if (eventListeners.length > 0) { const unsubscribe = yield* events.listen((event) => { if (event.location?.directory !== ctx.directory) return Effect.void return Effect.sync(() => { for (const hook of eventListeners) { void hook.event!({ event: { id: event.id, type: event.type, properties: event.data } as any }) } }) }) yield* Effect.addFinalizer(() => unsubscribe) } ``` **Impact**: Zero-listener projects (the majority — most plugins are auth/config only) pay absolutely nothing. Listener projects iterate a smaller pre-filtered array without optional-chaining overhead. --- ### Problem 2: `trigger()` linearly scans all hooks on every call `trigger()` is the **hottest function in the plugin system** — it fires for `chat.params`, `chat.message`, `tool.execute`, `config`, etc. Current implementation: ```ts // current upstream for (const hook of s.hooks) { const fn = hook[name] as any if (!fn) continue yield* Effect.promise(async () => fn(input, output)) } ``` With N plugins and M trigger names, every trigger call does N property lookups and N conditional branches even when 0 or 1 hooks actually implement that name. On a 12-plugin setup triggering ~6 hook names per assistant message, this is 72 wasted iterations per message turn. **Fix**: Build a `Map<string, Hooks[]>` dispatch table once at plugin-load time: ```ts // at state init: const hooksByName = new Map<string, Hooks[]>() for (const hook of hooks) { for (const name of Object.keys(hook) as (keyof Hooks)[]) { if (typeof hook[name] !== "function") continue const list = hooksByName.get(name as string) if (list) list.push(hook) else hooksByName.set(name as string, [hook]) } } return { hooks, hooksByName } // in trigger(): const matched = s.hooksByName.get(name as string) if (!matched) return output for (const hook of matched) { const fn = hook[name] as any yield* Effect.promise(async () => fn(input, output)) } ``` **Impact**: - Unhandled hook names (the common case per trigger): **O(1) early return** instead of O(N) scan. - Handled hook names: iterate only the relevant subset, zero wasted branches. - Hook execution order preserved (insertion order of the Map values array). --- ### Summary | Path | Before | After | |------|--------|-------| | `trigger("chat.params", ...)` with 12 plugins, 1 handler | 12 iterations, 11 `if (!fn) continue` | 1 iteration, direct dispatch | | `trigger("chat.message", ...)` with 12 plugins, 0 handlers | 12 iterations, all skipped | Map miss → immediate return | | Event stream, 0 event hooks | Subscribe + per-event O(N) scan | No subscription at all | Both changes add ~15 lines of init-time code and `State.hooksByName: Map<string, Hooks[]>`. No runtime allocations added to the hot path — only removed. Happy to send a PR with these changes if maintainers are interested. #### Notes - Related but orthogonal to #20285 (parallel plugin events) — that proposal is about concurrency policy; this one is about dispatch-table cost. - Type `State` gains one field: `hooksByName: Map<string, Hooks[]>`. - No public API change, no plugin contract change.

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Provide Drizzle SQLite database schema documentation (SCHEMA.md)
signals.text: ### Description There is **no documentation of the SQLite database schema** of `opencode.db`. Users who need to recover sessions from the DB (e.g. after a UI bug) must reverse-engineer the Drizzle ORM schema from source code. `packages/docs/` and all README files contain **zero** references to database structure, tables, or JSON columns. Originally filed as NeuralNomadsAI/CodeNomad#559 (closed as wrong repo). ### Solution A `SCHEMA.md` or docs page documenting: - All 19 tables with column types (definitions in `packages/core/src/*/sql.ts`) - JSON discriminator shapes for `message.data` (role: user/assistant), `part.data` (type: text, reasoning, tool, file, snapshot, patch, agent, compaction, subtask, retry, step-start, step-finish), and `session_message.data` - ID prefixes: `ses_` (session), `msg_` (message), `prt_` (part), `wrk_` (workspace) - Timestamp convention: epoch milliseconds (`Date.now()`) - Relationship between `session_message` (legacy) and `message`+`part` (current) - `workspace_id`/`workspace` relationship - Recovery query examples ### Verification - [x] I searched for existing issues and found none about database schema documentation - [x] This is a feature request for documentation, not a bug report - [x] I have read the contributing guidelines

signals.title: OpenCode Desktop keeps restoring old project (frisiusmc2025) instead of selected project (groningenairport2023)
signals.text: ### Description OpenCode Desktop keeps binding the active chat/session to an old project (frisiusmc2025), even when I explicitly open groningenairport2023. In the active chat, the working directory remains frisiusmc2025. Environment OpenCode Desktop: 1.16.2 macOS User data directory: ~/Library/Application Support/ai.opencode.desktop Expected behavior When I open /Users/sakevellema/projects/groningenairport2023, the active/new session should use that project. lastProject and workspace state should switch to groningenairport2023. Actual behavior opencode.global.dat repeatedly reverts to: server.lastProject.local = /Users/sakevellema/projects/frisiusmc2025 server.projects.local = [frisiusmc2025] layout.page.lastProjectSession may contain both projects, but the active session still resolves to frisius. Even after resetting profile/state and explicitly opening airport, the chat returns to frisius context. ### Plugins “I’m not using any OpenCode plugins (plugin is not set in my config). I only have two MCP servers enabled: figma (remote, localhost) context7 (local @upstash/context7-mcp)” ### OpenCode version Version 1.16.2 (1.16.2) ### Steps to reproduce Steps to reproduce Open OpenCode with an existing session on frisiusmc2025. Open/select /Users/sakevellema/projects/groningenairport2023. Ask “which project is this?” (or check cwd). It still reports/uses frisiusmc2025. What I already tried Manually edited opencode.global.dat (server.lastProject, projects.local, layout.page.lastProjectSession). Renamed/removed opencode.global.dat*. Full profile reset: moved ~/Library/Application Support/ai.opencode.desktop and let it recreate. Started app with explicit project path: open -na OpenCode "/Users/.../groningenairport2023" Started with alternate --user-data-dir. Fully closed app processes (pkill) between attempts. signals.title: [FEATURE]: Preserve Failed Attempts During Context Compaction
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request During context compaction, when the conversation context becomes full, the model may fail to preserve information about previous unsuccessful attempts. As a result, after compaction, it can lose awareness that a particular approach has already been tried and failed. This leads to the model repeating the same attempt instead of exploring alternative solutions, reducing efficiency and potentially causing loops in long-running tasks. Expected behavior: Context compaction should retain key information about failed attempts, rejected approaches, and encountered errors. After compaction, the model should be able to recognize that a previous strategy did not work and avoid unnecessarily repeating it. Actual behavior: Information about failed attempts may be omitted during compaction. The model sometimes retries the same approach after compaction, even though it had already been attempted and proven unsuccessful earlier in the conversation. Impact: Repeated work and wasted tokens. Reduced effectiveness in debugging, coding, and multi-step problem-solving tasks. Increased likelihood of entering repetitive solution loops during long conversations.

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Surface compaction progress and live context usage in the TUI
signals.text: ## Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. I did find the closed overlap in #16395, where the TUI expected a compacting status but the server never set one. I think this is worth reviving as that lifecycle fix plus a separate always-visible context countdown. ## Describe the enhancement you want to request I maintain oh-my-openagent, a community OpenCode plugin. Filing this as a regular community proposal, not on behalf of OpenCode. Right now compaction can make the TUI feel frozen. During `/compact` or auto-compaction, there may be no clear signal for several seconds, which matches the pain in #26381 around long spinners with no visible progress. There is also no always-visible context countdown, so users cannot anticipate auto-compaction. I am proposing two honest indicators: 1. Always show `Context NN%`, computed from used tokens divided by the model context window. When the threshold is computable, the PoC now renders `Context NN% · auto-compact ~MM%`, mirroring the server `usable()` formula with the default reserved buffer. 2. While compaction runs, show `Compacting conversation...`, a spinner, elapsed seconds, and an indeterminate bar. Here is the PoC in the real TUI during `/compact`: ![compaction progress and context countdown in the opencode TUI](https://github.com/MoerAI/opencode/releases/download/demo-compaction-progress/compaction-demo.gif) I do not want a fake operation percent or ETA. The compaction summary is an LLM call with no known output length, so elapsed time plus an indeterminate animation is the honest version. The only percent should be the context countdown, based on used/window. Related issues: #16395 is the closest one. #27359 asks for async compaction with a `Compacting...` signal. #24807 asks for better terminal-native progress. #11434 asks for more context-window visibility. #21520 points at the same user problem from the threshold side. Design questions for maintainers: 1. Channel: should this add a `compacting` variant to public `session.status` / `SessionStatus`, giving one source for active/idle state, abort/undo, notifications, and SDK polling, or should it use a dedicated compaction event to avoid widening the public union? 2. Should the always-visible countdown be default-on or opt-in? 3. Should the countdown show `auto-compact ~MM%` only if a real threshold is exposed, and is exposing that threshold desirable? I have a working PoC: [the draft PR](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/32927). The operation indicator is gated behind `experimentalEventSystem`, so default UX stays unchanged when the flag is off. A live TUI capture shows both indicators during `/compact`, including `Compacting conversation...` with elapsed seconds and `Context 5%`. The recording above is from that run.

signals.title: [BUG] MCP tools connected but not exposed to agent
signals.text: ### Description # [BUG] MCP tools connected but not exposed to agent ## Description MCP server `pdfrag` connects successfully and exposes 6 tools via `tools/list`, but the tools do not appear in the agent's available tool list. The server is working correctly (responds to MCP protocol, tools are valid), but something in the opencode pipeline isn't passing those tools to the agent. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Create a custom MCP server (Python, stdio transport) 2. Register in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`: ```json "mcp": { "pdfrag": { "type": "local", "command": "/Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.14/bin/pdfrag-mcp" } } ``` 3. Run `opencode mcp list` → shows "connected" with green checkmark 4. Start opencode session → tools NOT available to agent ## Expected Behavior MCP tools should be available as first-class tools in the agent session after successful connection. ## Actual Behavior - Server connects successfully - `opencode mcp list` shows "connected" - MCP protocol handshake works (initialize, tools/list returns 6 valid tools) - Tools do NOT appear in agent's available tool list - Agent cannot call MCP tools ## Investigation 1. **Server works correctly**: Verified with Python MCP client - server responds to `initialize`, `tools/list`, and tool calls 2. **Server format matches working servers**: Compared with `token-optimizer` and `lean-ctx` servers - same structure, capabilities, and tool definitions 3. **No error logs**: opencode logs show no errors related to pdfrag 4. **opencode binary is compiled**: Cannot inspect source directly, but binary analysis shows MCP tool registration code exists ## Similar Issue Found similar issue on hermes-agent: [#41625](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/41625) - "MCP tools discovered but not exposed to agent in TUI mode" The suspected cause there is a race condition in the TUI startup path with a timeout that's too short for MCP discovery. ## Environment - OpenCode version: 1.17.8 - OS: macOS (darwin) - Python: 3.14 - MCP transport: stdio (local subprocess) ## Workaround Use CLI or Python direct calls: ```bash python3 pdf_rag.py query "question" ``` ## Request Please investigate why MCP tools are not being exposed to the agent despite successful connection. This may be related to: - Race condition in tool discovery (similar to hermes-agent #41625) - Tool filtering logic - Agent tool context initialization ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signals.title: '--continue' flag causes 'Unexpected server error' toast at boot (sessionID placeholder is literal 'dummy')
signals.text: **Version**: 21 (bundled binary, macOS arm64) **Steps**: 1. Run `opencode --continue` (or `-c`) 2. Toast appears: "Unexpected server error. Check server logs for details." **Log evidence** (`~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`): ``` level=ERROR message=failed error="Error: Expected a string starting with \"ses\", got \"dummy\"" ``` **Root cause** — TUI bundle sets a hardcoded placeholder `"dummy"` as the initial route sessionID when `--continue` is passed: ```js get initialRoute(){ return U.args.continue ? {type:"session", sessionID:"dummy"} : void 0 } ``` Session-ID validation expects the `ses_` prefix, so `"dummy"` throws before the subsequent `useEffect` hook navigates to the actual last session. Cosmetic — functionality still works — but the error toast is alarming to users. **Fix suggestion**: pass `undefined` instead of `"dummy"`, or skip initial-route validation when the session has not loaded yet.

signals.title: Remote MCP OAuth: access token is not refreshed despite refresh token being present
signals.text: ### Description I'm using a remote MCP server protected by OAuth 2.0 / OIDC. The initial authentication flow succeeds, and OpenCode stores both the access token and the refresh token. However, when the short-lived access token expires, OpenCode does not appear to perform a refresh-token grant. Instead, the MCP transitions to **"Requires Authentication"** and all MCP calls fail until I authenticate again. ## Environment * OpenCode **1.17.11** * Remote MCP server * OAuth 2.0 / OIDC * Identity Provider: **Keycloak** * Access token lifetime: **5 minutes** * Refresh token: long-lived ## Expected behavior When the access token expires, OpenCode should use the stored refresh token (`grant_type=refresh_token`) to obtain a new access token and continue communicating with the MCP server without requiring user interaction. ## Actual behavior After the access token expires: * MCP requests fail. * `opencode mcp list` reports the server as **Requires Authentication**. * The stored refresh token does not appear to be used. * Running `opencode mcp auth <server>` restores functionality until the next access-token expiration. ## `opencode mcp debug` output (redacted) ```text $ opencode mcp debug quartermaster ┌ MCP OAuth Debug │ ● Server: quartermaster │ ● URL: https://<redacted>/mcp │ ● Auth status: ✓ authenticated │ ● Access token: eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIs... │ ● Expires: 2026-06-30T15:13:10.634Z │ ● Refresh token: present │ ◇ HTTP response: 401 Unauthorized │ ● WWW-Authenticate: │ Bearer realm="Instructions MCP", │ resource_metadata="https://<redacted>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource" │ ▲ Server returned 401 Unauthorized │ ● Testing OAuth flow (without completing authorization)... │ ◆ Connection successful (already authenticated) │ └ Debug complete ``` ## Additional information The OAuth server is **Keycloak**, and refresh-token flow has been verified to work correctly with other OAuth clients. The authorization server supports `grant_type=refresh_token`, and OpenCode's debug output reports: ``` Refresh token: present ``` This suggests that the refresh token is successfully stored, but is either never used or the refresh flow fails before retrying the original request. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version 1.17.11 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Configure a remote MCP server protected by OAuth/OIDC. 2. Authenticate using: ```bash opencode mcp auth <server> ``` 3. Confirm authentication succeeds. 4. Verify with: ```bash opencode mcp debug <server> ``` that both an access token and refresh token are present. 5. Wait for the 5-minute access token to expire. 6. Invoke any MCP tool or run: ```bash opencode mcp list ``` ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Ubuntu 24.04 ### Terminal tmux

signals.title: New Workspace sessions stall forever under the new layout — worktree.ready listener only lives in the legacy layout
signals.text: ### Description Starting a session with **"New Workspace"** (instead of "Local repository") in the desktop app / web UI stalls indefinitely: after sending the first message, nothing happens, no assistant response is produced, and no session title is generated. After ~5 minutes a toast appears saying the workspace is still preparing. **Root cause:** When "New Workspace" is selected, the client creates a git worktree and then holds the first prompt in `waitForWorktree()` (`packages/app/src/components/prompt-input/submit.ts`) until the shared `WorktreeState` transitions `pending → ready`. That transition only happens when `WorktreeState.ready(...)` is called in response to the `worktree.ready` server event. The **only** code that listens for `worktree.ready` / `worktree.failed` and calls `WorktreeState.ready/failed(...)` is `useSDKNotificationToasts()` in the **legacy** layout (`packages/app/src/pages/layout.tsx:389-403`, invoked at line 498). The **new** layout (`packages/app/src/pages/layout-new.tsx`, used when `newLayoutDesigns()` is enabled — see `app.tsx:335-339`) does **not** register this listener and doesn't even import `WorktreeState`. Because the "New Workspace" selector is surfaced under the new design, users on the new layout create a worktree whose `worktree.ready` event is emitted by the server and does reach the browser, but nothing consumes it to release the gate. The prompt is therefore never sent → no model turn, no title, and eventually the 5-minute `waitForWorktree` timeout toast. Evidence gathered while diagnosing: - Server log: the worktree boots cleanly (`creating instance` → `bootstrapping` → `init count=21`), a session is created in the worktree directory with the default title, and **no prompt loop ever runs** for that session (the server never received a prompt). - Raw SSE stream (`GET /global/event`) in DevTools: the `worktree.ready` payload **does** arrive at the renderer with the correct `directory`, e.g. `{"directory":".../worktree/<projectID>/kind-rocket","payload":{"type":"worktree.ready",...}}`. - The stall ends only via the `waitForWorktree` 5-minute timeout ("still preparing" toast), confirming the waiter is created but never resolved. - Verified **not** caused by: SDK event-schema dropping (worktree events are in the union and the stream is pass-through), event coalescing, scope-key mismatch (single sidecar → both scopes are `"local"`), directory-string mismatch, `WorktreeState` module duplication across chunks, or stream-not-started. ### Plugins None. ### OpenCode version 1.17.18 (desktop, Beta channel) — also affects `dev`/`origin/dev` (the handler is still only in `layout.tsx`, not `layout-new.tsx`). ### Steps to reproduce 1. Enable the new layout designs (`newLayoutDesigns`) so the workspace selector is shown (non-prod channel). 2. Open a git project and start a new session. 3. In the new-session form, select **"New Workspace"** instead of "Local repository". 4. Type a message and send it. 5. Observe: the session stalls, no response, no title. After ~5 minutes a "workspace still preparing" toast appears. Expected: the worktree becomes ready, the prompt is delivered, the model responds, and a title is generated — the same as "Local repository". ### Screenshot and/or share link N/A ### Operating System macOS (reproduced on macOS; root cause is platform-independent). ### Terminal Desktop app (Electron renderer) — not terminal-specific.
