signals.title: Groq requests exceed TPM limit even in an empty directory
signals.text: ### Description # Bug: Groq requests exceed TPM limit even in an empty directory ## Environment * OpenCode version: **1.18.4** * OS: Linux 6.17.0-PRoot-Distro (Termux + Ubuntu PRoot, arm64) * Provider: **Groq** * Models tested: * `groq/llama-3.1-8b-instant` * `groq/openai/gpt-oss-20b` ## Description OpenCode consistently sends requests that exceed Groq's Tokens Per Minute (TPM) limit, even when started in an empty directory with a brand-new session. The problem occurs before any meaningful user prompt is sent. Even the hidden **title** request exceeds the TPM limit. This makes OpenCode unusable with Groq's free tier. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Install OpenCode 1.18.4. 2. Configure a valid Groq API key. 3. Create an empty directory: ```bash mkdir empty cd empty ``` 4. Run: ```bash opencode run hi --print-logs ``` ## Expected behavior The prompt for a one-word request (`hi`) should be small enough to fit within Groq's TPM limits. ## Actual behavior The request is rejected immediately: For `llama-3.1-8b-instant`: ```text Request too large for model `llama-3.1-8b-instant` Limit 6000 TPM Requested 42781 ``` For `openai/gpt-oss-20b`: ```text Request too large for model `openai/gpt-oss-20b` Limit 8000 TPM Requested 38369 ``` ## Diagnostics performed I verified all of the following: * Fresh Groq API key * Fresh Groq account * Empty directory * New OpenCode session * `opencode run` * `opencode --pure` * No project files * No `AGENTS.md` * No plugins * Default configuration * Multiple Groq models Resolved configuration: ```json { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "compaction": { "auto": false, "prune": false }, "agent": {}, "mode": {}, "plugin": [], "command": {}, "username": "root" } ``` `opencode debug info`: ```text opencode version: 1.18.4 plugins: none ``` ## Additional observations The requests appear to have nearly constant sizes across completely fresh sessions: ### Title agent Approximately **32.5k tokens** ```text agent=title Requested 32550 tokens ``` ### Build agent Approximately **42.7k tokens** ```text agent=build Requested 42781 tokens ``` ### GPT-OSS ```text agent=title Requested 32589 tokens agent=build Requested 38369 tokens ``` The consistency suggests the large token count is not coming from my project or conversation history. ## Question Is OpenCode intentionally sending a very large internal prompt/tool schema to Groq, or could this be a regression in prompt construction or the Groq provider integration? I'm happy to run additional diagnostics or test a development build if that would help. [log.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30217590/log.txt) ### Plugins none ### OpenCode version 1.18.4 ### Steps to reproduce just said hi in a new chat using groq gpt oss or any groq model ### Screenshot and/or share link ### Operating System proot-distro ubuntu ### Terminal termux

signals.title: Desktop 1.18.4: Settings "Auto-accept permissions" is disconnected from runtime auto-accept (toggle ON still prompts)
signals.text: ## Summary OpenCode Desktop's **Settings → General → "Auto-accept permissions"** control is broken / misleading on **v1.18.4 (macOS arm64)**. There are **two separate problems that combine into one user-facing failure**: 1. **Persistence / settings-store bug family** (already reported across several issues): the Settings toggle either won't flip, won't stick across restart/workspace changes, or requires hand-editing `default.dat`. 2. **Runtime disconnect (main finding on 1.18.4):** even when `settings.permissions.autoApprove` is successfully set to `true` and the Settings UI shows the switch **ON**, **permission prompts still appear** because the live auto-accept engine does **not** read that settings field. In short: the Settings toggle looks like a global "auto-approve all tool permissions" switch, but the runtime auto-accept path is a **different store** (session/directory `autoAccept` map). The Settings value is not wired into `shouldAutoRespond()`. --- ## Environment | Item | Value | |---|---| | OpenCode Desktop | **1.18.4** (`CFBundleShortVersionString` / `app-version.v1`) | | OS | macOS **26.5.2** (Build 25F84) | | Arch | **arm64** (Apple Silicon) | | App path | `/Applications/OpenCode.app` | | Desktop data dir | `~/Library/Application Support/ai.opencode.desktop/` | | Settings file | `default.dat` → key `settings.v3` | | Terminals installed | **Ghostty** present; **WezTerm not installed** | | Default shell | `/bin/zsh` | --- ## Expected behavior 1. Turning **Settings → General → Auto-accept permissions** ON should: - persist across app restarts - cause subsequent tool permission prompts to be auto-approved (or clearly document that this setting is only a default and that a separate session/directory auto-accept must also be enabled) 2. When the toggle is ON and persisted as `"permissions":{"autoApprove":true}`, users should **not** continue to get blocking permission modals for ordinary tool calls unless an explicit deny rule exists. 3. If the Settings toggle is intentionally only a default / not runtime-authoritative, the UI copy should say so (today it reads like a working global switch). ## Actual behavior ### A) Settings toggle does not reliably control runtime approvals After forcing persistence so the Settings UI shows **Auto-accept permissions = ON**, a session still showed a blocking permission modal: - **Title:** Permission needed - **Prompt:** Run shell command - **Command:** `wezterm start --cwd <home>` - **Actions shown:** Always allow / Reject / Allow once - **Workspace context:** `<home>` (home) So the global Settings switch being ON did **not** suppress the prompt. ### B) Persistence is fragile (same family as prior reports) Before workaround, `default.dat` contained: ```json "permissions":{"autoApprove":false} ``` Observed symptoms matching prior reports: - toggle hard to turn on / does not feel sticky - users resort to quitting the app and hand-editing `default.dat` Manual workaround used: 1. Quit OpenCode completely 2. Edit `~/Library/Application Support/ai.opencode.desktop/default.dat` 3. Set nested `settings.v3` → `permissions.autoApprove` to `true` 4. Relaunch After that: - Settings UI showed the switch **ON** - file still contained `"permissions":{"autoApprove":true}` - **but permission prompts still appeared** --- ## Reproduction steps ### Path 1 — UI toggle (common user path) 1. Open OpenCode Desktop **1.18.4** on macOS. 2. Open **Settings → General**. 3. Toggle **Auto-accept permissions** ON. 4. Quit and relaunch the app (or switch workspace). 5. Observe either: - toggle returns OFF / is not clickable / does not stick, **or** - toggle appears ON but permission prompts still appear for shell/tool calls. ### Path 2 — Forced settings persistence (proves runtime disconnect) 1. Fully quit OpenCode. 2. Edit: ```text ~/Library/Application Support/ai.opencode.desktop/default.dat ``` 3. Ensure nested JSON in `settings.v3` contains: ```json "permissions":{"autoApprove":true} ``` 4. Relaunch OpenCode. 5. Confirm Settings UI shows **Auto-accept permissions = ON**. 6. In a session, trigger a tool that needs approval (example observed: shell command / external terminal launch). 7. **Observe:** permission modal still appears (`Always allow` / `Reject` / `Allow once`). ### Path 3 — Contrast with working auto-accept entry points Per docs and in-app strings, these *do* target the runtime auto-accept path: - TUI/command: **Enable auto-approve permissions** / `command.permissions.autoaccept.enable` - CLI: `opencode --auto` - Session/directory auto-accept APIs (`enableAutoAccept`, `toggleAutoAcceptDirectory`) Expected: Settings toggle should either call the same path or clearly not claim to. --- ## Evidence from installed Desktop build (1.18.4 asar) Inspected `/Applications/OpenCode.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar` (extracted renderer assets). ### 1) Settings store has a dedicated field Default settings include: ```js permissions: { autoApprove: false } ``` Getter/setter: ```js permissions: { autoApprove: withFallback( () => store2.permissions?.autoApprove, defaultSettings.permissions.autoApprove ), setAutoApprove(value) { setStore("permissions", "autoApprove", value); } } ``` This is what lands in `default.dat` → `settings.v3`. ### 2) Runtime auto-accept uses a different store Permission runtime methods: ```js function isAutoAccepting(sessionID, directory) { return autoRespondsPermission(store2.autoAccept, sessions(directory), { sessionID }, directory); } function shouldAutoRespond(permission, directory) { return autoRespondsPermission( store2.autoAccept, sessions(directory), permission, directory ); } ``` Enable path writes **`store2.autoAccept[key] = true`** (session key / directory key), then optionally drains pending permissions via `permission.list` + `respondPending`. Event handler only auto-responds on `permission.asked` when that **autoAccept map** says so: ```js const handlePermission = (e2) => { const event = e2.details; if (event?.type !== "permission.asked") return; void respondPending(event.properties, e2.name); }; ``` ### 3) No bridge found from settings.autoApprove → runtime autoAccept In the 1.18.4 renderer bundle, `settings.permissions.autoApprove` / `setAutoApprove` appear to be settings-persistence only. Runtime decisions read `store2.autoAccept`, **not** `settings.permissions.autoApprove`. That explains the user-visible contradiction: | Layer | State after workaround | Effect | |---|---|---| | `default.dat` `permissions.autoApprove` | `true` | Settings switch can show ON | | Runtime `store2.autoAccept` | empty / not enabled for session/dir | prompts still block | ### 4) UI labels reinforce the wrong mental model In-app strings present auto-accept as a real runtime mode: - `command.permissions.autoaccept.enable` = "Auto-accept permissions" - toast: "Permission requests will be automatically approved" Settings exposes a control with the same product language, but it is not clearly scoped as "default only" / "session must still enable". --- ## Related issues (please link / consider consolidating) This is not an isolated report; it looks like a multi-issue regression cluster around Desktop permissions UX: | Issue | Relevance | |---|---| | https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/27487 | Toggle resets OFF after restart / `default.dat` stays false (closed stale; still reproducible in spirit on 1.18.4) | | https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/37617 | Desktop 1.18.3 toggle permanently disabled (`not-allowed`); notes dual settings implementations under `newLayoutDesigns` | | https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/33788 | 1.17.10 can't use Auto Approve toggle in settings | | https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/37880 | Desktop "Always Allow" acts like one-shot / not sticky | | https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/20998 | Pending permissions not auto-accepted after refresh/reconnect | | https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/21578 | Request to restore per-session auto-accept control in Desktop UI | **Why this issue is still worth a new report:** prior issues mostly cover "toggle won't flip/persist". This report adds a stronger claim for 1.18.4: > Even when the persisted settings value is `true` and the Settings UI shows ON, runtime permission prompts still appear because the Settings field is not the source of truth for auto-response. --- ## Secondary observation (same session; may be separate bug) While auto-accept was ON in Settings, the agent requested: ```bash wezterm start --cwd <home> ``` On this machine: - **WezTerm is not installed** - **Ghostty is installed** (`/Applications/Ghostty.app`) - Desktop "Open with" app list in the bundle includes `terminal`, `iterm2`, `ghostty`, `warp`, etc., and does **not** list `wezterm` So the permission prompt was for launching a terminal app the user does not have. That may be agent/tool choice rather than Desktop open-app integration, but it made the broken auto-accept UX much more alarming ("what is this WezTerm process?"). If useful, happy to split that into a separate issue (prefer installed terminal / Ghostty / configured shell; don't propose missing `wezterm`). --- ## Impact - Users cannot trust the Settings switch. - Workarounds are unsafe/confusing (hand-edit Electron data files). - Permission prompts continue to block agent flow even after users believe they enabled auto-accept. - Erodes trust: a prompt for an unknown binary name (`wezterm`) while auto-accept appears enabled feels like malware, even though WezTerm is a legitimate terminal emulator. --- ## Suggested fix ### Minimum correct behavior 1. **Wire Settings → Auto-accept permissions into runtime** - On app/project load, if `settings.permissions.autoApprove === true`, initialize runtime auto-accept for the active directory/session (same path as `enableDirectory` / `enableAutoAccept`). - When the Settings toggle changes, call the same enable/disable APIs used by the command palette / session controls. 2. **Or**, if Settings is intentionally only a default: - rename/clarify UI copy - show effective runtime state separately ("Session auto-accept: ON/OFF") - make the Settings control actually seed new sessions. ### Also fix persistence - Ensure Settings toggle writes `settings.v3.permissions.autoApprove` reliably under both layout implementations (`newLayoutDesigns` true/false). - Prevent silent overwrite back to `false` on restart/workspace switch. - Add a regression test: flip toggle → quit → relaunch → value remains true → next `permission.asked` auto-responds. ### Acceptance criteria - [ ] Settings toggle ON persists in `default.dat` across restart. - [ ] With toggle ON, new `permission.asked` events for the active workspace are auto-approved (unless explicit deny rules). - [ ] With toggle OFF, prompts still appear. - [ ] Command-palette / CLI `--auto` / session toggle remain consistent with Settings (or Settings is clearly labeled as default only and still seeds runtime state). - [ ] No dual-store split where UI says ON and runtime stays OFF. --- ## Workarounds for other users (current) 1. **Session/runtime auto-accept** via command palette: - **Auto-accept permissions** / stop command - Desktop keybind users report: **Cmd+Shift+A** (verify locally; command id `permissions.autoaccept`) 2. CLI: `opencode --auto` 3. Config permissions (documented global rules), e.g. project/user config: ```json { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "permission": { "*": "ask", "bash": "allow" } } ``` 4. Nuclear/hacky: quit app and set `default.dat` → `settings.v3` → `permissions.autoApprove: true` **Note:** on 1.18.4 this may only fix the Settings display, **not** runtime prompts. --- ## Additional local file evidence `default.dat` after workaround (outer keys): ```json { "app-version.v1": "{\"version\":\"1.18.4\"}", "settings.v3": "{...\"permissions\":{\"autoApprove\":true}...}", "highlights.v1": "{\"version\":\"1.18.4\"}" } ``` Parsed: ```json { "permissions": { "autoApprove": true } } ``` Despite that value, shell permission modal still appeared for: ```text wezterm start --cwd <home> ``` --- ## Request Please treat this as a **Desktop permissions source-of-truth bug**, not only a toggle persistence nit. Happy to provide more logs / screen recording if needed. I can also retest a nightly/PR build quickly on this machine.

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Show per-tool elapsed time and turn duration in TUI and web UI
signals.text: ## Verified - [x] I have verified this feature hasn't been suggested before. ## Description **Problem:** Currently neither the TUI nor the web/desktop UI show how long each tool call takes or how much time the current conversation turn has consumed. When debugging slow tools or tracking productivity, users have no visibility into timing. **Data is already available:** The backend already stores ime.start / ime.end on every tool part state and ime.created / ime.completed on every message. No server/protocol changes needed - this is purely a frontend rendering change. **Proposed scope (4 files, ~100 lines):** - **TUI** (packages/tui): show duration text next to each tool row in InlineTool, plus a live elapsed timer in the prompt input area while a turn is running - **Session-UI** (packages/session-ui): show duration in BasicTool component (covers most tools), pass timing through to all registered tool renderers, and surface turn duration in the assistant text part footer The i18n keys (ui.message.duration.seconds / minutesSeconds) already exist in all supported languages. **Benefits:** Users can identify slow tools at a glance, estimate remaining wait time, and benchmark prompts across models - all without changing workflow. The change is additive (no existing UI removed or restructured).

signals.title: [Bug] Agent loop produces duplicate responses due to non-monotonic MessageID comparison
signals.text: ## Description Agent loop fails to exit after `finish=stop` when the assistant message ID is lexicographically smaller than the user message ID, causing a duplicate LLM call and a second assistant response. In `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts`, the `runLoop` function uses a **string comparison** to decide whether to break the loop: ```typescript if ( lastAssistant?.finish && !["tool-calls"].includes(lastAssistant.finish) && !hasToolCalls && lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id // string lexicographic comparison ) { break } ``` `MessageID.ascending()` generates IDs like `msg_f93b221d1...`. These IDs are **not guaranteed to be lexicographically monotonic**. When the assistant message ID happens to sort before the user message ID, the condition `lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id` evaluates to `false`, the loop does not break, and a second LLM call is made — producing a duplicate assistant response. This only affects agents that return `finish=stop` without tool calls (e.g. a plan-mode / discussion agent). Agents that use `finish=tool-calls` follow a different code path and are unaffected. ## Concrete evidence Session with 5 consecutive duplicate pairs. Each pair: same `parentID`, two `finish=stop` assistant messages, gap of 2–32ms between them. | User message ID | First assistant ID | `user.id < asst1.id` | Second assistant ID | `user.id < asst2.id` | |---|---|---|---|---| | `msg_f93b221d1...` | `msg_f93b221b9...` | `false` ← loop continues | `msg_f93b2853f...` | `true` ← loop breaks | | `msg_f93b7b78b...` | `msg_f93b7b748...` | `false` ← loop continues | `msg_f93b7efa2...` | `true` ← loop breaks | | `msg_f93bb731c...` | `msg_f93bb72da...` | `false` ← loop continues | `msg_f93bbd637...` | `true` ← loop breaks | | `msg_f93c03ac5...` | `msg_f93c03a9e...` | `false` ← loop continues | `msg_f93c0b842...` | `true` ← loop breaks | | `msg_f93c23126...` | `msg_f93c230ef...` | `false` ← loop continues | `msg_f93c26a5d...` | `true` ← loop breaks | In all 5 cases, the first assistant message's ID is lexicographically **smaller** than the user's, so the loop runs one extra iteration and produces a second response. ## Plugins oh-my-openagent@latest ## OpenCode version 1.18.5 ## Steps to reproduce 1. Use an agent that responds with text only (no tool calls), returning `finish=stop` directly. 2. Send a message. In ~some cases (when `MessageID.ascending()` produces an assistant ID that sorts before the user ID), the agent will respond twice with similar but slightly different content. 3. The issue is intermittent because it depends on ID generation, but happens frequently in sessions with many turns. ## Suggested fix Replace the string ID comparison with a more reliable ordering check. Options: - Compare by `time.created` timestamps instead of ID strings - Use a numeric counter that is guaranteed monotonic - Or at minimum, don't use the ID comparison as the loop exit gate — `finish=stop` (when not `tool-calls` and no pending tool calls) should be sufficient to break ## Operating System macOS 15.7.7 (x64) ## Terminal OpenChamber (Electron app, opencode v1.18.5)
signals.author: woohahahaaa

signals.title: Run loop can never exit when message ids are not time-sortable (imported sessions loop until the provider 400s)
signals.text: ### Summary `SessionPrompt.runLoop` decides a turn is finished by comparing message ids as **plain strings**. That is only correct because opencode's own ids embed a timestamp. Any session whose ids do not sort chronologically — e.g. one produced by a third-party importer — can put the loop in a state where it never exits: opencode re-requests indefinitely, each request ending on an assistant message, which providers reject. On Anthropic the user-visible result is a generic `Unexpected server error`, with the real cause (`This model does not support assistant message prefill`) buried. ### Where `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts`, in `runLoop`: ```ts if ( lastAssistant?.finish && !["tool-calls"].includes(lastAssistant.finish) && !hasToolCalls && lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id // <-- lexicographic id comparison ) { yield* Effect.logInfo("exiting loop", { "session.id": sessionID }) break } ``` `MessageV2.latest()` selects the "last" user/assistant the same way. The invariant this relies on comes from `packages/schema/src/identifier.ts`: ids are a 12-hex-char prefix encoding `timestamp_ms * 0x1000 + counter`, plus 14 random chars — so they sort chronologically as strings. Nothing validates that invariant at the `import` boundary, and it is not documented in the `SessionV1` schema. ### Reproduction 1. Import a session whose message ids are random rather than time-sortable (I hit this with [baton](https://github.com/Kaseban/baton), which emitted `msg_<uuid>`; a hand-written JSON with random ids reproduces it too). 2. Resume it and send any prompt. 3. The first request succeeds. opencode then immediately issues a second request with the assistant's own reply appended, and the provider returns 400. Captured with a forwarding proxy in front of the provider: ``` req 1: 1035312B -> 200 OK response: "stop_reason":"end_turn" + "message_stop" req 2: 1035378B -> 400 "This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message." ``` The first response is a clean, complete turn — `end_turn`, `message_stop` — and opencode continues anyway. Failure is probabilistic in session length, because ~2.6% of random hex ids sort above a freshly generated native id: | messages | P(at least one imported id outranks the live ones) | observed | |---|---|---| | 3 | ~8% | worked | | 6 | ~15% | worked once, failed once | | 423 | ~100% | failed every attempt | Ruled out by testing, in case they look like suspects: plugins (reproduced with `--pure`), missing `step-start`/`step-finish` parts (synthesised them, no change), unpaired `tool_use`, unsigned thinking blocks, and empty message content. It reproduces with a structurally valid history — I replayed the exact captured payload standalone and it returned 200. ### Suggested fixes Either would resolve it; the first is the smaller change: 1. **Order by `time.created`** (falling back to id) in the loop test and in `MessageV2.latest()`, instead of comparing id strings. 2. **Break on a terminal finish reason regardless of ordering** — if `lastAssistant.finish === "stop"` and there are no pending tool calls, the turn is over; the id comparison is then only a tiebreaker. Worth considering alongside: a continuation request that would end on an assistant message is invalid for providers that disallow prefill, so guarding that at the request-building layer would turn this class of bug into a clear error rather than a loop. ### Related - #38620 — same seam (replay 400 with thinking + tool use) but a different trigger (`message.error !== undefined`); does not cover id ordering. - #21326, #25774 — orphaned/dangling `tool_use`; also this area, different cause. ### Environment opencode 1.18.4 · macOS arm64 (container, linux/arm64) · Anthropic-compatible endpoint (LiteLLM), `claude-opus-4-8`, `thinking: adaptive`. ### Note on the provider side Not an opencode bug, but it made diagnosis much harder: when the upstream rejected the request, the gateway's fallback chain retried on models that do not support `thinking: adaptive`, so both the original and fallback errors were collapsed into one opaque message. Surfacing the provider's `error.message` verbatim in the session log would have saved a lot of time here.

signals.title: OpenAI Codex OAuth GPT-5.6 limits stale after Codex 0.144.6 correction
signals.text: ### Description The OpenAI Codex OAuth model transform still hardcodes GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna to: ```ts { context: 500_000, input: 372_000, output: 128_000 } ``` That mapping was added by #36248 against the Codex catalog available on July 10. OpenAI subsequently released Codex CLI 0.144.6 on July 18 with the explicit fix: "corrected [GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna] context windows to 272,000 tokens." Codex CLI 0.145.0's bundled `models.json` still reports both `context_window` and `max_context_window` as `272000` for all three GPT-5.6 variants, matching GPT-5.5. OpenCode `dev` still applies the earlier 372k OAuth input override, so compaction can be delayed beyond the window currently advertised by the first-party Codex harness. Following OpenCode's existing split-window convention for GPT-5.5, the current Codex OAuth mapping for GPT-5.6 should be: ```ts { context: 400_000, input: 272_000, output: 128_000 } ``` Direct OpenAI API-key metadata should remain unchanged at the API's full model limits. This only concerns requests routed through ChatGPT/Codex OAuth. References: - Previous report and now-stale values: #36247 - Previous fix: #36248 - Codex 0.144.6 release: https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/tag/rust-v0.144.6 - Codex 0.145.0 catalog: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.145.0/codex-rs/models-manager/models.json - Current OpenCode OAuth transform: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/plugin/openai/codex.ts - Longer-term provider-specific metadata proposal: https://github.com/anomalyco/models.dev/issues/3183 ### Plugins None required to reproduce. The mismatch is in the built-in OpenAI Codex OAuth model transform. ### OpenCode version 1.18.5 and current `dev` as of 2026-07-26. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Authenticate the `openai` provider using ChatGPT Pro/Plus OAuth. 2. Run `opencode models openai --verbose`. 3. Inspect `limit` for `gpt-5.6-sol`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, or `gpt-5.6-luna`. 4. Observe `context: 500000`, `input: 372000`, `output: 128000`. 5. Compare with the Codex 0.145.0 bundled catalog, where all three report `context_window: 272000` and `max_context_window: 272000`. ### Screenshot and/or share link Not applicable; this is directly visible in the two model catalogs. ### Operating System Debian 13 Linux, x86_64. ### Terminal OpenCode web/headless server and CLI.

signals.title: [BUG] Cloudflare AI Gateway: OpenCode duplicates gateway token into Universal Endpoint headers.authorization, bypassing BYOK and leaking credential to upstream provider
signals.text: ### Description When using Cloudflare AI Gateway with DeepSeek as the upstream provider, OpenCode sends requests through the Cloudflare Universal Endpoint. The gateway token is correctly passed via the `cf-aig-authorization` HTTP header. However, the captured request JSON body additionally includes a request-level `headers.authorization` field containing the same Cloudflare gateway token: ```json [ { "endpoint": "chat/completions", "headers": { "authorization": "Bearer <redacted Cloudflare gateway token>", "content-type": "application/json" }, "query": { "model": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash", "max_tokens": 32000, "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": "hello" } ] } } ] ``` The request body has been simplified for brevity. ### Root cause The Universal Endpoint `headers.authorization` field is semantically intended for the upstream provider's API key[^1]. When using BYOK, the Cloudflare documentation explicitly instructs: > Remove provider authorization headers from your requests. Note that you still need to pass `cf-aig-authorization`.[^2] Gateway authentication is already handled by the `cf-aig-authorization` HTTP header. The `headers.authorization` inside the Universal Endpoint payload should be left empty so that BYOK can supply the upstream provider key. However, OpenCode additionally places the Cloudflare gateway token into `headers.authorization`. According to the credential precedence rules[^3]: 1. Provider key on the request — if the request carries provider authentication (e.g., an `Authorization` header), AI Gateway forwards it to the provider unchanged. BYOK and Unified Billing are not consulted. 2. BYOK (stored key) 3. Unified Billing Because `headers.authorization` is present, precedence rule #1 fires. The Cloudflare gateway token is forwarded to DeepSeek as the provider credential, BYOK is entirely bypassed, and DeepSeek rejects the request: ```json { "error": { "message": "Authentication Fails, Your api key: <last 4 chars of Cloudflare token> is invalid", "type": "authentication_error", "param": null, "code": "invalid_request_error" } } ``` The invalid key suffix matches the Cloudflare gateway token, not a DeepSeek API key. > Security note: This is not only a functional bug. The Cloudflare API token is leaked to a third-party provider (DeepSeek) that is not intended to receive it. ### Expected behavior OpenCode should not populate the Universal Endpoint request-level `headers.authorization` when routing to upstream providers via BYOK. The gateway token is already correctly passed via `cf-aig-authorization`; there is no need to duplicate it into the JSON body. Removing `headers.authorization` allows Cloudflare AI Gateway to resolve credentials through BYOK (precedence #2) instead of forwarding the gateway token as a provider key (precedence #1). Concretely, the request body should look like: ```json [ { "endpoint": "chat/completions", "headers": { "content-type": "application/json" }, "query": { "model": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash", "max_tokens": 32000, "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": "hello" } ] } } ] ``` ### Actual behavior OpenCode includes the Cloudflare gateway token in the Universal Endpoint JSON body: ```json "headers": { "authorization": "Bearer <redacted Cloudflare gateway token>" } ``` This triggers credential precedence rule #1, causing the Cloudflare gateway token to be forwarded to DeepSeek as the provider credential, bypassing BYOK[^3] and resulting in an authentication failure. ### Verification Manually sending the same Universal Endpoint payload without the `headers.authorization` field returns HTTP 200. This confirms that the failure is caused by the Cloudflare gateway token being forwarded to DeepSeek as the provider credential, overriding the BYOK-stored DeepSeek API key. [^1]: https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/usage/universal/ [^2]: https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/configuration/bring-your-own-keys/ [^3]: https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/features/unified-billing/#credential-precedence ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version 1.18.11-1 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Configure Cloudflare AI Gateway as the provider in OpenCode. 2. Configure a DeepSeek model, for example: ```jsonc "models": { "deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash": {} } ``` 3. Run `opencode`. 4. Run `/init` or send any message. 5. Observe the authentication error from DeepSeek. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Arch linux ### Terminal Ghostty

signals.title: Grep tool fails on Windows: ripgrep extraction broken by MSIX PowerShell 7 PSModulePath, and failures are cached until restart
signals.text: ### Description The built-in `grep`/`glob` tools fail on Windows when `rg.exe` is not installed. Two bugs are involved: **Bug 1 — ripgrep zip extraction always fails when the Microsoft Store (MSIX) version of PowerShell 7 is installed and used to launch opencode.** opencode downloads ripgrep successfully, then extracts the zip by spawning `powershell.exe` (Windows PowerShell 5.1) with `Expand-Archive` (`packages/core/src/ripgrep/binary.ts`). If opencode was launched from the MSIX PowerShell 7 session, that session's `PSModulePath` lists the Store package's own Modules dir (`c:\program files\windowsapps\microsoft.powershell_<ver>_x64__8wekyb3d8bbwe\Modules`, i.e. `$PSHOME\Modules` of the MSIX pwsh) **before** `C:\Windows\system32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\Modules`. The spawned 5.1 process inherits this `PSModulePath` (`extendEnv: true`). When autoloading `Expand-Archive`, the 5.1 module autoloader hits the **PowerShell-7-only (Core edition)** `Microsoft.PowerShell.Archive` module in the MSIX dir first, deems it incompatible, and **stops searching** instead of continuing to the compatible 5.1 module in System32. Result: ``` Expand-Archive : 无法加载模块"Microsoft.PowerShell.Archive"，因为找不到模块"Microsoft.PowerShell.Archive"中的"Expand-Archive"命令。 Import-Module Microsoft.PowerShell.Archive 所在位置 行:1 字符: 50 + ... lobal:ProgressPreference = 'SilentlyContinue'; Expand-Archive -Litera ... + ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ + CategoryInfo : ObjectNotFound: (Expand-Archive:String) [], CommandNotFoundException + FullyQualifiedErrorId : CouldNotAutoloadMatchingModule ``` The zip is downloaded to `~/.cache/opencode/bin/` but never extracted; every Grep/Glob call repeats download + extraction failure. **Bug 2 — the failed ripgrep resolution is permanently cached.** `binary.ts` wraps the locate/download/extract logic in `Effect.cached`, which caches **failures** as well as successes. Even after the environment is fixed (e.g. `rg.exe` manually placed in `~/.cache/opencode/bin/`), every Grep/Glob call in the **same process** keeps returning the stale failure with no retry, until opencode is restarted. Verified via logs: a fresh process finds `rg.exe` and works immediately; the long-running process keeps failing without even logging a new "downloading ripgrep" attempt. ### Plugins None (default) ### OpenCode version 1.18.13 (CLI, installed via npm) ### Steps to reproduce 1. Do not have `rg.exe` in PATH or in `~/.cache/opencode/bin/` 2. Install PowerShell 7 via Microsoft Store (MSIX) and launch opencode from its terminal 3. Ask the agent to use the `grep` tool 4. Observe `CouldNotAutoloadMatchingModule` error; `ripgrep-15.1.0-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip` is downloaded but never extracted 5. Manually place `rg.exe` into `~/.cache/opencode/bin/` — the tool still fails until opencode is restarted ### Screenshot and/or share link N/A ### Operating System Windows 11 ### Terminal Windows Terminal (PowerShell 7.6.3, Microsoft Store/MSIX install)

signals.title: One configuration file cannot be used by version 1 and version 2
signals.text: ## Description Version 1 and version 2 can be installed at the same time. The two versions read the same configuration file. But one file cannot satisfy both versions. Version 1 stops with an error when the file contains the version 2 keys. The keys are `providers` and `agents`. Version 1 shows this message: ``` Configuration is invalid at <config-dir>/opencode.json ↳ Unrecognized keys: providers, agents ``` The migration document is at https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1 The document says that version 1 fields and version 2 fields can stay together in one file. The document says: "Supported V1 and native V2 fields may coexist at the top level". The document also says: "when both forms set the same canonical value, a valid native V2 value takes precedence". Thus the user can write the provider with the version 1 fields. Version 2 does not obey this rule for a custom provider package. I declare a provider with the version 1 fields. I use the `provider` key. I use the `npm` field. Version 1 reads the file correctly. But version 2 shows no models for this provider. Version 2 shows no error message. I declare the same provider with the version 2 fields. I use the `providers` key. I use the `package` field. Version 2 shows all 32 models. But version 1 stops with the error above. Thus neither format is correct for both versions. The fault does not occur for all packages. A provider with the `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` package loads correctly with the version 1 fields. The fault occurs with the package `commandcode-go-opencode-provider`. ## Environment - opencode version 2: `0.0.0-next-16974` (next channel) - opencode version 1: `1.18.15` - Operating system: macOS 25.5.0 - Architecture: arm64 ## How to repeat the fault 1. Install the package `commandcode-go-opencode-provider` from npm. 2. Put configuration A in the global configuration file. 3. Run this command with version 2: `opencode models` 4. Count the lines that start with `commandcode/`. 5. Run the same command with version 1. 6. Put configuration B in the same file. 7. Do step 3 to step 5 again. Configuration A uses the version 1 fields: ```json { "provider": { "commandcode": { "npm": "commandcode-go-opencode-provider", "name": "Command Code", "env": ["COMMANDCODE_API_KEY"], "options": { "baseURL": "https://api.commandcode.ai" }, "models": { "deepseek-v4-flash": { "id": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash", "name": "DeepSeek V4 Flash", "tool_call": true } } } } } ``` Configuration B uses the version 2 fields: ```json { "providers": { "commandcode": { "package": "aisdk:commandcode-go-opencode-provider", "name": "Command Code", "settings": { "baseURL": "https://api.commandcode.ai" }, "models": { "deepseek-v4-flash": { "modelID": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash", "name": "DeepSeek V4 Flash", "capabilities": { "tools": true } } } } } } ``` ## Result Configuration A: version 2 shows 0 models for the provider. There is no error message. Version 1 shows all models. Configuration B: version 2 shows all models. Version 1 stops with the error message. I did more tests with configuration A. The result stays the same for each test: - The `package` field and the `npm` field together in the `provider` key. - Only the `package` field in the `provider` key. - Model entries with only version 1 fields. I removed `modelID`, `capabilities` and `cost.cache`. A second file does not correct the problem. Both versions read the file `opencode.jsonc`. Version 1 also stops with an error for that file. ## Expected result Version 2 must load the provider when the configuration uses the version 1 fields. Then one file can satisfy both versions. If version 2 cannot load the provider, then version 2 must show an error message.

signals.title: Windows: postinstall fails to copy binary from optionalDependency — stub remains 479 bytes
signals.text: ## Description After installing or updating `opencode-ai` via npm on Windows, the `opencode` command fails with: ``` Error al ejecutar el programa 'opencode.exe': El ejecutable especificado no es una aplicación válida para esta plataforma de sistema operativo. ``` The root cause: the `postinstall.mjs` script fails to copy the real platform-specific binary over the stub. The `bin/opencode.exe` remains a 479-byte stub instead of the ~174MB real binary. ## Environment - **OS**: Windows 10/11 x64 - **Node.js**: v22.16.0 - **npm**: global install - **opencode-ai version**: 1.18.11 (also reproducible on 1.18.15) ## Steps to Reproduce 1. `npm install -g opencode-ai` 2. `opencode --version` 3. Error: binary not valid for platform ## Diagnosis The package structure: ``` opencode-ai/ bin/opencode.exe ← 479 bytes (STUB - broken) postinstall.mjs ← should copy real binary node_modules/ opencode-windows-x64/ bin/opencode.exe ← 174MB (REAL binary) ``` The `postinstall.mjs` script: 1. Detects platform (windows) and arch (x64) 2. Checks AVX2 support 3. Should copy `opencode-windows-x64/bin/opencode.exe` to `bin/opencode.exe` 4. **Fails silently** — stub remains unchanged Running the postinstall manually works: ```bash node "C:\Users\...\npm\node_modules\opencode-ai\postinstall.mjs" # After this, bin/opencode.exe is 174MB and works ``` ## Additional Context - The real binary IS downloaded as an optionalDependency (`opencode-windows-x64`) - The `postinstall.mjs` uses `fs.linkSync` with fallback to `fs.copyFileSync` - No error is thrown — the script exits cleanly but the stub is not replaced - This happens consistently across multiple install/update cycles - Windows Defender may be blocking the binary copy operation ## Suggested Fix The `postinstall.mjs` should: 1. Verify the target binary was actually replaced (check file size or hash) 2. Throw an explicit error if the copy/link failed 3. Or: skip the stub entirely and have npm use the optionalDependency binary directly ## Workaround Run the postinstall manually after each install/update: ```bash node "$(npm root -g)/opencode-ai/postinstall.mjs" ```

signals.title: V2 AI package: audit and close critical protocol correctness gaps
signals.text: ## Summary Track correctness and parity gaps in the V2 native `@opencode-ai/ai` package by wire protocol. This is **not** a feature wishlist. It excludes citations, provider-hosted tools, and unsupported optional capabilities. Scope is critical flow integrity: normalization, ordering, streamed-state settlement, persistence/replay, request intent, terminal outcomes, transport classification, and accounting. ## Anthropic Messages (`/v1/messages`) ### P0 — tool/result integrity - [x] **Coalesce parallel tool results into the immediately following user turn.** V2 previously lowered `assistant[tool_use A, tool_use B]` into `user[result A]`, `user[result B]`. Completed in #41948. - [ ] **Settle or fail pending streamed tool calls at `message_stop`.** Native only emits a call on `content_block_stop`; terminal `message_stop` can report success while pending tool state is silently dropped. ### P0 — output and continuation integrity - [ ] **Preserve Anthropic compaction blocks and deltas.** Native accepts unknown block types structurally but silently drops compaction content from output and persisted history. - [ ] **Map compaction stop reasons and retain continuation state** rather than converting them to `unknown`. ### P1 — request normalization - [ ] **Normalize thinking budgets and answer-token semantics.** Enforce minimum budget and `budget < max_tokens`; account for thinking tokens when canonical `maxTokens` represents answer budget. - [ ] **Remove incompatible thinking/sampling combinations.** Do not forward invalid combinations of enabled thinking, `temperature`, `top_p`, and `top_k`. - [ ] **Add `anthropic-beta: mid-conversation-system-2026-04-07`** whenever native lowering emits a mid-conversation system-role message. - [ ] **Do not silently downgrade supported system updates into wrapped user text.** Capability and negotiation should be explicit. - [ ] **Never replay unsigned visible `thinking` blocks.** Replay valid signed/redacted Anthropic state or fail/lower locally. - [ ] **Trim/normalize final assistant prefill whitespace** where Anthropic requires it. - [ ] **Reject, serialize, or explicitly warn for every accepted provider option.** Open-ended options currently type-check while lowering reads only `thinking` and `effort`; parallel-tool controls and request metadata can silently vanish. ### P1 — stream and accounting integrity - [ ] **Validate lifecycle ordering:** require `message_start`, reject duplicate/out-of-order starts, reject events after terminal completion, and settle open fragments at EOF. - [ ] **Aggregate raw usage once at terminal completion**, including split start/delta counters and compaction/advisor/fallback iterations. Existing tracker: #40713. - [ ] **Retain response identity and stop diagnostics:** actual served model, response ID, initial content snapshot, stop/refusal details, and complete provider metadata. ## Bedrock Converse ### P0 — tool/result integrity - [ ] **Coalesce parallel tool results into one immediately following Bedrock user turn.** Same deterministic failure class as Anthropic Messages; existing report: #41445. - [ ] **Normalize adjacent user/tool messages generally** so synthetic, compaction, and ordinary user content cannot violate Converse role/turn requirements. ### P1 — replay safety - [ ] **Keep Bedrock/Anthropic thought and tool metadata bound to compatible route origin.** Do not replay incompatible Anthropic signatures or foreign protocol state after model/provider switches. Related: #34996 and #35827. ## OpenAI Chat Completions (`/v1/chat/completions`) ### P0 — output integrity - [ ] **Preserve streamed `delta.refusal`.** Native accepts the field structurally but ignores it, allowing a refusal to become an empty successful response and disappear from persisted history. ### P0 — tool integrity - [ ] **Classify and retain truncated tool arguments correctly.** Distinguish provider truncation, transport interruption, and adapter premature finalization; never execute malformed input; add bounded safe recovery. Existing report: #36766. ### P1 — stream integrity - [ ] **Require valid terminal lifecycle state** rather than treating partial content/tool buffers as clean completion. ## OpenAI Responses (`/v1/responses`) ### P0 — tool integrity - [ ] **Finalize or fail pending function calls when `response.completed` arrives without `response.output_item.done`.** Current behavior can leave a tool permanently pending. Existing deterministic report: #37159. - [ ] **Retain terminal provider diagnostics for truncated argument buffers**, including whether the stream ended normally, finish state, and bounded byte counts. Related: #36766. ### P0 — output integrity - [ ] **Preserve `response.refusal.delta` and `response.refusal.done`.** Native ignores them, yields an empty successful response, and cannot replay the refusal. - [ ] **Do not mark reasoning-only output with no text/refusal/tool call as successful.** Existing production report: #37372. ### P1 — reasoning lifecycle - [ ] **Normalize overlapping reasoning fragments** instead of crashing the execution as `unknown`. Existing report: #36892. - [ ] **Finalize or explicitly interrupt every open reasoning/text fragment before response completion.** ## Gemini `generateContent` ### P0 — function-call integrity - [ ] **Support official incremental function arguments (`partialArgs` / `willContinue`).** Native currently requires complete `name + args` in each frame, so valid Gemini streams fail schema decoding before accumulation. - [x] **Normalize omitted zero-argument call input to `{}`.** A valid `functionCall: { name: "ping" }` currently fails decoding. Completed in #43111. ### P0 — safety outcome integrity - [x] **Preserve prompt-level safety blocks (`promptFeedback.blockReason`) as a typed terminal outcome.** Candidate-less blocked prompts currently lose the safety reason and become generic incomplete-stream failures. Completed in #43070. ## Shared V2 runner/history layer ### P0 — successful execution contract - [ ] **A successful execution must contain usable text, a refusal, or completed tool work.** Token usage or a provider `stop` alone is insufficient. Existing report: #37372. - [ ] **Every announced local tool call must settle exactly once before its owning step terminates.** ### P1 — persistence and replay - [ ] **Bind opaque provider metadata to resolved protocol origin**, not only the configured provider/model reference. Existing trackers: #34996 and #35827. - [ ] **Distinguish normally ended fragments from cleanup-interrupted text, reasoning, and tool input.** Existing tracker: #36874. - [ ] **Do not persist interrupted raw tool input as an executable call.** ### P1 — request intent - [ ] **Keep variants effective after native package overrides.** Confirmed end-to-end: `#low`, `#high`, and `#max` for `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash` through native Anthropic produced identical request bodies with no effort/thinking field. - [ ] **Every accepted request option must be serialized, explicitly ignored with a warning, or rejected locally.** ### P1 — transport and error classification - [ ] **Classify response-body resets as transport failures, not invalid model output**, and retain a sanitized low-level cause. Existing report: #39326. - [ ] **Before output starts, preserve bounded transport retry behavior.** After output/tool side effects begin, expose an explicit interrupted-step recovery path rather than silently retrying. - [ ] **Keep child-session stream failures visible to the parent** so dropped subagent work can be restarted. ## Protocol conformance matrix Add fixtures and differential tests for every native protocol covering: 1. Single, sequential, and parallel tool calls. 2. Adjacent user/tool/synthetic/system messages. 3. Missing, duplicate, reordered, and truncated stream boundaries. 4. Pending tools/fragments at every terminal event. 5. Text, refusal, safety block, content filter, empty response, and normal stop outcomes. 6. Same-origin replay and incompatible provider/model/protocol switching. 7. Request options and model variants at the actual wire body/header boundary. 8. Split streaming usage, cache counters, executor iterations, and fallback accounting. 9. Transport reset before output, during reasoning/text, during tool input, and after tool execution. ## Suggested implementation order 1. Anthropic Messages and Bedrock parallel-result normalization. 2. Pending tool settlement across Anthropic, Responses, Chat, and Gemini. 3. Refusal, safety, and empty-success outcome invariants. 4. Replay provenance and interrupted-fragment semantics. 5. Request option/variant normalization. 6. Transport classification and usage aggregation.

signals.title: ACP session/load response omits sessionId — breaks resume for Agent of Empires and any spec-compliant ACP client
signals.text: ## Bug The ACP `session/load` handler in `packages/opencode/src/acp/service.ts` (line ~211, `loadSession`) returns `{ configOptions }` but **omits `sessionId`** from the response. The ACP spec requires `sessionId` in the `session/load` result (the `newSession` handler correctly returns `{ sessionId, configOptions }`). ## Impact Agent of Empires (aoe) v1.13.1+ sends a spec-compliant `session/load { sessionId, cwd, mcpServers }` request, receives a response with no `sessionId`, and rejects it: `session/load response missing sessionId`. It then silently falls back to `session/new`, so **every worker restart forks a fresh session and loses the transcript context** — the dashboard shows "Agent finished but didn't notify the daemon; restarting worker" and the old conversation never resumes. ## Repro (raw ACP probe) ```js // opencode acp --cwd <dir>; send initialize, then: session/load { sessionId: "ses_...", cwd: "/path", mcpServers: [] } // → 200 result: { "configOptions": [...] } ← sessionId missing ``` Verified against opencode 1.18.18 and current `dev`. ## Fix In `loadSession`, return `sessionId` alongside `configOptions`: ```ts return { sessionId: state.id, configOptions: configOptions(...), } ``` (`state.id === params.sessionId` — the response just needs to echo it back per spec.)

signals.title: Compaction request exceeds context window on high-output models (v2)
signals.text: ### Description A V2 session using a custom OpenAI-compatible model reached about 236k of its 299,964-token context window (79%). Automatic compaction did not run, and `/compact` failed because the provider reported that the prompt plus requested output exceeded the context limit. The model advertises a 131,072-token output limit. `SessionCompaction.required()` caps its reserved output budget at 32,000, but the compaction `LLM.request()` does not set `generation.maxTokens`. OpenAI-compatible lowering therefore leaves `max_tokens` unset, allowing the provider to use 131,072 instead. Expected: the compaction request should use the same bounded output budget used to calculate the automatic-compaction threshold. Before `/compact`, the model also returned `finish=stop` with no text or tool calls several times, leaving the TUI with no visible response. This may be a separate empty-response issue. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version 0.0.0-next-17403 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Configure a custom OpenAI-compatible model with context limit 299964 and output limit 131072. 2. Grow a V2 session to approximately 236k tokens, displayed as 79% context usage. 3. Observe that automatic compaction does not run. 4. Run `/compact`. 5. Observe that the provider rejects the request because the prompt plus requested output exceeds the context window. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signals.title: Legacy plugin loader pushes non-Hooks return values, corrupting plugin loading and crashing startup
signals.text: ## Summary opencode 1.16.2's legacy plugin loader (`getLegacyPlugins` in `packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts`) invokes EVERY exported function of a plugin module as a plugin and pushes its return value into the hooks array WITHOUT validating it is a Hooks object. A plugin that exports helper functions that return `undefined`/`false` (in addition to the real plugin factory) pollutes the hooks array with non-Hooks entries. This corrupts plugin loading and can crash startup without a visible load error. The same root cause explains two crash signatures observed at startup: - config-hook loop: `(hook as any).config?.(cfg)` throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'config')` (looped under `Effect.ignore`, so non-fatal but logged). - provider state initializer (`packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts`, `instanceState.make` does `for (const hook of plugins) { const p = hook.provider; ... }`): `undefined.provider` throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'provider')`. This loop is NOT wrapped in `Effect.ignore`, so it aborts provider state init and crashes `Provider.list`. ## Context Custom plugins written as `{ id: <plugin>, ...hooks }` legacy-style modules, or plugin modules (built with the `@opencode-ai/plugin` SDK) that chose named exports: the plugin factory plus adjacent helper functions. Example: a plugin module exporting `isLockdownError`, `handleRateLimit`, `timerTick`, and `<Plugin>` as four named function exports. The legacy loader treats all four as plugin factories. ## Root cause detail 1. `readV1Plugin(mod, "detect")` returns `undefined` when `mod.default` is absent or is a function (only a record with `id`/`server`/`tui` keys routes to the v1 path). So any module without a record `default` falls through to the legacy path. 2. `getLegacyPlugins(mod)` iterates `Object.values(mod)` and calls `getServerPlugin(entry)` (which only checks `typeof value === "function"`). Every function export is treated as a plugin. 3. `applyPlugin` does `hooks.push(await entry(input, load.options))` with no check that the returned value is a Hooks object. Helper functions that return `undefined` or `false` get pushed into the shared hooks array. 4. Later consumers index the array as if every entry were a Hooks object. The fatal one is `instanceState.make`: `const p = hook.provider` on an `undefined` entry throws. ## Expected behavior A plugin that returns a non-Hooks value from its module export should fail that plugin load gracefully and log a clear error, rather than polluting the hooks array and crashing a later consumer. At minimum, `getLegacyPlugins` / `applyPlugin` should filter out entries whose value is not a Hooks object. ## Impact - Crash #1 (load list: magic-context, instant-file-search, mullvad, server-start-guard, bmc-panel, speak, gk-hooks): 2x `j.config` + `t.provider` crash. - Crash #2 (same minus bmc-panel and server-start-guard): identical 2x `j.config` + `t.provider` crash. - Clean boot (crashing plugin removed): zero errors. The single discriminating variable between the crashing boots and the clean boot was the plugin with the helper exports returning `undefined`. ## Environment - opencode 1.16.2 (WinGet install) - @opencode-ai/plugin SDK 1.17.8 - Loader ref: tag v1.16.2 = commit 76c631d198f9ff620e15468e45f3457d50481b57

signals.title: Bug Report: 5‑hour rolling quota incorrectly hits 100% while actual USD spend is far below limit
signals.text: ### Description （ I’m experiencing abnormal quota‑counting behavior with the OpenCode‑Go subscription plan. According to my usage chart, my total real‑world spending for the day was under **5 USD**. My weekly quota sits at 45% and monthly quota at 22%, both well below their hard limits. However, the **5‑hour rolling quota hit 100% and blocked further API calls**. The dashboard showed a full reset would take another 1 hour and 14 minutes. Per official documentation, OpenCode‑Go applies these limits measured in USD value within sliding time windows: - 5‑hour rolling limit: 12 USD - Weekly limit: 30 USD - Monthly limit: 60 USD There are two clear contradictions between documented rules and observed behaviour: 1. **Broken 5‑hour rolling‑window calculation** Total daily spend was less than 5 USD, far under the 12 USD 5‑hour cap, yet the rolling‑usage counter maxed out at 100% and triggered rate‑limiting. The counter also did **not behave as a sliding window**: old usage was not gradually released as time passed. Instead the quota stayed fully locked until the full waiting period completed. 2. **Mismatched quota metrics across different time ranges** - Weekly usage: 45% (not exhausted) - Monthly usage: 22% (not exhausted) - 5‑hour rolling usage: 100% (hard‑blocked) Weekly and monthly percentage values align reasonably with real dollar spend. Only the 5‑hour rolling counter hits the ceiling prematurely. This strongly suggests the 5‑hour rolling counter is tracking raw token / request throughput internally, **not USD‑denominated consumption as stated in the documentation**. ## To Reproduce 1. Activate an OpenCode‑Go subscription 2. Run long‑running Agent / MCP workflows with heavy tool calls and large output token volume; mix multiple backend models (`deepseek‑v4‑flash(go)`, `deepseek‑v4‑pro(go)`, `kimi‑k3(go)` etc.) 3. Keep actual total daily monetary consumption below 5 USD ## Expected behavior 1. The 5‑hour rolling quota should calculate real USD‑equivalent consumption within the sliding 5‑hour time window. 2. Rate‑limiting should **not trigger at 100%** when spend remains well under the 12 USD threshold. 3. The rolling window should operate in true sliding fashion: old usage decays over time and frees up quota incrementally, instead of locking completely until full reset. ## Actual behavior - Total real‑world daily spend <5 USD, but 5‑hour rolling usage hits 100% and blocks API requests. - Weekly and monthly quota percentages remain normal and unexhausted. - The rolling‑usage progress bar stays locked; quota only becomes available again after waiting for the full remaining reset time, without gradual decay. ## Additional context - Subscription type: OpenCode‑Go paid subscription - Models involved: `deepseek‑v4‑flash(go)`, `deepseek‑v4‑pro(go)`, `kimi‑k2.6(go)`, `kimi‑k3(go)`, `minimax‑m3(go)`, `qwen3.7‑plus(go)` - Screenshots attached: daily cost bar chart, 5‑hour rolling‑usage full‑cap screen, weekly/monthly usage panel - Documentation reference: [[https://opencode.ai/docs/zh](https://link.wtturl.cn/?target=https%3A%2F%2Fopencode.ai%2Fdocs%2Fzh&scene=im&aid=582478&lang=zh)](https://link.wtturl.cn/?target=https%3A%2F%2Fopencode.ai%2Fdocs%2Fzh&scene=im&aid=582478&lang=zh)‑cn/go/ This issue heavily breaks MCP / long‑agent use‑cases. Workflows with low real monetary cost get unexpectedly terminated by the 5‑hour rolling limiter, which conflicts with the advertised quota‑billing logic. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signals.title: OpenAI WebSocket 1009 retries the same oversized response.create five times before HTTP fallback
signals.text: ### Description With the OpenAI Responses WebSocket enabled, an oversized request containing base64 image tool outputs is deterministically rejected with: ``` ProviderResponseStreamError: WebSocket closed before response.completed (code 1009: message too big) ``` OpenCode retries the same oversized WebSocket request five times with backoff before falling back to HTTP. The session therefore appears stuck for about a minute and repeats a request that cannot succeed over that transport. Cancelling or restarting before fallback starts the cycle again. The session eventually recovered over HTTP and then compacted, so this report is about delayed recovery and unnecessary retries, not permanent data loss. In the observed session, one tool round read six 1920x1080 PNG files. Their base64 data URLs totaled 17,390,364 bytes. Including an image from the immediately preceding round, the request history contained 19,895,594 bytes of image data before JSON overhead. The next model request produced five consecutive code 1009 failures. In v1.18.18, the complete `response.create` payload is sent as one WebSocket message: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.18.18/packages/opencode/src/plugin/openai/ws.ts#L289-L295 Code 1009 is currently only annotated as `message too big`: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.18.18/packages/opencode/src/plugin/openai/ws.ts#L350-L354 Expected behavior: code 1009 should immediately bypass WebSocket and retry once over HTTP, or OpenCode should preflight the serialized payload size and use HTTP for oversized requests. It should not replay the same known-too-large WebSocket message five times. Related issues: - https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/14562 covers the same base64-image root cause through HTTP 413 and compaction, but not WebSocket code 1009 or delayed HTTP fallback. - https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/29646 covers generic early WebSocket disconnects (for example transient code 1006). Code 1009 is deterministic and should trigger immediate transport fallback. ### Plugins `telegram-notify.js` (not involved in request construction) ### OpenCode version 1.18.18 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start OpenCode with `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_WEBSOCKETS=true`. 2. Use the OpenAI provider with `gpt-5.6-sol`. 3. In one tool round, read enough PNG images for the base64 tool-result attachments to exceed the WebSocket message-size limit (six 1920x1080 PNGs totaling about 17.4 MB reproduced it here). 4. Continue the turn so OpenCode sends the next `response.create`. 5. Observe five consecutive code 1009 errors before HTTP fallback succeeds. ### Screenshot and/or share link No public share link. The raw error and measured payload sizes are included above. ### Operating System Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 host; Ubuntu 24.04 on WSL2 (kernel 6.18.33.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2) ### Terminal PowerShell 7 launcher; headless `opencode serve` running in WSL2

signals.title: Message IDs wrap around, silently dropping new user input in sessions with history
signals.text: ### Description In a session with existing message history, a new user message can be silently ignored — the agent loop exits without processing it. Root cause: Identifier.ascending() IDs are NOT monotonic. packages/opencode/src/id/id.ts encodes `Date.now()*0x1000 + counter` into a 6-byte (48-bit) field: let now = BigInt(currentTimestamp) * BigInt(0x1000) + BigInt(counter) const timeBytes = Buffer.alloc(6) // only 48 bits `Date.now()*0x1000` (~7.2e15 in 2026) exceeds 2^48 (~2.8e14) by ~25x, so the high bits are truncated. A freshly generated "msg_000..." sorts before older IDs. MessageV2.latest() picks the latest message by `info.id > user.id` (string compare), assuming IDs are monotonic (its comment says so). After wraparound it returns a stale message; the run loop then sees `lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id` and exits, dropping the new input. Suggested fix: compare by `info.time.created` (a real ms timestamp) with id as tiebreaker, matching the existing `(desc time_created, desc id)` pagination ordering. ### Plugins N/A (default config) ### OpenCode version v1.18.15 (also confirmed on dev @ 5d0f866) ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start a session and exchange a few messages (build up message history). 2. Wait until the 48-bit timestamp field wraps — current date (2026) is already in the wrap window, since Date.now()*0x1000 overflows 2^48. 3. Send a new user message in the SAME session. 4. Observe: the agent does not respond. The run loop logs "exiting loop" and the new input is never sent to the model. Reproduction is time-dependent (tied to the wraparound point of the 48-bit timestamp), so it is intermittent rather than on every message. A reliable way to reproduce without waiting: unit-test latest() with messages whose time.created increases but whose ids wrap (a fresh "msg_000..." after older "msg_0a8a..."). ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Linux ### Terminal _No response_

Adding this mid-sized model will give users a high-performing, cost-efficient option for everyday coding tasks, local-agent parity, and fast multi-file refactoring within the OpenCode ecosystem. Proposed Solution Integrate Qwen3.8-27B into the OpenCode Go managed model catalog. Expose the endpoint under the explicit runtime reference (e.g., opencode-go/qwen3.8-27b). Provide standard OpenAI/Anthropic API compatibility for seamless integration with the OpenCode CLI, IDE extensions, and third-party coding agents. Key Reasons & Benefits - Optimal Sweet Spot for Speed & Accuracy At 27 billion parameters, Qwen3.8-27B strikes an ideal balance between low latency and strong reasoning/code-generation capabilities. It outperforms smaller 7B/14B models on complex coding benchmarks while remaining significantly faster and cheaper to serve than dense 70B+ models. - Strong Agentic & Multi-File Capabilities The Qwen series is natively tuned for tool calling, precise repository context understanding, and file editing. Adding Qwen3.8-27B directly enhances OpenCode's agentic workflows (e.g., automated refactoring, test generation, and terminal command execution). - Diversity in Open-Source Model Options Users who prefer the Qwen architecture for specific languages, long context retention, or regional strengths currently lack a mid-weight Qwen option in OpenCode Go. Adding Qwen3.8-27B fills a key gap between ultra-light models and massive, heavy-tier models.

signals.title: Message ID counter overflow (wrap-around) breaks session loop — new messages silently ignored in older sessions
signals.text: ### Description ### Summary The message ID counter (12-hex-digit component after the `msg_` prefix) wrapped around from `fffb` back to `0035` on Aug 15, 2026 (after ~2 months of use). Because the session loop and `MessageV2.latest()` determine "newest message" via **lexicographic string comparison of message IDs** (not by timestamp), every message created after the wrap-around is considered *older* than all pre-wrap messages. As a result, **any user message sent in a pre-existing session is silently ignored**: the agent loop exits at `step=0` without ever calling the model. Newly created sessions work fine (their IDs are internally consistent), which makes the bug confusing to diagnose. ### Environment - OS: Windows 10 (also likely platform-independent) - opencode desktop app (`@opencode-aidesktop`), version: `[fill in your exact version from the app]` - Data migrated from JSON storage to SQLite (`opencode.db`) on Jun 16, 2026 - Provider/model: `[e.g. zhipuai / glm-5.2]` (irrelevant to the bug) ### Steps to reproduce 1. Use opencode daily for ~2 months (until the message ID counter passes `ffff` and wraps to `0000`). - Faster repro on a scratch install: manually insert messages with IDs near `msg_ffff...` and then send a new message. 2. Open a session created **before** the counter wrapped around. 3. Send any message (e.g. `hello`). ### Actual behavior - The user message is persisted (present in the `message` table with its parts), but no assistant response is ever generated. - Log shows the loop exiting immediately without any LLM call: ``` level=INFO message=loop session.id=ses_XXXX step=0 level=INFO message="exiting loop" session.id=ses_XXXX ← ~10ms later ``` - Affects **all sessions that contain pre-wrap messages**. Restarting the app does not help. - Sessions created entirely after the wrap-around behave normally. ### Expected behavior Sending a message in any session should always trigger a model response, regardless of ID ordering. Message recency should be determined by creation time, not by string comparison of IDs. ### Root cause analysis 1. Exit condition in `SessionPrompt.run` (found in `app.asar`, `node-*.js` chunk): ```js if (lastAssistant2?.finish && !["tool-calls"].includes(lastAssistant2.finish) && !hasToolCalls3 && lastUser.id < lastAssistant2.id) { // string comparison! yield* exports_Effect.logInfo("exiting loop", { "session.id": sessionID }); break; } ``` 2. `MessageV2.latest()` also selects the latest user/assistant message by ID comparison: ```js if (info32.role === "user" && (!user || info32.id > user.id)) user = info32; if (info32.role === "assistant" && (!assistant2 || info32.id > assistant2.id)) assistant2 = info32; ``` 3. Message IDs look like `msg_<12-hex-counter><random-suffix>`. Evidence from my database (first 2-4 hex of counter vs. creation time): | Period | ID prefix (hex) | Notes | |---|---|---| | Jun 16, 2026 (first message) | `ed01` | counter start after migration | | Aug 14, 2026 (evening) | `ffed` … `fffb` | approaching top | | Aug 15, 2026 (morning) | `0035` | **wrapped around** | | Aug 15, 2026 (afternoon) | `0043` | continues | After the wrap, for any old session: `lastUser.id` (e.g. `msg_0043...`) `<` `lastAssistant2.id` (e.g. `msg_fffb...`) is always true, so the loop treats the new user message as already answered and exits. ### Suggested fix - Compare by `time_created` (with the existing same-millisecond `id` tiebreaker, e.g. the `older()` helper already used for cursor pagination), instead of raw string ID comparison in `latest()` and the loop-exit condition. - And/or generate message IDs with a monotonically increasing counter that cannot wrap (e.g. wider counter, or a per-database sequence table). ### Workaround (already applied locally) I hot-fixed my database by remapping all 2610 pre-wrap message IDs into the `00000001xxxx` low range (preserving order and random suffixes), cascading updates to `part.message_id` (10,704 rows), `message.data.parentID` (2,197), and in-JSON references (21). All affected sessions recovered immediately. Happy to share the Node script if useful for other affected users. ### Additional context - The same wrap-around will recur roughly every 2 months of active use until fixed upstream. - Event-table history references were intentionally left untouched (do not affect the loop), so event replay may still show old IDs. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version v1.17.9 ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signals.title: Resuming an old session exits silently (no API call, no error) — even with a valid --model override; stale recorded model also breaks resume
signals.text: ## Description Old sessions can no longer be continued after restarting opencode. Two layers of failure: 1. **Stale model reference**: Sessions last used with a model that the provider has since removed (`zai-coding-plan/glm-5.1`) fail to resume with `ProviderModelNotFoundError` (only visible in logs). 2. **Silent exit even with a valid model override**: Even when passing `--model zai-coding-plan/glm-5.2`, resuming an old session exits the session loop immediately (~20ms, `step=0` → `exiting loop`) with **no API call, no error output, and exit code 0**. The user message is persisted, but no assistant reply is ever produced. Freshly-created sessions resume fine, so this is specific to replaying sessions created by an older version. ## Environment - opencode: 1.17.13 (Linux x64) - Session originally created with: 1.16.2 - Provider: `zai-coding-plan` (glm-5.1 recorded in session; glm-5.1 since removed from provider's model list — glm-4.7 / glm-5-turbo / glm-5.2 remain) ## Reproduction ```console $ opencode run --session <old-session-id> --model zai-coding-plan/glm-5.2 "Reply with exactly: OK" --format json # (no output at all, exit code 0) $ opencode run --session <old-session-id> --model zai-coding-plan/glm-5.2 "Reply with exactly: OK" --print-logs --log-level DEBUG 2>&1 | tail -3 timestamp=2026-08-15T14:13:45.216Z level=INFO run=2b186860 message=loop session.id=ses_161a26406ffe... step=0 timestamp=2026-08-15T14:13:45.233Z level=INFO run=2b186860 message="exiting loop" session.id=ses_161a26406ffe... timestamp=2026-08-15T14:13:45.239Z level=INFO run=2b186860 message="disposing instance" directory=/home/irlovan/AOC/Test ``` Without the model override, the log additionally shows: ``` level=ERROR message="share subscriber failed" type=message.updated cause="Cause([Fail(ProviderModelNotFoundError: Model not found: zai-coding-plan/glm-5.1. Did you mean: glm-4.7, glm-5-turbo, glm-5.2?)])" ``` ### What I verified while debugging - Resuming a **brand-new** session (created and resumed with the same 1.17.13 binary) works fine → not an environment/auth issue. - I patched all 412 stale `"modelID":"glm-5.1"` references in `message.data` to `glm-5.2` and updated `session.model` in the DB — resume **still** exits silently. So the stale model is not the only cause; old-session replay itself is broken. - Session data is structurally intact: no orphan parts, no malformed JSON, all tool parts have valid states, `time_compacting` is NULL. - `OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOCOMPACT=1` makes no difference. - `--fork` works and preserves full conversation context. ## Expected behavior - Resume should either work, or surface the error (e.g. "model no longer available — pick another") instead of exiting silently with code 0. - A `--model` override on `run`/`tui` should take precedence over the model recorded in old messages. ## Workaround Fork the session (copies history into a new session that resumes fine): ```console $ opencode --session <old-session-id> --fork ``` ## Related - #33043 / #31141 mention `ProviderModelNotFoundError` for subagents with `model=undefined` — possibly the same class of stale/missing model resolution, but this report is about top-level session resume.
signals.author: irlovanwon

signals.title: Ascending ID space wrapped on 2026-08-14: sessions created before that instant silently stop accepting new messages
signals.text: ## Summary `Identifier.create()` truncates the encoded timestamp to 6 bytes, so the ascending ID space wraps every ~795 days. **It wrapped on `2026-08-14T11:19:55.136Z`.** Since then, every freshly minted message ID sorts *lexicographically before* every ID written prior to that instant. Because the session engine resolves "newest" by lexicographic ID ordering, any session whose messages predate the wrap silently stops accepting new input: prompts and `/compact` are persisted but never served, and the agent appears to do nothing at all. ## Root cause `packages/opencode/src/id/id.ts`: ```js let now = BigInt(currentTimestamp) * BigInt(0x1000) + BigInt(counter) now = direction === "descending" ? ~now : now const timeBytes = Buffer.alloc(6) // <-- 48 bits only for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) { timeBytes[i] = Number((now >> BigInt(40 - 8 * i)) & BigInt(0xff)) } ``` `timestamp * 0x1000` needs 53 bits today but only the low 48 are kept, so the value wraps every `2^36` ms = 68 719 476 736 ms ≈ **795.4 days**. ``` last wrap : 2026-08-14T11:19:55.136Z next wrap : 2028-10-17T20:04:31.872Z id minted 1 min before wrap : msg_fffff15a0001… id minted 1 min after wrap : msg_00000ea60001… "msg_00000ea60001…" < "msg_fffff15a0001…" // ordering inverted ``` ## Observed impact Real IDs from an affected session (144k messages, session spans the wrap): ``` last message before wrap : msg_ffff07b29001lvZ1aOBcxm1fBY 2026-08-14T11:02:58Z first message after wrap : msg_00003f7d6001SjWSlWsUjBmLWQ 2026-08-14T11:24:15Z ``` Consequences in that session, reproduced against the real data: - `MessageV2.filterCompacted` walks the stream in descending-ID order and stops at the retained compaction tail, so post-wrap messages are **never reached** — 92 of 561 messages walked, and the three newest (two `/compact` markers and a user prompt) are absent from the returned view. - `MessageV2.latest()` therefore reports an old, already-closed turn as the most recent one, the loop exits on its break invariant without issuing a request, and the user sees **no reaction at all** — no error, no assistant message. - The same applies to any code deriving recency from IDs (queued-prompt lookup, run anchoring). The relevant code even documents the assumption being violated: ``` // Derive each binding by max id (MessageID is monotonic via MessageID.ascending) ``` ## Reproduction 1. Use any session containing messages created before `2026-08-14T11:19:55Z`. 2. Send a prompt, or run `/compact`. 3. The message is persisted, but no assistant turn ever starts. Sessions created *after* the wrap behave normally — until the next wrap in October 2028. ## Scope Anyone who resumes a pre-wrap session is affected, on every install, regardless of version: the trigger is wall-clock time, not code. In the store I inspected, 2 281 of 2 310 sessions predate the wrap. ## Suggested fixes 1. **Widen the encoded field** so the timestamp is not truncated (breaks ID comparability with existing IDs, but stops future wraps). 2. **Mint monotonically per scope**: when generating an ID, if it does not sort after the highest existing ID of that session, mint past that high-water mark. This repairs pre-wrap sessions without changing the ID format: ```js export function monotonic(generated: string, highest: string | undefined): string { if (highest === undefined || generated > highest) return generated const start = highest.indexOf("_") + 1 const bumped = (BigInt("0x" + highest.slice(start, start + 12)) + 1n).toString(16).padStart(12, "0") if (bumped.length > 12) return generated return highest.slice(0, start) + bumped + generated.slice(generated.indexOf("_") + 13) } ``` 3. **Stop deriving recency from ID ordering** and use `time_created` (already stored and correct) — the most robust fix, but the widest change. Happy to open a PR for whichever direction you prefer.
