signals.title: fix(core): preserve previous V2 database lineage
signals.text: ## What Preserves databases created by the completed pre-split OpenCode V2 migration lineage when they start current V2. The August 5 V1/V2 database split replaced the old July V2 migration registry with a generated squash migration. A database that had already completed the removed V2 lineage therefore replayed the squash and failed on its existing `event.created` column. ## Before / After **Before:** A previous-V2 database contains `20260730195856_optional_session_title`, `session`, canonical `session_message` history, durable events, and an existing `event.created` column. Current V2 sees the new squash migration as pending, attempts `ALTER TABLE event ADD created`, and exits with `SQLiteError: duplicate column name: created`. **After:** The squash recognizes the terminal previous-V2 marker, preserves the canonical V2 tables in place, renames `session` to `session_v2`, retargets SQLite foreign keys, and recreates the renamed session indexes. Durable messages, pending input, events, and sequence watermarks remain unchanged before later current-V2 migrations run. Databases containing V1-only history fail transactionally with an explicit error rather than silently making that history undiscoverable. ## How - `packages/core/src/database/migration/20260804233008_loose_psylocke.ts` - Detects the terminal pre-split V2 migration marker. - Rejects unsupported mixed lineage with V1-only sessions before mutation. - Drops the legacy qualified partial index before SQLite renames the table. - Renames `session` to `session_v2`, recreates current index names, and removes obsolete transient tables. - `packages/core/test/database-migration.test.ts` - Verifies session, message, pending-input, event, and sequence preservation through the complete post-squash migration chain. - Verifies child foreign keys target `session_v2` after rename. - Verifies mixed lineage fails without changing the schema or migration journal. ## Scope - Does not change fresh database bootstrap or the ordinary V1-to-V2 importer. - Does not attempt to merge V1-only history with a completed previous-V2 database. - Does not alter event payloads or sequence numbers. ## Testing - `bun run test database-migration.test.ts`: 13 passed - `bun run test v1-migration.test.ts`: 23 passed - `bun run test` in `packages/core`: 1,836 passed, 16 skipped - `bun run typecheck` in `packages/core` - Pre-push workspace typecheck: 33 tasks passed - Exact-lineage check: bootstrapped a database with deployed revision `9437ad8c54c6a3f094501cf391e5434de87a39ba`, then applied this branch's full migration registry successfully - Repository lint retains one unrelated pre-existing Session UI octal-escape error; changed files pass Prettier and typecheck ## Flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Pending V2 squash migration] --> B{Terminal previous-V2 marker?} B -- No --> C[Run ordinary V1 squash] B -- Yes --> D{V1-only session history?} D -- Yes --> E[Fail transactionally] D -- No --> F[Drop legacy session indexes] F --> G[Rename session to session_v2] G --> H[Recreate current indexes] H --> I[Apply later current-V2 migrations] ```

signals.title: fix(session): guard cost calc against non-numeric provider usage/cost fields
signals.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #43098 (#6010 reported the same error string and is closed; the crash still reproduces on `dev` through the `model.cost` operands — repro in the tests below.) ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? `Session.getUsage` computes per-turn cost by feeding provider-supplied values straight into `decimal.js`: ```ts .add(new Decimal(tokens.input).mul(costInfo?.input ?? 0).div(1_000_000)) ``` `costInfo` comes from `model.cost` (models.dev / provider config). Those fields are declared `Schema.Finite` in `provider/provider.ts`, but the raw payload is never decoded against that schema before use, and `?? 0` only guards `null`/`undefined`. So if `cost.input`, `cost.output`, `cost.cache.read` or `cost.cache.write` — or the same fields inside `cost.tiers[]` / `cost.experimentalOver200K` — is an object or otherwise non-numeric at runtime, `.mul()` throws: ``` [DecimalError] Invalid argument: [object Object] ``` The cost block runs while the turn is being finalized, so the throw takes the turn with it: - CLI: cosmetic — the answer is already printed and the error just follows it. - `opencode acp`: fatal — a tool-using turn aborts mid-flight, which breaks any ACP client (Zed, or automation driving `opencode acp`). Reported against the `zai-coding-plan` provider (GLM models). Two things worth stating plainly about that attribution, since they cut both ways: - **The cost block is the only place this error can come from.** `decimal.js` is imported exactly once in the package — `session/session.ts` — and every `new Decimal(...)` call sits inside `getUsage`. Since the `tokens.*` operands already pass through `safe()`, the only value that can reach `decimal.js` unchecked is `costInfo`, i.e. `model.cost`. So a `[DecimalError]` logged under `service=session.prompt` is necessarily this expression. - **The published catalog is not the culprit today.** I scanned the cached models.dev payload — 18,719 cost fields across every provider, including `zai-coding-plan/glm-5.3`, whose cost is a well-formed all-zero block — and found no non-numeric value. So the malformed payload reaches `cost()` from a local/plugin provider config or an older catalog, not from models.dev as published. That is precisely why the guard belongs at the consumer: `cost()` copies whatever it is handed. The fix adds a `num()` helper next to the existing `safe()` and wraps the cost operands fed to `decimal.js`, defaulting non-numbers to 0. Cost degrades to a correct partial value — the well-formed fields still bill — instead of throwing. Providers with well-formed pricing are unaffected: numbers in, same cost out. The other commits close the same hole one expression higher up. Tier selection reads `item.tier.type` / `item.tier.size` unguarded, and `cost()` in `provider/provider.ts` copies `tier: item.tier` straight from the models.dev / plugin payload with no `?? 0` of its own — unlike `input`/`output`/`cache`. So the same unvalidated source aborts the turn through three more shapes, each verified by probe before fixing: | `cost.tiers` payload | before | | --- | --- | | `[{ input, output, cache }]` (no `tier` key) | `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'item.tier.type')` | | `[null]` | `TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 'item.tier')` | | `{}` (not an array) | throws on `.filter` | Malformed tiers are now dropped instead of trusted, at the level of the payload as well as the field. Two notes on the shape of that guard: - a non-numeric `size` must **not** be coerced to 0 — that would make the tier match every context instead of none — so the filter uses a `finite()` predicate rather than the `num()` coercion; - the `.sort()` is deliberately left unguarded: everything reaching it has already been filtered to a finite `size`. On scope: the guard is only on the cost operands. The `tokens.*` values already go through `safe()` a few lines above, so they provably cannot be non-numeric there, and the Copilot `totalNanoAiu` branch is already narrowed to a finite non-negative number — both are left untouched. `num()` also keeps pricing **numeric strings**. `?? 0` handed the raw value to `decimal.js`, which parses `"3"` fine, so a number-only guard would have turned a working (if off-contract) cost into a silent 0 — trading a crash for under-reported billing. Checked against decimal.js 10.5.0, every string it could parse computes the same cost with and without this PR: | `cost.input` | before | after | | --- | --- | --- | | `"3"`, `"1e3"`, `"0x10"` | priced | priced, identical | | `"NaN"`, `"Infinity"` | 0 (via the outer `safe()`) | 0 | | `"abc"`, `" 3.5 "` | **threw** | 0 / 3.5 | So the only inputs whose behaviour changes are the ones that used to abort the turn. ### How did you verify your code works? Six unit tests added to the existing `describe("SessionNs.getUsage")` block in `packages/opencode/test/session/compaction.test.ts`. Each one was written first and confirmed failing on `dev` before the fix. The two malformed-cost tests fail with exactly the reported error: ``` [DecimalError] Invalid argument: [object Object] at getUsage (packages/opencode/src/session/session.ts:398:51) ``` and pass with the fix. The two malformed-tiers tests fail with the `TypeError`s in the table above. The last two are regression guards: an all-numeric cost and an all-numeric-string cost both still compute to `4.185`. - `bun test --timeout 30000 test/session/compaction.test.ts test/server/negative-tokens-regression.test.ts` → 61 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail - `bun test --timeout 60000 test/session/llm.test.ts` → 28 pass, 0 fail - `bun run typecheck` in `packages/opencode` → clean - `bun run lint` → no new errors (the one error present is pre-existing on `dev`, an unrelated octal literal) The originally reported reproduction was `opencode run "hi" -m zai-coding-plan/glm-5.3`, or any tool-using prompt under `opencode acp`. Don't expect that to reproduce against today's catalog — as noted above, that model's published cost is well-formed now, so the malformed payload came from a local provider config, a plugin, or an older catalog. The deterministic reproduction is the unit tests: they fail on `dev` and pass here. ### Screenshots / recordings N/A — not a UI change. ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

signals.title: fix(core): fall back on oversized websocket requests
signals.text: ## Summary - detect WebSocket close code 1009 as a transport size failure - retry the rejected request immediately over HTTP and keep the session on HTTP - preserve the existing retry budget for transient WebSocket closes Fixes #42572 ## Reproduction Requires `ffmpeg` and OpenAI authentication. From the repository root: ```sh ffmpeg -y -loglevel error \ -f lavfi -i "nullsrc=s=1920x1080:r=1,noise=alls=100:allf=t+u" \ -frames:v 6 /tmp/opencode-ws-%d.png cd packages/opencode OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_WEBSOCKETS=true bun run src/index.ts run \ "Reply with only: received" \ --pure --print-logs --log-level DEBUG --auto \ --model openai/gpt-5.6-sol \ -f /tmp/opencode-ws-{1..6}.png ``` On unpatched `dev`, this produces five `ProviderResponseStreamError` failures with `code 1009: message too big` before HTTP fallback succeeds. With this change, the same request immediately falls back to HTTP and returns the normal streamed response. ## Testing - `bun test test/plugin/openai-ws.test.ts` - `bun typecheck` - `bunx prettier --check src/plugin/openai/ws.ts src/plugin/openai/ws-pool.ts test/plugin/openai-ws.test.ts`

signals.title: fix(core): fall back on oversized websocket requests v2
signals.text: ## Summary - classify WebSocket close code 1009 before provider observation as rejected delivery - retry the current model request immediately through its HTTP fallback - keep the Session on HTTP after an oversized WebSocket rejection Fixes #42572 ## Reproduction V2 contains the Responses WebSocket transport, but normal OpenAI Sessions currently do not select it: the built-in OpenAI plugin registers `session.http.request`, and `SessionModelRequest` treats any HTTP hook as WebSocket-ineligible. To exercise the transport on either `v2` or this branch, temporarily make this local-only change in `packages/core/src/session/model-request.ts`: ```diff - const webSocketEligible = - !(yield* hooks.has("session", "http.request")) && !(yield* hooks.has("session", "http.response")) + const webSocketEligible = true ``` Start the development server in one terminal: ```sh OPENCODE_PASSWORD=issue-42572 \ OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_OPENAI_RESPONSES_WEBSOCKET=true \ OPENCODE_CONFIG_PROJECT_DISABLE=true \ bun run --cwd packages/cli --conditions=browser src/index.ts \ --log-level debug serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 4097 ``` In another terminal, generate six valid noisy PNGs and submit them through the raw API. Using the raw API avoids the CLI SSE reader's separate 16 MiB event limit. ```sh ffmpeg -y -loglevel error \ -f lavfi -i "nullsrc=s=1920x1080:r=1,noise=alls=100:allf=t+u" \ -frames:v 6 /tmp/opencode-ws-%d.png SESSION=$(jq -n --arg directory "$PWD" \ '{model:{providerID:"openai",id:"gpt-5.6-sol"},location:{directory:$directory}}' | curl -fsSu opencode:issue-42572 \ -H "content-type: application/json" \ --data-binary @- http://127.0.0.1:4097/api/session | jq -r .data.id) jq -n '{ text:"Reply with only: received", files:[range(1;7) as $i | { uri:("file:///tmp/opencode-ws-" + ($i|tostring) + ".png"), name:("opencode-ws-" + ($i|tostring) + ".png") }] }' | curl -fsSu opencode:issue-42572 \ -H "content-type: application/json" \ --data-binary @- "http://127.0.0.1:4097/api/session/$SESSION/prompt" while :; do RESULT=$(curl -fsSu opencode:issue-42572 \ "http://127.0.0.1:4097/api/session/$SESSION/message?order=asc&limit=200" | jq -c '[.data[] | select(.type == "assistant")][-1] | select(.error != null or .time.completed != null) | {error, completed:.time.completed}' 2>/dev/null) [ -n "$RESULT" ] && printf '%s\n' "$RESULT" && break sleep 1 done ``` Observed against real OpenAI infrastructure with a 20,127,431-byte serialized `response.create`: - Unpatched `v2`: WebSocket closes with code 1009 and the assistant ends with `provider.transport`; there is no HTTP recovery. - This branch: the same request completes normally over HTTP, and a subsequent prompt in the same Session remains on HTTP without opening another WebSocket. The warm-up test also exposed a separate V2 parser issue: ChatGPT may emit `codex.rate_limits` before `response.created`, which currently produces `provider.invalid-output`. That is independent of this fallback change. ## Testing - `bun test test/session-model-transport.test.ts test/session-model-transport-live.test.ts` - `bun typecheck --force` - `bunx prettier --check src/session/model-transport.ts test/session-model-transport.test.ts`

signals.title: docs: sync engine plan — fold + outbox client over the existing durable log
signals.text: ## What A plan document, presented as an option: redesign frontend state management so the client consumes the event-sourced session core that already exists server-side, instead of maintaining a hand-defended mirror of it. The end state is **less code that is more reliable**: optimistic UI, gapless reconnect, and safe retry become structural guarantees (`state = fold(events)`, `outbox` of intents, `view` derived) rather than special cases defended at every sync path. This PR is a discussion vehicle — outline first, sections filled in as the design conversation happens. The doc opens with a context ledger of audit receipts (file:line) establishing what the v2 server already provides: - durable per-session event log with atomic projections (`bus.ts`, `event/sql.ts`) - 40/46 session events durable; deltas ephemeral by design - replay+live log endpoint (`/api/experimental/session/:id/log`) - adopt-on-ID admission (`SessionInbox.admit`) and what's actually missing (one watermarked-hydration read, one adopt-strictness fix). ## Scope - Doc only; no code changes. - Builds on the optimistic-submission stopgap PRs #42807 / #42808 — client-generated IDs stay, the ledger + guards there are what this plan eventually deletes. - Validated by a standalone prototype (Effect + Solid, six laws as tests, seeded chaos simulation) — happy to share.

signals.title: fix(session): skip in-flight sessions in --continue selection
signals.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #43133 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? `opencode run --continue` picks the most recently updated session with no liveness check, so a second instance can silently inject its prompt into a session another instance is actively using. The fix adds an `excludeActive` query param to `session.list`. A session is considered in-flight when it holds an assistant message with `time.created` but no `time.completed` (the durable signal both V1 and V2 writers leave in the `message` table). The list query excludes such sessions via `NOT EXISTS` over `json_extract(data, '$.role')` / `json_extract(data, '$.time.completed')`. `run --continue` now lists all and idle sessions in parallel, prints a warning when the top candidate was skipped because it is still active in another instance, and uses the idle candidate. Explicit `-s <session-id>` selection is unaffected. ### How did you verify your code works? - `bun typecheck` passes in `packages/opencode` and `packages/core`. - New tests in `packages/opencode/test/session/session.test.ts` cover in-flight exclusion and the set-preserving case (completed assistant message does not cause exclusion). Full file: 10 pass, 0 fail. - Live two-instance repro: instance A running a long prompt (in-flight assistant message present in the DB), instance B `opencode run --continue` prints `Skipped session <A> (still active in another instance)` and continues the idle session instead. DB forensics confirm B's prompt landed in the idle session, not A's. ### Screenshots / recordings N/A — not a UI change. ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

signals.title: fix(core): support older previous-channel databases
signals.text: ## What Make the previous-V2 database importer tolerate older `opencode-next.db` schemas whose optional project or session columns predate the current importer. Fixes #43139. Fixes #41341. ## Before / After **Before:** The importer read `project` and `session` with `SELECT *` into the current TypeScript row shapes. If the source database lacked a newer nullable column such as `icon_url_override`, `fork_boundary`, or `time_suspended`, property access returned `undefined`. Drizzle rendered that value as an empty SQL expression, producing statements like `VALUES (..., , ...)` and failing migration with `SQLiteError: near ",": syntax error`. **After:** The importer inspects each source table and builds an explicit projection. Existing columns are selected normally, absent optional columns are projected as SQL `NULL`, and absent required columns fail early with a compatibility error naming the table and columns. Historical field backfills, including `icon_url_override` from `icon_url`, are preserved. The destination inserts therefore never receive `undefined` for declared historical fields. ## How - `packages/core/src/database/v1-migration.bun.ts` defines an exhaustive compatibility strategy for every previous-V2 project and session field. Adding a future field now requires declaring whether it is required, nullable, or copied from an older field. - `selectNextRows` reads `pragma_table_info`, synthesizes compatible source projections, and preserves session import ordering. - `packages/core/test/v1-migration.test.ts` creates a real older-shape SQLite database, runs the importer, verifies missing fields arrive as `NULL`, and verifies the historical project icon backfill. ## Scope This fixes the Core previous-V2 import path. It does not change client migration readiness or restored-session error handling. ## Testing - `bun run test ./test/v1-migration.test.ts` from `packages/core`: 24 passed - `bun run test` from `packages/core`: 1,842 passed, 16 skipped - `bun typecheck` from `packages/core`: passed - Repository pre-push typecheck: 33 tasks passed

signals.title: feat: add /reload slash command
signals.text: ## Summary Adds a `/reload` slash command that hot-reloads OpenCode configuration, plugins, MCP servers, and other instance-scoped services without restarting the TUI. If any sessions are active in the current instance, reload is queued until they become idle, then the backend instance is reloaded and the TUI re-syncs before dismissing the reload overlay. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e5e9138c-25b9-43db-a53f-ba1de26bf5f9 Closes #6719 <!-- Old screencasts from an earlier implementation may not reflect current behavior: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7e14c446-80bc-4a81-b092-94b08ae120e7 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eb8140be-d770-4b26-be41-9d9536088fcd --> ## How it works The current implementation is built on the instance HttpApi and EventV2 flow: 1. The global TUI command `/reload` calls `POST /config/reload` for the current workspace. 2. `ConfigReload.request()` records reload state for the current instance/workspace, not globally across every open project. 3. If sessions are active, the reload stays pending until every active session in that instance becomes idle. 4. When execution starts, the server reloads the current instance through `InstanceStore.reload(...)` after the HTTP response is produced. 5. The TUI receives `config.reload.executing`, shows the blocking `Reloading configuration...` overlay, and performs a full bootstrap refresh. 6. The TUI acknowledges the exact bootstrap cycle with `POST /config/bootstrap-complete?cycle=...` only after the full refresh completes. 7. The server emits `config.reload.done`, and the TUI dismisses the overlay and shows a success toast. Reload state is scoped per instance/workspace, bootstrap completions require a matching cycle, and repeated reload requests during an active reload are coalesced so users do not see a false ready state between back-to-back reloads. ## User-visible behavior If no session is active, `/reload` starts immediately and shows the reload overlay. If sessions are running, `/reload` queues the reload and shows a queued toast; the reload starts once all active sessions in that client become idle. During the reload overlay, keyboard input is blocked so stray keystrokes are not leaked into the prompt. The `reload_config` tool still stops the current tool-processing turn with `stopSession: true`, but it no longer injects a synthetic user prompt to continue the conversation after reload. This avoids adding artificial “continue where you left off” text to durable session history or model context. ## Validation - Added focused regression tests for per-instance reload isolation, same-client multi-session queuing, bootstrap-cycle scoping, repeated reload coalescing, and absence of synthetic continuation prompt data. - Regenerated the v2 SDK from the updated HttpApi schema. - Typechecked `packages/opencode` and `packages/tui`. - Stress-tested the real TUI in tmux: `/reload` works from the home screen and from a session screen, no longer resolves to `/snippets:reload`, shows and clears the reload overlay, and remains stable when `/reload` is hammered during an in-flight reload.

signal.title: [FEATURE]: Surface compaction progress and live context usage in the TUI
signal.text: ## Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. I did find the closed overlap in #16395, where the TUI expected a compacting status but the server never set one. I think this is worth reviving as that lifecycle fix plus a separate always-visible context countdown. ## Describe the enhancement you want to request I maintain oh-my-openagent, a community OpenCode plugin. Filing this as a regular community proposal, not on behalf of OpenCode. Right now compaction can make the TUI feel frozen. During `/compact` or auto-compaction, there may be no clear signal for several seconds, which matches the pain in #26381 around long spinners with no visible progress. There is also no always-visible context countdown, so users cannot anticipate auto-compaction. I am proposing two honest indicators: 1. Always show `Context NN%`, computed from used tokens divided by the model context window. When the threshold is computable, the PoC now renders `Context NN% · auto-compact ~MM%`, mirroring the server `usable()` formula with the default reserved buffer. 2. While compaction runs, show `Compacting conversation...`, a spinner, elapsed seconds, and an indeterminate bar. Here is the PoC in the real TUI during `/compact`: ![compaction progress and context countdown in the opencode TUI](https://github.com/MoerAI/opencode/releases/download/demo-compaction-progress/compaction-demo.gif) I do not want a fake operation percent or ETA. The compaction summary is an LLM call with no known output length, so elapsed time plus an indeterminate animation is the honest version. The only percent should be the context countdown, based on used/window. Related issues: #16395 is the closest one. #27359 asks for async compaction with a `Compacting...` signal. #24807 asks for better terminal-native progress. #11434 asks for more context-window visibility. #21520 points at the same user problem from the threshold side. Design questions for maintainers: 1. Channel: should this add a `compacting` variant to public `session.status` / `SessionStatus`, giving one source for active/idle state, abort/undo, notifications, and SDK polling, or should it use a dedicated compaction event to avoid widening the public union? 2. Should the always-visible countdown be default-on or opt-in? 3. Should the countdown show `auto-compact ~MM%` only if a real threshold is exposed, and is exposing that threshold desirable? I have a working PoC: [the draft PR](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/32927). The operation indicator is gated behind `experimentalEventSystem`, so default UX stays unchanged when the flag is off. A live TUI capture shows both indicators during `/compact`, including `Compacting conversation...` with elapsed seconds and `Context 5%`. The recording above is from that run.

signal.title: [FEATURE]: Progress indicator for MCP calls
signal.text:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [X] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ← Note: suggested but abandoned, see section *Prior art* ### Describe the enhancement you want to request ## Motivation While an MCP call is running, OpenCode’s TUI currently doesn’t show progress info, even if the MCP server sends progress updates. Especially with longer-running services (which are common in MCP, e.g. on-demand embedding runs), this is awkward from the user’s point of view because the conversation can seem stuck for minutes. That effect is about to get even more noticeable when [#24964]() is merged, which (correctly) fixes an issue with `resetTimeoutOnProgress`, causing the “user is waiting for anything to happen” time to become potentially unbounded. ## Suggestion If an MCP server sends progress messages, then the text in the TUI should reflect that progress message. Depending of whether the MCP progress message includes the optional `total` and `message` fields, I suggest that instead of the current message: ```plain ⚙ mcp_service_name [query=very long running call] ``` I suggest that the TUI render one of the following: ```plain ⚙ mcp_service_name [query=very long running call] · In progress [42] ``` or, if the server includes a `total`: ```plain ⚙ mcp_service_name [query=very long running call] · In progress [42/800] ``` or, if the server includes both a `total` and a custom `message`: ```plain ⚙ mcp_service_name [query=very long running call] · Calculating embeddings [42/800] ``` ## Prior art Here’s what has been done so far: * @fahreddinozcan’s PR [#24964]() ← this is the foundation that actually triggers the MCP server to send progress messages (and fixes the timeout issue). Needs to be merged first. * @wangguodong-f’s report anomalyco/opencode#22153 ← related but different focus (subagents). Pinging them anyway for ideas and to keep them in the loop. Related but abandoned: * @rfhold’s report [#11821]() ← very related, also abandoned. A bit more focused (it mentions only the SDK plumbing, not the TUI changes.) However, doing both plumbing and TUI at once might give the user more immediate value (and the developer a closer feedback loop). * @xhuw’s report [#2101]() ← very similar to this report, abandoned * @CagierAsh123’s report [#5472]() ← related but broader (not just focused on MCP), abandoned * @ravshansbox’s report [#3742]() ← related but broader, abandoned * @Becktor’s report anomalyco/opencode#9655 ← related, different proposal (sidebar), broader, abandoned ## Technical design (draft/proposal) *Note: I started out entirely unfamiliar with the code base, and there’s no way I could have possibly come up with a design draft by myself. The following is the gist of a few days of back-and-forth with Opus 4.7 and includes insights from a PoC implementation.*
Design draft MCP client Accepts a new optional `onProgress` callback and passes that to the MCP SDK’s `callTool` options. If none is supplied, passes an empty callback (that same empty callback as in PR [#24964](), which tickles the MCP SDK to include a progress token in the request so the server can send progress messages and the timeout is properly reset.) Session runner (prompt.ts) Gets to own a small adapter (in form of an `onProgress` callback) that it injects into the MCP client. The adapter consumes progress reports and converts them into a v1 bus event and a v2 sync event (dual-write, just like the rest of the codebase does). Bus Needs a new v1 event type `.tool.progress.report`. v2 sync-event registry Gets a new v2 event type `.next.tool.progress.report`. A similar event type named `.next.tool.progress` already exists but handles unrelated stuff, i.e. partial tool output, which arrives entirely separate from progress reports. We can’t rename the existing `….progress` type lest we’d break existing consumers. Hence, `….progress.report`. Session projector Receives the progress report as a v2 sync event, updates the database, and updates the `ToolStateRunning` model in the v2 `SessionMessage`. TUI v1 client Receives the progress report from the bus and updates its `store.part[messageID][idx].state.progress`. TUI v2 client Receives the progress report from the bus and updates the `ToolStateRunning` model. TUI v1/v2 renderer Presents the progress info in its `InlineTool` and `BlockTool` components when a tool is `running`.
## Commitment If the core team decides that this is worth doing, I’ll be happy to implement this end to end.

signal.title: [FEATURE]: Preserve Failed Attempts During Context Compaction
signal.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request During context compaction, when the conversation context becomes full, the model may fail to preserve information about previous unsuccessful attempts. As a result, after compaction, it can lose awareness that a particular approach has already been tried and failed. This leads to the model repeating the same attempt instead of exploring alternative solutions, reducing efficiency and potentially causing loops in long-running tasks. Expected behavior: Context compaction should retain key information about failed attempts, rejected approaches, and encountered errors. After compaction, the model should be able to recognize that a previous strategy did not work and avoid unnecessarily repeating it. Actual behavior: Information about failed attempts may be omitted during compaction. The model sometimes retries the same approach after compaction, even though it had already been attempted and proven unsuccessful earlier in the conversation. Impact: Repeated work and wasted tokens. Reduced effectiveness in debugging, coding, and multi-step problem-solving tasks. Increased likelihood of entering repetitive solution loops during long conversations.

signal.title: `opencode run --format json --session` hangs after final answer is persisted
signal.text: ### Description ### Summary `opencode run --format json --session <session_id>` can hang even after the model has completed and the final assistant answer has been persisted to OpenCode’s session DB. In our repro, the process stayed alive, stdout remained empty, but the SQLite session DB contained both the completed tool result and final answer. ### What We Tried We tested PR #31505, which flushes missed parts after the stream loop finishes: ```ts await finish() if (!args.attach) await flushParts(result.data?.parts) ``` That did not fix our case because `finish()` itself can hang waiting for the event stream to observe `session.status: idle`. Since `flushParts()` runs after `finish()`, the fallback is never reached. ### Custom Patch We changed JSON mode to flush returned prompt/command parts before waiting for stream completion: ```ts async function finishBestEffort() { if (args.format !== "json") { await finish() return } await Promise.race([ finish(), new Promise<void>((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1000)), ]) } ``` Then changed both `session.command` and `session.prompt` paths from: ```ts await finish() if (!args.attach) await flushParts(result.data?.parts) ``` to: ```ts if (!args.attach) await flushParts(result.data?.parts) await finishBestEffort() ``` ### Why This Works Once `client.session.prompt()` or `client.session.command()` returns, `result.data.parts` contains the completed assistant parts. For `--format json`, emitting those parts immediately avoids depending on the event stream’s idle signal. The stream is still given a short best-effort drain window, but output delivery no longer blocks forever on it. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version 0.17.7 ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signal.title: [BUG] TUI session view doesn't reflect external updates to an active session
signal.text: ### Description ### Describe the bug When a session is being driven by an **external** process — another opencode client, a remote agent or `opencode serve` running the session elsewhere — the TUI session view goes stale. New messages and parts produced outside this TUI's own event stream never appear until you manually switch away and back. The root cause is in the `useSync` hook: `sync.session.sync(sessionID)` short-circuits once a session has been fully hydrated: ```ts async sync(sessionID: string) { if (fullSyncedSessions.has(sessionID)) return // <- never re-fetches ... } ``` So after the first hydration the TUI relies entirely on live SSE events. Any update that doesn't arrive over that stream (external writer, dropped/missed event, a session being advanced by a different process) leaves the view permanently out of date. ### Expected behavior While a session is active, the TUI should periodically reconcile with the server so externally-produced updates appear, instead of trusting the initial hydration plus the local event stream alone. ### Proposed fix - Add a `{ force?: boolean }` option to `useSync().session.sync()` that bypasses the `fullSyncedSessions` cache and re-fetches. - In the session route, poll every 2s with `{ force: true }` only while the session status is working or compacting, and stop polling (clearInterval via `onCleanup`) once it goes idle. - Covered by a new test asserting that a normal `sync()` is a no-op on an already- hydrated session while `sync(id, { force: true })` re-fetches and picks up new messages. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version 1.15.13 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start a session and let it hydrate in the TUI. 2. 2. Drive that same session from an external source (e.g. opencode-remote, a second client, or the server directly) so new assistant messages are appended. 3. Observe the TUI session view — it does not show the new messages/parts. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System macOS 26.3 ### Terminal iTerm2

signal.title: [QOL]:  Treat directories with .git or opencode.json as local projects (not global)
signal.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request ## Description: OpenCode currently only promotes a directory from “global” to a distinct project when Git has at least one commit. This forces users to make an initial commit even when they only want project-scoped config or agents. We should treat a directory as a local project if either (a) a `.git` directory exists (even without commits) or (b) an `opencode.json` file is present at the root. ### Current behavior - `git init` alone (no commits) → `project.id === "global"` [1](#2-0) - Adding `opencode.json` does not affect project ID detection [2](#2-1) - Tests confirm: repo with only `git init` yields global; repo with commits yields non-global [3](#2-2) ### Expected behavior - Presence of `.git` directory OR `opencode.json` should cause OpenCode to assign a non-global project ID and enable project-scoped features (e.g., `.opencode/` directories, project config precedence). ### Why this matters - Users often create a project to set up agents or project-specific config before committing. - Requiring an initial commit is unnecessary friction for configuration-only workflows. - `opencode.json` already signals intent to be a project; it should influence project detection. ### Suggested implementation hints - In `Project.fromDirectory`, after the existing Git toplevel/common-dir checks, add a fallback: - If `existsSync(path.join(directory, ".git"))` OR `Filesystem.findUp("opencode.json", directory)` succeeds, generate a non-global project ID (e.g., hash of the absolute path) and set `vcs: "git"` if `.git` exists, else `vcs: undefined`. - Ensure `migrateFromGlobal` runs for these newly-recognized projects [4](#2-3) . - Update tests to cover both cases. ### Acceptance criteria - [ ] Directory with only `.git` (no commits) opens as a local project. - [ ] Directory with `opencode.json` (no Git) opens as a local project. - [ ] Existing behavior with committed Git repos is unchanged. - [ ] Sessions migrate from global to the new local project when applicable. ## Notes - The UI determines “global” status by checking `projectID === "global"` or when metadata lacks an ID but has local overrides [5](#2-4) . - Project configs already override global configs in the merge order, but they don’t affect the initial project ID assignment [6](#2-5) . Wiki pages you might want to explore: - [Architecture (anomalyco/opencode)](/wiki/anomalyco/opencode#2) - [Agent System (anomalyco/opencode)](/wiki/anomalyco/opencode#3.3) ### Citations **File:** packages/opencode/src/project/project.ts (L143-192) ```typescript const top = await git(["rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"], { cwd: sandbox, }) .then(async (result) => path.resolve(sandbox, (await result.text()).trim())) .catch(() => undefined) if (!top) { return { id, sandbox, worktree: sandbox, vcs: Info.shape.vcs.parse(Flag.OPENCODE_FAKE_VCS), } } sandbox = top const worktree = await git(["rev-parse", "--git-common-dir"], { cwd: sandbox, }) .then(async (result) => { const dirname = path.dirname((await result.text()).trim()) if (dirname === ".") return sandbox return dirname }) .catch(() => undefined) if (!worktree) { return { id, sandbox, worktree: sandbox, vcs: Info.shape.vcs.parse(Flag.OPENCODE_FAKE_VCS), } } return { id, sandbox, worktree, vcs: "git", } } return { id: "global", worktree: "/", sandbox: "/", vcs: Info.shape.vcs.parse(Flag.OPENCODE_FAKE_VCS), } ``` **File:** packages/opencode/src/project/project.ts (L294-314) ```typescript async function migrateFromGlobal(id: string, worktree: string) { const row = Database.use((db) => db.select().from(ProjectTable).where(eq(ProjectTable.id, "global")).get()) if (!row) return const sessions = Database.use((db) => db.select().from(SessionTable).where(eq(SessionTable.project_id, "global")).all(), ) if (sessions.length === 0) return log.info("migrating sessions from global", { newProjectID: id, worktree, count: sessions.length }) await work(10, sessions, async (row) => { // Skip sessions that belong to a different directory if (row.directory && row.directory !== worktree) return log.info("migrating session", { sessionID: row.id, from: "global", to: id }) Database.use((db) => db.update(SessionTable).set({ project_id: id }).where(eq(SessionTable.id, row.id)).run()) }).catch((error) => { log.error("failed to migrate sessions from global to project", { error, projectId: id }) }) } ``` **File:** packages/web/src/content/docs/config.mdx (L41-52) ```text ### Precedence order Config sources are loaded in this order (later sources override earlier ones): 1. **Remote config** (from `.well-known/opencode`) - organizational defaults 2. **Global config** (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`) - user preferences 3. **Custom config** (`OPENCODE_CONFIG` env var) - custom overrides 4. **Project config** (`opencode.json` in project) - project-specific settings 5. **`.opencode` directories** - agents, commands, plugins 6. **Inline config** (`OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` env var) - runtime overrides This means project configs can override global defaults, and global configs can override remote organizational defaults. ``` **File:** packages/web/src/content/docs/config.mdx (L104-114) ```text ### Per project Add `opencode.json` in your project signal.title: MCP session recovery does not trigger on HTTP 400 (only 404) — breaks servers that return 400 for expired sessions
signal.text: PR #32088 (closes #25137) added MCP Streamable HTTP session recovery, but it only reinitializes when a POST receives **HTTP 404**. Some MCP servers return **HTTP 400** for an expired/missing session, so recovery never fires and every tool call fails until opencode is restarted. Reopening as a separate issue because #25137 is closed and may not be re-triaged. ## Description When the remote MCP server invalidates a Streamable HTTP session via idle timeout, the Atlassian/Jira MCP server (uvicorn, Atlassian MCP 1.12.4) responds to the stale `mcp-session-id` with **HTTP 400**, not 404. The recovery logic from #32088 only handles 404, so the session is never reinitialized and all subsequent tool calls fail with `Bad Request: No valid session ID provided` until a full restart. Reproducible every ~15-30 min of inactivity. The PR description for #32088 explicitly scopes the fix to the 404 POST failure, so this is a known gap rather than a regression. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Configure a remote Streamable HTTP MCP server that returns 400 for an unknown/expired session id (e.g. Atlassian MCP 1.12.4). 2. Use it normally; a few tool calls succeed. 3. Wait for the server-side idle timeout (~15-30 min). 4. Call any tool again → fails permanently with `Bad Request: No valid session ID provided`. Only a restart fixes it. Reproduced directly against the live server with a stale session id: ``` $ curl -si <server>/mcp/ -X POST \ -H "Authorization: Token ***" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \ -H "mcp-session-id: 00000000000000000000000000000000" \ -d "{\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"id\":1,\"method\":\"tools/list\",\"params\":{}}" HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request server: uvicorn content-length: 41 Bad Request: No valid session ID provided ``` Handshake without a session also returns a structured JSON-RPC error (code -32600): ```json {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"server-error","error":{"code":-32600,"message":"Bad Request: Missing session ID"}} ``` ## Suggested fix Extend the recovery trigger (currently 404-only, see #32088) to also cover a **400** that indicates a missing/expired session — e.g. body matching `No valid session ID` / `Missing session ID`, or JSON-RPC error code `-32600` with `session` in the message. Keep the same bounded single-retry behavior already implemented. ## OpenCode version 1.17.8 (desktop) ## Operating System macOS Related: #25137, #28567

signal.title: perf(plugin): O(N) dispatch overhead on every trigger call — pre-index hooks by name
signal.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request ## Performance: eliminate O(N) plugin dispatch overhead on every trigger call `packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts` has two hot paths that scale linearly with the number of loaded plugins on **every single message, tool call, and config change**. With 10+ plugins loaded these add measurable latency to the session loop — especially `trigger()`, which fires multiple times per assistant turn. Both fixes are purely internal (no public API change, no behaviour change, no new dependencies), and together they reduced our measured plugin-dispatch overhead to near-zero on a 12-plugin workload. --- ### Problem 1: `events.listen(...)` always subscribes even when no plugin uses `event` The current code unconditionally subscribes to the global event bus: ```ts // current upstream const unsubscribe = yield* events.listen((event) => { if (event.location?.directory !== ctx.directory) return Effect.void return Effect.sync(() => { for (const hook of hooks) { void hook["event"]?.({ event: { id: event.id, type: event.type, properties: event.data } as any }) } }) }) yield* Effect.addFinalizer(() => unsubscribe) ``` **Cost**: On every emitted event — even when zero plugins implement `event` — this allocates an `Effect.sync`, does a directory equality check, then linearly scans all hooks hitting `?.` on each. For a typical session producing hundreds of events/sec during streaming, this is pure waste. **Fix**: Pre-filter once at startup; skip the subscription entirely when the filtered set is empty: ```ts const eventListeners = hooks.filter((h) => typeof h.event === "function") if (eventListeners.length > 0) { const unsubscribe = yield* events.listen((event) => { if (event.location?.directory !== ctx.directory) return Effect.void return Effect.sync(() => { for (const hook of eventListeners) { void hook.event!({ event: { id: event.id, type: event.type, properties: event.data } as any }) } }) }) yield* Effect.addFinalizer(() => unsubscribe) } ``` **Impact**: Zero-listener projects (the majority — most plugins are auth/config only) pay absolutely nothing. Listener projects iterate a smaller pre-filtered array without optional-chaining overhead. --- ### Problem 2: `trigger()` linearly scans all hooks on every call `trigger()` is the **hottest function in the plugin system** — it fires for `chat.params`, `chat.message`, `tool.execute`, `config`, etc. Current implementation: ```ts // current upstream for (const hook of s.hooks) { const fn = hook[name] as any if (!fn) continue yield* Effect.promise(async () => fn(input, output)) } ``` With N plugins and M trigger names, every trigger call does N property lookups and N conditional branches even when 0 or 1 hooks actually implement that name. On a 12-plugin setup triggering ~6 hook names per assistant message, this is 72 wasted iterations per message turn. **Fix**: Build a `Map<string, Hooks[]>` dispatch table once at plugin-load time: ```ts // at state init: const hooksByName = new Map<string, Hooks[]>() for (const hook of hooks) { for (const name of Object.keys(hook) as (keyof Hooks)[]) { if (typeof hook[name] !== "function") continue const list = hooksByName.get(name as string) if (list) list.push(hook) else hooksByName.set(name as string, [hook]) } } return { hooks, hooksByName } // in trigger(): const matched = s.hooksByName.get(name as string) if (!matched) return output for (const hook of matched) { const fn = hook[name] as any yield* Effect.promise(async () => fn(input, output)) } ``` **Impact**: - Unhandled hook names (the common case per trigger): **O(1) early return** instead of O(N) scan. - Handled hook names: iterate only the relevant subset, zero wasted branches. - Hook execution order preserved (insertion order of the Map values array). --- ### Summary | Path | Before | After | |------|--------|-------| | `trigger("chat.params", ...)` with 12 plugins, 1 handler | 12 iterations, 11 `if (!fn) continue` | 1 iteration, direct dispatch | | `trigger("chat.message", ...)` with 12 plugins, 0 handlers | 12 iterations, all skipped | Map miss → immediate return | | Event stream, 0 event hooks | Subscribe + per-event O(N) scan | No subscription at all | Both changes add ~15 lines of init-time code and `State.hooksByName: Map<string, Hooks[]>`. No runtime allocations added to the hot path — only removed. Happy to send a PR with these changes if maintainers are interested. #### Notes - Related but orthogonal to #20285 (parallel plugin events) — that proposal is about concurrency policy; this one is about dispatch-table cost. - Type `State` gains one field: `hooksByName: Map<string, Hooks[]>`. - No public API change, no plugin contract change.

signal.title: TUI hangs in tmux after opentui 0.1.103 upgrade (theme detection)
signal.text: ## Description After the opentui upgrade from 0.1.99 to 0.1.103 in commit 3a5507de9, the TUI becomes unresponsive when running inside tmux. Every keystroke lags significantly, making the app unusable. ## Root Cause `0.1.103` introduced `renderer.waitForThemeMode(timeout)` which sends OSC escape sequences to detect the terminal's background color. tmux doesn't forward these properly, so the call blocks for the full timeout duration on each render cycle — not just once at startup. The call site is in `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/app.tsx:133`: ```ts const mode = (await renderer.waitForThemeMode(1000)) ?? "dark" ``` ## Reproduction 1. Open a tmux session 2. Run `opencode` (built from dev branch with opentui >= 0.1.103) 3. Try typing — keystrokes are delayed by ~1 second each 4. Exit tmux, run `opencode` directly — works fine ## Workaround Pin opentui back to 0.1.99 in `package.json` and replace the `waitForThemeMode` call with a hardcoded `"dark"`. ## Environment - Linux (WSL2) - tmux 3.5a - Terminal: Windows Terminal / wezterm - TERM: xterm-256color

signal.title: fix(session): inherit parent directory + workspaceID in subagent sessions
signal.text: ### Description When opencode is run in HTTP server mode, the directory is always set to ctx.directory, which is the daemon's process.cwd(), NOT the parent session's context. For subagent sessions (parentID set), this is wrong: they should inherit the parent's directory to maintain workspace coherence. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce **Evidence (Session IDs from live observation, port 4096):** - Parent session: `ses_17cdba9cfffeC5A6FQLkMAFYtM` - Created in headless client project root - Correct: `directory=/path/to/headless/client/project/directory` - `workspaceID=wsv2_6uN7E5rF1I0rJy2qL` - Child Planner session: `ses_17cb08557ffe8G2ucNG1fi1F0c` - Created by Brain task tool for subagent execution - Incorrect: `directory=/path/to/opencode/daemon/home` (daemon's $HOME) - Should have been: `directory=/path/to/headless/client/project/directory` (inherited from parent) **Call trace:** - `headless client` makes HTTP POST to daemon's task endpoint with parent session context - Daemon's `task.ts` creates child session via `Session.create({ parentID })` - `session.ts` `Session.create()` previously did NOT inherit parent's directory - Result: child receives `ctx.directory` = daemon `process.cwd()` = `/path/to/opencode/daemon/home` ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Linux Debian/testing ### Terminal xterm ## Resolution See #32807 (supersedes #30650). The new PR is a fresh PR from the feature branch with improved scope: it adds structural projectID inheritance (so project_id can't drift from directory) on top of the original directory/workspaceID inheritance, includes a dedicated regression test, and excludes the unrelated bin/opencode ESM-shim change. Result is a conflict-free branch upstream can merge directly. Note: cross-project fork directory divergence is a separate deferred concern.

signal.title: macOS notifications show as 'Script Editor' instead of terminal app — no click-to-focus
signal.text: ## Problem On macOS, desktop notifications from OpenCode appear to come from **"Script Editor"** (AppleScript) instead of the terminal emulator (iTerm2, Terminal.app, etc.). Clicking the notification opens Script Editor instead of focusing the correct terminal tab. This happens because OpenCode uses `osascript -e 'display notification...'` as a fallback, and macOS attributes the notification to the osascript process (Script Editor) rather than the terminal. ## Expected Behavior - Notifications should be attributed to the terminal emulator (iTerm2, Terminal.app, etc.) - Clicking a notification should focus the correct terminal tab/window - On iTerm2 specifically, notifications should use OSC 9 escape sequences for native integration ## Current State I found **PR #23212** (`feat(tui): add terminal notifications` by @kitlangton) which addresses this by adding: - OSC 9 escape sequences (`\x1b]9;message\x07`) for iTerm2, Ghostty, Apple Terminal, Warp - OSC 777 for Kitty, WezTerm, VTE-based terminals - Bell (`\x07`) as fallback - Auto-detection based on `TERM_PROGRAM` However, this PR is: - **Draft** status - Has **merge conflicts** - Open since April 18 ## Suggested Fix The notification resolution logic from PR #23212 looks correct: ```typescript // For iTerm2 if (env.TERM_PROGRAM === "iTerm.app") return "osc9" // \x1b]9;title:body\x07 // For Kitty/WezTerm if (env.KITTY_WINDOW_ID || env.TERM === "xterm-kitty") return "osc777" // \x1b]777;notify;title;body\x07 // Fallback return "bell" // \x07 ``` Additionally, for terminals that don't support OSC sequences, consider using `terminal-notifier` with `-activate <bundle-id>`: - iTerm2: `com.googlecode.iterm2` - Terminal.app: `com.apple.Terminal` - Warp: `dev.warp.Warp-Stable` ⚠️ **Do NOT use `-sender` flag** — it conflicts with `-activate` on macOS Sequoia 15.x+ and breaks click-to-focus. ## Environment - macOS (Sequoia/Tahoe) - iTerm2 - OpenCode v1.14.18 - Installed via Homebrew ## Related - Draft PR: #23212

signal.title: OpenCode overwrites data in a different directory without any notification
signal.text: ### Description I work in a single repository but with multiple branches simultaneously. The branches are checked out into different directories (pkb, pkb_develop, pkb_gateway, pkb_checker, etc.). When opening the pkb_develop directory, OpenCode opened the pkb directory and started making changes there, without any notifications, warnings, or informational windows, and with no way to know that writing was happening to a different directory. I only found out after noticing the data discrepancy. The same thing happens with the other directories — OpenCode silently redirects everything to the first one. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version 1.17.7 ### Steps to reproduce **Steps to Reproduce** 1. **Prepare the environment:** - Clone a single Git repository into several different directories, for example: - `pkb` (main branch) - `pkb_develop` (develop branch) - `pkb_gateway` (gateway branch) - `pkb_checker` (checker branch) - In each directory, switch to its respective branch so that the file states differ across directories. 2. **Open and use the `pkb` directory first:** - Launch OpenCode and open the `pkb` directory as the working directory. - Make some changes to files there (this establishes it as the initially opened directory). 3. **Close and try to open a different directory:** - Close the `pkb` directory (or close OpenCode entirely and relaunch it). - Attempt to open any other directory, for example `pkb_develop`. 4. **Observe which directory is actually opened and where changes land:** - Check which directory OpenCode actually opens – it will be `pkb`, not `pkb_develop`. - Without receiving any notification, make file-modifying operations (edit code, create new files, modify existing ones). 5. **Verify where changes were written:** - After making changes, check which directory actually received those changes. **Actual Result:** - Once the `pkb` directory has been opened first, closing it and then trying to open any other directory (e.g. `pkb_develop`) causes OpenCode to silently open the `pkb` directory again instead of the selected one. - All subsequent file modifications are applied inside `pkb`, not in the directory the user intended to work in. - No notifications, warnings, or indicators appear to inform the user that writing is happening in a different directory. The behavior repeats for all other directories: OpenCode always silently redirects to `pkb`. **Expected Result:** - OpenCode should open the directory explicitly selected by the user, regardless of previous sessions. - File changes should be written to the currently opened and actively worked‑in directory. - Any fallback or redirect to a different directory must be clearly communicated to the user, with a warning and the option to abort. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Windows 10 ### Terminal _No response_

signal.title: [Bug] Kimi K2.6 reasoning content leaks into main response instead of being rendered as thinking block
signal.text: **Description:** When using **Kimi K2.6** through the **direct Moonshot AI** provider, the model's reasoning content is not separated into a thinking/rationale block. Instead, it is streamed as part of the main assistant response, making it look like the model is "talking to itself" in the answer. This does **not** happen with **Kimi K2.7** under the same setup — reasoning is correctly handled there. **Environment:** - OpenCode version: `1.17.7` - Provider: Moonshot AI (direct, via `/connect`) - Model: `Kimi K2.6` - OS: Windows 11 + WSL - Terminal: WezTerm **Steps to reproduce:** 1. Run `opencode`. 2. Connect Moonshot AI provider via `/connect`. 3. Select `Kimi K2.6` model via `/models`. 4. Send any prompt. 5. Observe that reasoning text appears inline in the assistant response rather than in a separate thinking block. **Expected behavior:** Reasoning should be rendered as a collapsible `Thought:` block (when `/thinking` is enabled) or hidden from the response entirely (when `/thinking` is disabled). **Actual behavior:** Reasoning text is mixed into the normal response text, as if it were part of the answer. The `/thinking` command has no effect on this behavior — the reasoning content is never recognized as a separate block. **Additional context:** - `/thinking` command state does not affect this behavior. - The issue appears specific to Kimi K2.6; Kimi K2.7 works correctly. - Possibly related to open issues around `reasoning_content` handling for Kimi K2.6: #29690, #29619, #27852, #32545.

signal.title: [FEATURE]: Expose applyable patch in edit permission metadata
signal.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request OpenCode currently sends `permission.asked` events for `edit` permissions with `metadata.diff`. This isnt applyable as a unified patch because it is run through `trimDiff()`, which removes common indentation from diff content lines. This breaks clients/integrations that consume `permission.asked` over the server/SSE API and want to preview the proposed edit using standard patch tooling, as in the case in https://github.com/nickjvandyke/opencode.nvim. Requested enhancement: Expose an untrimmed, applyable patch separately from the display diff, for example: ```ts metadata: { filepath, diff, // current trimmed display diff patch, // untrimmed createTwoFilesPatch(...) output } ```

signal.title: fix(session): unhandled PlatformError when binary file attachment does not exist
signal.text: ## Bug Description Attaching a binary file (image, PDF, HTML, etc.) that does not exist crashes the TUI with an unhandled \PlatformError\. Text file and directory attachments handle this gracefully — only the binary file path is missing error handling. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Start opencode in any project 2. Attach a non-existent binary file (e.g. \@missing_file.html\ or drag in a file that has been deleted) 3. Send the message ## Error \\\ PlatformError: NotFound: FileNotFoundError: W:\\path\\to\\missing_file.html at SessionPrompt.resolveUserPart ... at SessionPrompt.createUserMessage at SessionPrompt.prompt at SessionHttpApi.prompt \\\ The TUI becomes broken/unresponsive after this error. ## Root Cause In \packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts\, the \ esolveUserPart\ function handles file attachments differently depending on mime type: - **Text files** (lines 931-972): Uses \Effect.exit\ + \Exit.isFailure\ — catches errors gracefully, publishes to bus, returns error text part - **Directories** (lines 976-999): Same graceful pattern - **Binary files** (lines 1022-1043): Uses \Effect.catch(Effect.die)\ which converts any error (including \PlatformError.NotFound\) into an unrecoverable defect that crashes the session The problematic line is: \\\ s Buffer.from(yield* fsys.readFile(filepath).pipe(Effect.catch(Effect.die))) \\\ ## Expected Behavior Binary file read failures should be caught and surfaced to the user as an error message (same as text files), not crash the TUI. ## Suggested Fix Replace \Effect.catch(Effect.die)\ at line 1038 with \Effect.exit\ and add \Exit.isFailure\ handling that mirrors the text file pattern (lines 957-972): log the error, publish to bus, and return a synthetic text part with the error message.

signal.title: cloudflare-ai-gateway: Azure GPT-5.x models fail (max_tokens vs max_completion_tokens); per-model compat not honored
signal.text: ## Summary Azure GPT-5.x deployments routed through the built-in **`cloudflare-ai-gateway`** provider fail in OpenCode because requests use `max_tokens` instead of `max_completion_tokens`. This is distinct from #25096 (custom `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` providers) and #22623 (native Azure provider). Here the failure is in the **built-in** `cloudflare-ai-gateway` path backed by `@earendil-works/pi-ai`. ## Environment - OpenCode: **1.17.8** - Provider: `cloudflare-ai-gateway` (connected via `/connect`, Azure keys in gateway BYOK) - Gateway compat endpoint: `https://gateway.ai.cloudflare.com/v1/{account}/{gateway}/compat` - Model IDs: `azure-openai/gpt-5.4-nano`, `azure-openai/gpt-5.4`, `azure-openai/gpt-5.4-mini`, `azure-openai/gpt-5.5` - Other Azure deployments on the same provider (e.g. `grok-4-20-non-reasoning`, `kimi-k2.6`) work fine ## Reproduce `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`: ```jsonc { "provider": { "cloudflare-ai-gateway": { "models": { "azure-openai/gpt-5.4-nano": { "name": "GPT 5.4 Nano (Azure)" } } } } } ``` ```bash opencode run -m cloudflare-ai-gateway/azure-openai/gpt-5.4-nano "Reply with exactly: OK" ``` **Error:** ``` Unsupported parameter: 'max_tokens' is not supported with this model. Use 'max_completion_tokens' instead. ``` ## Root cause (pi-ai) In `@earendil-works/pi-ai` `openai-completions.js`, `detectCompat()` treats all `cloudflare-ai-gateway` URLs as non-standard and sets: ```js maxTokensField: useMaxTokens ? "max_tokens" : "max_completion_tokens" // where useMaxTokens includes isCloudflareAiGateway ``` So every gateway request sends `max_tokens`, which newer Azure GPT-5 deployments reject. `getCompat()` can override via `model.compat.maxTokensField`, but that override is not reachable from normal OpenCode config for custom models added in `opencode.jsonc`. ## Workarounds attempted (none worked) 1. Per-model `options.compat.maxTokensField` in `opencode.jsonc` 2. `modelOverrides` / full model entries in `~/.config/opencode/models.json` 3. Full model entries in `~/.pi/agent/models.json` (pi docs path) 4. signal.title: fix(session): skip in-flight sessions in --continue selection
signal.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #43133 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? `opencode run --continue` picks the most recently updated session with no liveness check, so a second instance can silently inject its prompt into a session another instance is actively using. The fix adds an `excludeActive` query param to `session.list`. A session is considered in-flight when it holds an assistant message with `time.created` but no `time.completed` (the durable signal both V1 and V2 writers leave in the `message` table). The list query excludes such sessions via `NOT EXISTS` over `json_extract(data, '$.role')` / `json_extract(data, '$.time.completed')`. `run --continue` now lists all and idle sessions in parallel, prints a warning when the top candidate was skipped because it is still active in another instance, and uses the idle candidate. Explicit `-s <session-id>` selection is unaffected. ### How did you verify your code works? - `bun typecheck` passes in `packages/opencode` and `packages/core`. - New tests in `packages/opencode/test/session/session.test.ts` cover in-flight exclusion and the set-preserving case (completed assistant message does not cause exclusion). Full file: 10 pass, 0 fail. - Live two-instance repro: instance A running a long prompt (in-flight assistant message present in the DB), instance B `opencode run --continue` prints `Skipped session <A> (still active in another instance)` and continues the idle session instead. DB forensics confirm B's prompt landed in the idle session, not A's. ### Screenshots / recordings N/A — not a UI change. ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

signal.title: shell.created event never includes pid (publishes the pre-spawn info)
signal.text: ### Version `opencode2 v0.0.0-beta-17519` (branch `beta`, commit `6106cb6`) ### Summary The `shell.created` event publishes the *pre-spawn* `Info` object, so `pid` is always `undefined` for subscribers. The `POST /api/shell` HTTP response does include the pid, so the omission only affects event consumers. ### Where In `packages/core/src/shell.ts`: - L205-214: `info` is built before the spawn, with no `pid`. - L236-239: after the spawn, the pid is attached to a *copy* kept in `session.info`: `info: produce(info, (draft) => { draft.pid = handle.pid })`. - L331: the event is published with the original object, discarding the copy that carries the pid: `yield* bus.publish(Shell.Event.Created, { info })`. `pid` is optional in the schema (`packages/schema/src/shell.ts:36-49`), so this is not a type error — the field is simply always absent on the event. ### Impact A plugin cannot correlate a shell with an OS process from events alone. `ctx.shell` exposes only `hook("create.before")` (`packages/plugin/src/promise/shell.ts:15-17`), and the plugin `Context` (`packages/plugin/src/promise/plugin.ts:17-33`) has no shell client or server URL, so there is no in-process way to fetch the pid afterwards. The workaround is scanning `ps` for a child of the server process that is its own process-group leader, matching start time and command — racy, and it breaks whenever the spawner is not the plugin's own process. ### Suggested fix Publish the post-spawn info. `session` is already in scope — it is used on the very next line. ```diff - yield* bus.publish(Shell.Event.Created, { info }) + yield* bus.publish(Shell.Event.Created, { info: session.info }) ``` ### Repro 1. Subscribe to events (in-process plugin via `ctx.event.subscribe()`, or the event stream). 2. `POST /api/shell` with any long-running command. 3. The HTTP response contains `"pid": <n>`; the `shell.created` event for the same shell id has no `pid`.

signal.title: MCP schema warnings: non-standard "format" values (uint32/uint64) from schemars pollute TUI
signal.text: ## Problem MCP servers that derive their JSON Schemas from Rust types via `schemars` emit non-standard `format` values like `uint32`, `uint64`, `uint8`, and `uint`. When opencode registers these tools, AJV (the JSON Schema validator) outputs warnings for each unknown format: ``` unknown format "uint64" ignored in schema for path "/properties/pid" unknown format "uint32" ignored in schema for path "/properties/width" ... ``` These warnings cannot be suppressed — `--log-level ERROR` does not help because they come from AJV's `console.warn()` bypassing opencode's logger. ## Affected MCP servers - `computer-use-linux` (schemars-derived schemas for Rust u32/u64/u8 types) - BigQuery MCP (previously reported in #8581) - Any other MCP server built with Rust + schemars ## Previous attempt PR #12815 ("fix(mcp): strip non-standard JSON Schema formats to suppress AJV warnings") was closed without merging. ## Request Either: 1. Strip non-standard format values before AJV validation (resurrect #12815 approach) 2. Provide a mechanism to suppress/silence schema validation warnings from MCP tool registration 3. Both ## Why upstream fixes aren't enough While individual MCP servers can (and should) configure schemars to use `SchemaSettings::draft07()` to avoid emitting these formats, this is a systemic issue that will keep appearing for any Rust MCP server using default schemars config.

signal.title: fix(core): support older previous-channel databases
signal.text: ## What Make the previous-V2 database importer tolerate older `opencode-next.db` schemas whose optional project or session columns predate the current importer. Fixes #43139. Fixes #41341. ## Before / After **Before:** The importer read `project` and `session` with `SELECT *` into the current TypeScript row shapes. If the source database lacked a newer nullable column such as `icon_url_override`, `fork_boundary`, or `time_suspended`, property access returned `undefined`. Drizzle rendered that value as an empty SQL expression, producing statements like `VALUES (..., , ...)` and failing migration with `SQLiteError: near ",": syntax error`. **After:** The importer inspects each source table and builds an explicit projection. Existing columns are selected normally, absent optional columns are projected as SQL `NULL`, and absent required columns fail early with a compatibility error naming the table and columns. Historical field backfills, including `icon_url_override` from `icon_url`, are preserved. The destination inserts therefore never receive `undefined` for declared historical fields. ## How - `packages/core/src/database/v1-migration.bun.ts` defines an exhaustive compatibility strategy for every previous-V2 project and session field. signal.title: feat(opencode): Allow per-MCP-server trust configuration
signal.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #40111 Also partially addresses https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/23506 Rather than disabling verification globally, fingerprint pinning achieves the same goal — trusting a specific self-signed cert — without insecure: true. caFile handles private CAs cleanly without a blanket bypass. https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/14696 https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/26862 The createTlsFetch() wrapper and per-server TLS config injection proves the transport-layer plumbing needed for mTLS. Adding cert/key fields to the tls config block follows the same pattern — caFile validates PEM; cert+key would too. https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/1694 Provides a portable alternative. Instead of relying on OS-specific trust stores, caFile: "~/ca.pem" lets users point to their corporate CA explicitly, working identically across macOS/Linux/Windows without NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS. ### Type of change - [ ] Bug fix - [x] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [x] Documentation ### What does this PR do? Adds per-MCP-server TLS trust configuration for remote MCP servers using self-signed certificates or private CAs. Three options: `caFile` (path to CA cert), `caPem` (inline CA cert), and `fingerprint` (SHA256 certificate pinning, like SSH host keys). Config schema is added to both V1 and V2 MCP configs. A `buildTlsCa()` helper reads files, validates PEM content, and verifies fingerprints, then `createTlsFetch()` injects the trusted CA into a custom fetch wrapper scoped to that transport only — no global TLS changes. Fingerprint verification uses a one-time pre-flight TLS socket to retrieve the server cert, compares it against the user-provided fingerprint, and promotes the verified cert to a trusted CA. Trust applies only to that transport instance and does not leak across MCP servers. ### How did you verify your code works? - Unit tests cover PEM validation, fingerprint format validation, file reading, DER-to-PEM conversion, and `buildTlsCa` integration - Three-pass code review (security, style/contribution guidelines, architectural design) - TOCTOU in file reads fixed via fd-based atomic stat+read - Performance review confirmed zero overhead on the no-TLS path (the guard `if (mcp.tls)` prevents any new allocations or yields when TLS is not configured) ### Screenshots / recordings _Not a UI change._ ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

signal.title: core: V1 migration fails against older previous-channel database schemas
signal.text: ## Summary The V1→V2 migration fails with `SQLiteError: near ",": syntax error` when `opencode-next.db` was created by an older previous-channel build whose `project` or `session` table lacks nullable columns expected by the current importer. The importer reads source rows with `SELECT *` into current TypeScript shapes. Missing properties become `undefined`; raw SQL interpolation emits an empty expression such as `VALUES (..., , ...)`, and the per-session transaction rolls back. Migration remains incomplete and retries on the next server process. This broadens #41341: `fork_boundary` is one affected field, but the compatibility defect applies to every assumed source column added after the source database was created. ## Environment - opencode version: `0.0.0-beta-17519` - OS: macOS arm64; exact Darwin version unavailable from diagnostics - Terminal: Not applicable; observed through packaged Desktop - Shell: Unavailable; diagnostics only report that a login shell environment loaded - Install/channel: Beta - Previous-channel database version: service last registered as `0.0.0-next-16416` - Active plugins: Unavailable from exported diagnostics ## Reproduction 1. Create or retain an `opencode-next.db` from an older V2 build such as `next-16416`. 2. Ensure it contains at least one project and session, and that its schema predates one or more nullable columns expected by the current importer. 3. Start a current V2 server so `V1Migration.layer` runs. 4. Observe that normal schema migrations complete. 5. Observe the background data migration fail with: ```text V1 migration failed SQLiteError: near ",": syntax error ``` 6. Start another server process and observe the incomplete migration retry. ## Expected Behavior The migration should tolerate all supported historical previous-channel schemas: - Existing columns should be copied. - Absent nullable columns should be projected as SQL `NULL`. - Absent required columns should produce a direct compatibility error naming the table and column. - Source values must always be bound safely; `undefined` must never become an empty SQL expression. - Successfully committed sessions should remain idempotent across retries. ## Actual Behavior The importer declares current row shapes containing fields such as: ```text project: icon_url_override icon_color commands session: fork_boundary time_suspended ``` It then reads the old database without adapting its schema: ```ts source.query<NextProject, []>("SELECT * FROM project").all() source.query<NextSession, []>("SELECT * FROM session ORDER BY id DESC").all() ``` For a column absent from the source table, property access returns `undefined`. The destination SQL interpolates those values directly: ```ts sql` INSERT INTO session_v2 (..., fork_session_id, fork_boundary, slug, ...) VALUES (..., ${session.fork_session_id}, ${session.fork_boundary}, ${session.slug}, ...) ` ``` The generated statement can contain: ```sql VALUES (..., value, , value, ...) ``` SQLite rejects it with: ```text SQLiteError: near ",": syntax error ``` The transaction rolls back, including its migration cursor update, so the same input fails again on a later server process. ## Additional Context ### Observed timeline All timestamps UTC: ```text 23:16:52.519 new server process starts 23:16:52.750 normal database migrations begin 23:16:52.771 normal database migrations complete 23:16:54.798 V1 migration fails: SQLiteError near "," ``` The diagnostic window contains one server run and one V1 migration attempt. Client relaunches reused the same server. This rules out concurrent or duplicate migration execution as the cause of this occurrence. The event cleanup is also not the malformed statement. It uses fixed SQL: ```sql DELETE FROM event WHERE rowid IN (SELECT rowid FROM event LIMIT ?) ``` The near-comma failure occurs later, while importing rows from the previous-channel database. ### Static call stack and data flow ```text CLI / Desktop client Service.ensure(currentVersion) starts `opencode-cli serve --service` ServerProcess.start createRoutes Database layer DatabaseMigration.apply normal schema migrations succeed V1Migration.layer forks V1Migration.run read durable `migration.v1-v2` state count/read `<global-data>/opencode-next.db` importNextDatabase SELECT * FROM project SELECT * FROM session source row lacks historical column property read returns undefined tx.run(INSERT INTO project/session_v2) SQL template emits empty value between commas SQLite parser throws transaction rolls back catches cause runtime migration status = error ``` ### Inputs and outputs ```text Input: current destination database older opencode-next.db source table schema source project/session rows Transformation: SELECT * into current TypeScript interface property access for columns not guaranteed by source schema SQL-template interpolation Output: malformed INSERT statement SQLite syntax error rolled-back session import incomplete migration state ``` ### TUI and Desktop behavior Neither UI initiates this migration directly. The server auto-starts it through `V1Migration.layer`. The TUI migration overlay only polls status. Clients may replace a registered service when versions differ, but the observed failure occurs inside one server process and one migration run. ### Related issue - #41341 identifies the same compatibility pattern specifically for a missing `session.fork_boundary`. The implementation should handle the complete historical schema surface rather than special-case that column. ### Suggested fix 1. Inspect each source table with `PRAGMA table_info`. 2. Build an explicit source projection for the supported current shape. 3. Select `NULL AS <column>` for absent nullable fields. 4. Fail early with a named compatibility error for absent required fields. 5. Use bound destination inserts that preserve `null` and reject `undefined` before SQL generation. 6. Add fixtures for multiple historical `project` and `session` schemas, not only the `fork_boundary` variant.
