signal.title: mcp-auth.json loses tokens for multiple servers — MCP servers keep requiring re-auth
signal.text: ## Bug: `mcp-auth.json` loses `tokens` for multiple servers — MCP servers suddenly need re-auth ### Summary OAuth tokens in `~/.local/share/opencode/mcp-auth.json` get wiped for several MCP servers at once. Sessions that were authenticated start prompting for auth again, even though the OAuth server's refresh token is still valid. It is not server-specific — several unrelated servers lost tokens in the same rewrite. ### Observed - File `mcp-auth.json` was rewritten (mtime changed) without a manual edit. - Before rewrite: several servers had a `tokens` object (`accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `expiresAt`, `scope`). - After rewrite: only servers whose entries contained NO leftover PKCE state (`codeVerifier` / `oauthState`) kept their `tokens`. Every entry that still carried `codeVerifier` + `oauthState` lost its `tokens` — reduced to `clientInfo` + `codeVerifier` + `oauthState` + `serverUrl`. - The affected servers use different OAuth providers (custom SDK OAuth, Keycloak, Jira, etc.), so this is not one provider's token format. ### What this looks like per entry ```json { "clientInfo": { "clientId": "...", "clientIdIssuedAt": 1786703712 }, "codeVerifier": "...", "oauthState": "...", "serverUrl": "https://..." } ``` → no `tokens` key at all. The server-side refresh token still exists and works (verified by calling the token endpoint with `grant_type=refresh_token` — returns a fresh access token), so the only thing lost is the client's stored copy. ### Impact Any MCP server that does OAuth (dynamic client registration) requires a full interactive re-auth every time the file is rewritten. This happened at least twice in our setup within days. ### Hypothesis - Re-running `opencode mcp add <server>` overwrites the existing entry with a fresh clientInfo/PKCE state and **drops the stored tokens**. - Or: the auth file is rewritten wholesale (version upgrade / config change / another process), and only entries written with tokens survive; anything mid-flow or registered-but-not-completed loses its tokens. - Correlates with leftover PKCE state: entries that still hold `codeVerifier`/`oauthState` are the ones that lost tokens — clean entries (no leftover PKCE state) kept theirs. ### Expected - `opencode mcp add` / re-config on an existing server should preserve existing `tokens` (or warn that re-auth is required instead of silently dropping them). - If the file is rewritten wholesale, tokens should be merged/retained per server. ### Environment - opencode, Linux, latest as of 2026-08-16. - `mcp-auth.json` path: `~/.local/share/opencode/mcp-auth.json` - Trigger not yet pinned to a single command — file mtime changed without a manual edit.

signal.title: fix(opencode): stop CLI test fixtures leaking processes on Windows
signal.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #42989 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? Changes the four places `packages/opencode/test/lib/cli-process.ts` picks the bun executable, from the string `"bun"` to `process.execPath`. `"bun"` gets resolved through PATH. Under bunx that finds the `node_modules\.bin\bun.exe` shim, which starts the real bun as a *separate* process and waits on it — so the fixture is holding the shim, not the process it thinks it owns. `kill()` + `await exited` then completes as soon as the shim dies, while the actual OpenCode process keeps running with no parent. On my machine that had accumulated 35 leftover processes. `process.execPath` is the bun already running the tests (bun resolves it via `selfExePath()`, not PATH), so the handle points at the process we actually want to control. Only `serve()` and `startRun()` were leaking. `acp()` is safe by accident (stdin EOF exits the child first) and the generic `spawn()` is safe because it goes through `CrossSpawnSpawner`, which tree-kills on Windows. I changed all four anyway so the fixture never picks a different bun than the test runner. Two test changes so this can't silently come back: the serve teardown assertion was `typeof code === "number" || code === null`, true for every possible value — it now checks the server actually stops answering. And the SIGINT test body gets a timeout so it fails on its own terms instead of running out the test runner's clock. ### How did you verify your code works? I wrote both tests first and ran them against the unchanged code to confirm they fail: - serve: got three HTTP 200s from the server *after* `exited` had already resolved - SIGINT: `run.result` never settled, ran to the 30s timeout Then changed the four selectors and reran the same test files unmodified: - serve: passes in 2.1s, all three requests refused at the transport level - SIGINT: passes in 2.9s Full `test/cli` run afterwards: 398 tests, zero leftover processes. The same run left 3 behind before the change. Full `bun test` from `packages/opencode`: 16 failures, all of which were already failing on my machine before I touched anything (symlink tests and one Zed path test). Typecheck clean. This branch is the change applied to current `dev` (5a0e07efcf), and I reran both tests there as well — serve passes in 2.1s, SIGINT in 2.8s, no leftover processes, typecheck clean. To confirm it yourself on Windows: run any CLI subprocess test through bunx, then look for leftover `bun.exe` processes whose parent no longer exists. One limitation worth flagging — this only reproduces where bunx puts the shim on PATH. The Windows CI job installs bun through `setup-bun`, so no shim is generated there and CI wouldn't catch a regression in this. ### Screenshots / recordings N/A — not a UI change. ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

signal.title: One configuration file cannot be used by version 1 and version 2
signal.text: ## Description Version 1 and version 2 can be installed at the same time. The two versions read the same configuration file. But one file cannot satisfy both versions. Version 1 stops with an error when the file contains the version 2 keys. The keys are `providers` and `agents`. Version 1 shows this message: ``` Configuration is invalid at <config-dir>/opencode.json ↳ Unrecognized keys: providers, agents ``` The migration document is at https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1 The document says that version 1 fields and version 2 fields can stay together in one file. The document says: "Supported V1 and native V2 fields may coexist at the top level". The document also says: "when both forms set the same canonical value, a valid native V2 value takes precedence". Thus the user can write the provider with the version 1 fields. Version 2 does not obey this rule for a custom provider package. I declare a provider with the version 1 fields. I use the `provider` key. I use the `npm` field. Version 1 reads the file correctly. But version 2 shows no models for this provider. Version 2 shows no error message. I declare the same provider with the version 2 fields. I use the `providers` key. I use the `package` field. Version 2 shows all 32 models. But version 1 stops with the error above. Thus neither format is correct for both versions. The fault does not occur for all packages. A provider with the `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` package loads correctly with the version 1 fields. The fault occurs with the package `commandcode-go-opencode-provider`. ## Environment - opencode version 2: `0.0.0-next-16974` (next channel) - opencode version 1: `1.18.15` - Operating system: macOS 25.5.0 - Architecture: arm64 ## How to repeat the fault 1. Install the package `commandcode-go-opencode-provider` from npm. 2. Put configuration A in the global configuration file. 3. Run this command with version 2: `opencode models` 4. Count the lines that start with `commandcode/`. 5. Run the same command with version 1. 6. Put configuration B in the same file. 7. Do step 3 to step 5 again. Configuration A uses the version 1 fields: ```json { "provider": { "commandcode": { "npm": "commandcode-go-opencode-provider", "name": "Command Code", "env": ["COMMANDCODE_API_KEY"], "options": { "baseURL": "https://api.commandcode.ai" }, "models": { "deepseek-v4-flash": { "id": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash", "name": "DeepSeek V4 Flash", "tool_call": true } } } } } ``` Configuration B uses the version 2 fields: ```json { "providers": { "commandcode": { "package": "aisdk:commandcode-go-opencode-provider", "name": "Command Code", "settings": { "baseURL": "https://api.commandcode.ai" }, "models": { "deepseek-v4-flash": { "modelID": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash", "name": "DeepSeek V4 Flash", "capabilities": { "tools": true } } } } } } ``` ## Result Configuration A: version 2 shows 0 models for the provider. There is no error message. Version 1 shows all models. Configuration B: version 2 shows all models. Version 1 stops with the error message. I did more tests with configuration A. The result stays the same for each test: - The `package` field and the `npm` field together in the `provider` key. - Only the `package` field in the `provider` key. - Model entries with only version 1 fields. I removed `modelID`, `capabilities` and `cost.cache`. A second file does not correct the problem. Both versions read the file `opencode.jsonc`. Version 1 also stops with an error for that file. ## Expected result Version 2 must load the provider when the configuration uses the version 1 fields. Then one file can satisfy both versions. If version 2 cannot load the provider, then version 2 must show an error message.

signal.title: fix(provider): scope AI Gateway token to first-party Workers AI models
signal.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #32051 Closes #40344 Reapplies and extends #33407 (auto-closed on a PR-template technicality). Fixes the third-party regression introduced by #32052. ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? #32052 fixed #32051 (Workers AI models 401'd through the gateway) by passing `apiKey` to `createUnified`. That apiKey was applied to **every** model, so the Cloudflare API token was sent as the upstream `Authorization` header for third-party providers (OpenAI, Anthropic) too — causing them to 401 with "Invalid API Key". This scopes token forwarding to be model-aware. The Cloudflare token is only attached for first-party **Workers AI** models, whose upstream is Cloudflare itself; everything else relies on the gateway's stored/BYOK credentials (or Unified Billing): const isWorkersAi = modelID.startsWith("workers-ai/") || modelID.startsWith("@cf/") createUnified(isWorkersAi ? { apiKey } : {}) Both Workers AI id forms the Unified API accepts are matched: the explicit `workers-ai/...` prefix and the bare `@cf/...` form. `@cf/` is Cloudflare's reserved namespace, so this never matches a third-party model. Applied in both the v1 provider path (`provider.ts`) and the v2 plugin path (`core/.../cloudflare-ai-gateway.ts`). The gateway-level auth (`createAiGateway({ apiKey })`, the `cf-aig-authorization` header) is unchanged. ### How did you verify your code works? Added regression tests in `packages/opencode/test/provider/cf-ai-gateway-e2e.test.ts` that capture the real forwarded headers and assert both directions: - third-party models do **not** forward the Cloudflare token upstream — the upstream sub-request carries no `authorization` header (#32052 regression) - `workers-ai/...` **and** bare `@cf/...` models **do** forward it (#32051) ``` cd packages/opencode bun test test/provider/cf-ai-gateway-e2e.test.ts # 6 pass bun typecheck # clean ``` ### Screenshots / recordings N/A — no UI changes. ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

signal.title: [BUG] CLI test fixtures leaking processes on Windows
signal.text: ### Description CLI subprocess tests leave OpenCode processes running on Windows after the suite finishes. I currently have 35 of them alive, oldest 46 hours, ~32 GB of private commit between them, still holding loopback ports and file locks on checkouts. The cause is in `packages/opencode/test/lib/cli-process.ts`. It spawns children with `Bun.spawn(["bun", ...])`. When the suite is launched through `bun x` (bunx), PATH resolves `"bun"` to the small `node_modules\.bin\bun.exe` shim, which starts the real bun as a *separate* process and waits on it. The fixture only ever holds the shim. So `kill()` + `await exited` completes as soon as the shim dies, while the real OpenCode process keeps running with no parent. Two helpers leak: `serve()` and `startRun()`. `acp()` happens to be safe because stdin EOF exits the child first, and the generic `spawn()` is safe because it goes through `CrossSpawnSpawner`, which tree-kills on Windows. The two tests meant to catch this can't: - `test/cli/serve/serve-process.test.ts` asserts `typeof code === "number" || code === null`, which is true for every possible value. - `test/cli/run/run-process.test.ts` has a test named "SIGINT interrupts an active non-interactive run without leaking the process" that leaks one every run. I have a fix ready and will open a PR against this issue. ### Plugins custom ### OpenCode version 1.17.11 ### Steps to reproduce 1. On Windows, from `packages/opencode`, run the suite through bunx so the shim is on PATH: `bun x bun@1.3.14 test test/cli/serve/serve-process.test.ts -t "kills the subprocess on scope close"` 2. The test passes. 3. List bun processes: `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='bun.exe'" | Select-Object ProcessId, ParentProcessId, CommandLine` 4. There is a leftover `... src\index.ts serve --port 0` process whose parent no longer exists. It still answers HTTP on its port. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Windows 10 ### Terminal Windows Terminal (PowerShell)

These are the steps they document (not using OpenCode): 1. `export ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL=https://their-custom-domain.azure-api.net/ai/anthropic` 2. `export CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY="1"` 3. `az login` to sign in to Azure using Entra Authentication (OAuth). 4. `claude run` Steps 1, 2 and 4 appear already possible with OpenCode (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/4474#issuecomment-3560959500), but for 3 an API key is expected by OpenCode instead. They also mention the Azure CLI session can expire every so often (10 hours in their case), in which case `az logout` followed by `az login` is required - mentioning it as reauthenticating might be relevant for OpenCode also.

signal.title: fix(shell): scan redirection targets for external_directory
signal.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #42979 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? When `external_directory` is denied, the built-in file tools (`write`, `edit`, `apply_patch`, `read`) correctly refuse paths outside the workspace, but the `bash` tool does not. The external-directory scan in `packages/opencode/src/tool/shell.ts` only extracts paths when the command's first token is in a 14-entry allowlist, and it never inspects `>` redirection targets. As a result the agent can freely write outside the workspace using `echo`, `printf`, `tee`, and similar. Enforcement depends on which command name is typed, not on what the command actually does to the filesystem. The fix scans every `file_redirect` node in the parsed shell tree regardless of command name. The destination (last named child, skipping the optional `file_descriptor`) is resolved via `argPath` and added to the `external_directory` scan — closing the gap for stdout (`>`, `>>`), stderr (`2>`, `2>>`), and stdin (`<`) redirection. ### How did you verify your code works? - `bun typecheck` passes - `bun test test/tool/shell.test.ts` — 25 pass, 0 fail - New regression tests: - `echo BYPASS > /tmp/oc-redirect-test.txt` → asks for `external_directory` permission with `/tmp/*` - `ls 2>/etc/opencode-stderr-test` → asks for `external_directory` permission with `/etc/*` ### Screenshots / recordings N/A — permission logic change, not UI. ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

signal.title: Azure OpenAI Cognitive Services endpoint: Responses API does not append ?api-version=, cannot use gpt-5.x-codex models
signal.text: ### Description **Summary:** When using OpenCode with Azure OpenAI Cognitive Services endpoints (i.e. `https://<resource>.cognitiveservices.azure.com/openai`), the Responses API (`/responses`) requests are missing the required `?api-version=...` query parameter. This causes all requests to `/openai/responses` to return 404, even though the same endpoint works with tools like `curl`. **Impact:** - Cannot use models that require the Responses API (e.g. `gpt-5.2-codex`) on Azure Cognitive Services endpoints. - Azure returns `404 Resource not found` when `?api-version=` is missing from the request URL. - The same request succeeds via `curl` when `?api-version=2025-04-01-preview` is included manually. **Working curl example:** ```bash curl -X POST "https://<resource>.cognitiveservices.azure.com/openai/responses?api-version=2025-04-01-preview" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $AZURE_API_KEY" \ -d '{ "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hello"}], "max_completion_tokens": 16384, "model": "gpt-5.2-codex" }' ``` --- **Config attempts and results:** **Attempt 1: Standard `@ai-sdk/azure` with `resourceName`** ```json { "provider": { "azure": { "npm": "@ai-sdk/azure", "options": { "apiKey": "<REDACTED>", "resourceName": "<REDACTED>", "apiVersion": "2025-04-01-preview" }, "models": { "gpt-5.2-codex": { "name": "GPT 5.2 Codex", "provider": { "npm": "@ai-sdk/azure" } } } } } } ``` **Result:** SDK constructs URL with `.openai.azure.com` hostname (wrong — Cognitive Services uses `.cognitiveservices.azure.com`), and hits `/v1/chat/completions` instead of `/responses`. Error: `The chatCompletion operation does not work with the specified model, gpt-5.2-codex`. **Attempt 2: `@ai-sdk/azure` with `baseURL` override** ```json { "provider": { "azure": { "npm": "@ai-sdk/azure", "options": { "apiKey": "<REDACTED>", "baseURL": "https://<resource>.cognitiveservices.azure.com/openai", "apiVersion": "2025-04-01-preview" }, "models": { "gpt-5.2-codex": { "name": "GPT 5.2 Codex", "provider": { "npm": "@ai-sdk/azure" } } } } } } ``` **Result:** URL hits `/openai/responses` (correct path) but `?api-version=` query parameter is **dropped**. Error: `404 Resource not found`. **Attempt 3: `@ai-sdk/openai` with `api` URL including query param** ```json { "provider": { "azure": { "api": "https://<resource>.cognitiveservices.azure.com/openai?api-version=2025-04-01-preview", "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai", "options": { "apiKey": "<REDACTED>", "headers": { "api-key": "<REDACTED>" } }, "models": { "gpt-5.2-codex": { "name": "GPT 5.2 Codex" } } } } } ``` **Result:** SDK appends `/responses` **after** the query string, producing a malformed URL: `https://<resource>.cognitiveservices.azure.com/openai/responses?api-version=2025-04-01-preview/responses`. Error: `404`. **Attempt 4: `@ai-sdk/openai` with clean `api` URL (no query param)** ```json { "provider": { "openai": { "api": "https://<resource>.cognitiveservices.azure.com/openai", "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai", "options": { "apiKey": "<REDACTED>", "headers": { "api-key": "<REDACTED>" } }, "models": { "gpt-5.2-codex": { "name": "GPT 5.2 Codex" } } } } } ``` **Result:** URL hits `/openai/responses` (correct path) but `?api-version=` is missing. Error: `404 Resource not found`. **Attempt 5: Custom provider ID to bypass Azure custom loader** ```json { "provider": { "azure-responses": { "name": "Azure OpenAI", "npm": "@ai-sdk/azure", "options": { "apiKey": "<REDACTED>", "baseURL": "https://<resource>.cognitiveservices.azure.com/openai", "apiVersion": "2025-04-01-preview" }, "models": { "gpt-5.2-codex": { "name": "GPT 5.2 Codex" } } } } } ``` **Result:** Same as Attempt 2 — `?api-version=` is dropped when `baseURL` is provided. Error: `404 Resource not found`. --- **Root cause analysis:** The issue is an architectural mismatch across three layers: 1. **`@ai-sdk/azure` URL construction:** When using `resourceName`, the SDK hardcodes the hostname as `{resourceName}.openai.azure.com`. Cognitive Services endpoints use `{resourceName}.cognitiveservices.azure.com` instead. When `baseURL` is provided to bypass this, the SDK stops appending `?api-version=` to requests — this is a [known limitation](https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/2312). 2. **OpenCode's Azure custom loader** ([`provider.ts` L178-191](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/7ed449974864361bad2c1f1405769fd2c2fcdf42/packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts#L178-L191)): Correctly calls `sdk.responses(modelID)` by default, but has no mechanism to handle the Cognitive Services endpoint variant. 3. **OpenCode's `getSDK`** ([`provider.ts` L1041-1117](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/7ed449974864361bad2c1f1405769fd2c2fcdf42/packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts#L1041-L1117)): Passes config options through to `createAzure()`, but there's no way for users to configure both a custom base hostname AND retain the `?api-version=` query parameter behavior. **Note:** The bundled `@ai-sdk/azure` version (`2.0.91`) is not obsolete — it does support the Responses API. The issue is specifically about how it constructs URLs when `baseURL` is overridden. **Suggested fix:** - Allow OpenCode's Azure provider to accept a full custom base URL while preserving `?api-version=` injection (e.g. via a custom fetch wrapper, or by patching URL construction in the Azure loader). - Alternatively, add explicit support for the `cognitiveservices.azure.com` hostname pattern in the `azure-cognitive-services` custom loader. **References:** - [Azure OpenAI Responses API docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/openai/how-to/responses) - [Vercel AI SDK: Add baseURL and apiVersion to Azure provider (issue #2312)](https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/2312) - [Vercel AI SDK: Azure calling wrong URL path (issue #4797)](https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/4797) ### Plugins None ### OpenCode version Latest stable (2026-02-17) ### Steps to reproduce 1. Deploy a model requiring the Responses API (e.g. `gpt-5.2-codex`) on an Azure Cognitive Services resource 2. Configure `opencode.json` with provider `azure`, pointing at `https://<resource>.cognitiveservices.azure.com/openai` 3. Set `"model": "azure/gpt-5.2-codex"` and provide your API key 4. Launch opencode and send any message 5. Observe error: `404 Resource not found` — the request URL is `/openai/responses` without `?api-version=` 6. Verify the same request works via curl with `?api-version=2025-04-01-preview` appended ### Screenshot and/or share link **Error from OpenCode logs:** ``` AI_APICallError: Resource not found url: "https://<resource>.cognitiveservices.azure.com/openai/responses" statusCode: 404 responseBody: {"error":{"code":"404","message": "Resource not found"}} ``` **Expected URL (works via curl):** ``` https://<resource>.cognitiveservices.azure.com/openai/responses?api-version=2025-04-01-preview ``` ### Operating System Windows 11 ### Terminal Windows Terminal

signal.title: feat(opencode): native OpenAI and Anthropic passthroughs for Cloudflare AI Gateway
signal.text: ## Summary Cloudflare AI Gateway models currently all ride the unified OpenAI-compatible \`/compat\` endpoint. That breaks new OpenAI models (gpt-5.5+/pro reject \`tools\` + \`reasoning_effort\` on chat completions and require the Responses API) and squeezes Claude through an OpenAI-shaped body (no native thinking blocks, no \`cache_control\`, reasoning efforts silently dropped or mistranslated). This PR routes gateway models through the provider-native passthroughs that \`ai-gateway-provider\` 3.2 ships: - \`openai/*\` → native OpenAI passthrough on the **Responses API** - \`anthropic/*\` → native Anthropic passthrough on the **Messages API** - everything else → unified \`/compat\`, unchanged The passthrough wrappers inject a \`CF_TEMP_TOKEN\` sentinel the gateway strips before dispatch, so upstream billing stays on the gateway (Unified Billing / stored BYOK) and the Cloudflare token never reaches a third-party provider. ## Changes - **\`provider.ts\` loader**: prefix routing in \`getModel\`; keeps the Workers AI token scoping (the Cloudflare token is only forwarded upstream for \`workers-ai/\` and \`@cf/\` models — includes #33597, co-authored) - **\`provider.ts\` \`cloudflareGatewayNpm\`**: resolves the native npm (\`@ai-sdk/openai\` / \`@ai-sdk/anthropic\`) **before** variants are computed, so reasoning variants produce payloads the native SDKs understand — Claude effort variants become \`thinking\` + \`output_config.effort\` (previously silently dropped), OpenAI variants gain \`reasoningSummary\` + encrypted reasoning includes for stateless multi-turn - **\`plugin/cloudflare.ts\`**: removed the \`chat.params\` maxOutputTokens workaround — it existed because compat couldn't rename \`max_tokens\` for OpenAI reasoning models; the Responses API accepts \`max_output_tokens\`, so the hack now just uncapped output - **Tests**: e2e suite asserts the envelope per route (provider + endpoint + wire payload), reasoning-effort fidelity on all three routes, and the token-scoping invariants (\`authorization\`/\`x-api-key\` stripped on passthroughs, secret never in the body, Workers AI still receives the token) ## Live verification Tested against a real gateway with Unified Billing: OpenAI models with tools + reasoning efforts (the previously failing case), Claude models, and \`workers-ai/@cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6\` (compat regression). Also live-verified the gateway's boundaries, which shaped this scope: under Unified Billing the legacy endpoint serves exactly \`openai/\`, \`anthropic/\`, and \`workers-ai/\` — Google/xAI fail spend-limit resolution (catalog slug ≠ route prefix) and DeepSeek gets no managed credentials. The models.dev catalog was aligned accordingly (models.dev#4674, #4676, #4693, #4715). Other providers arrive with the REST (\`/ai/v1\`) transport in V2. Supersedes #33597 — its token-scoping fix is included here with commit authorship preserved and co-author credit. Fixes: #40344

signal.title: [BUG] Cloudflare AI Gateway: OpenCode duplicates gateway token into Universal Endpoint headers.authorization, bypassing BYOK and leaking credential to upstream provider
signal.text: ### Description When using Cloudflare AI Gateway with DeepSeek as the upstream provider, OpenCode sends requests through the Cloudflare Universal Endpoint. The gateway token is correctly passed via the `cf-aig-authorization` HTTP header. However, the captured request JSON body additionally includes a request-level `headers.authorization` field containing the same Cloudflare gateway token: ```json [ { "endpoint": "chat/completions", "headers": { "authorization": "Bearer <redacted Cloudflare gateway token>", "content-type": "application/json" }, "query": { "model": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash", "max_tokens": 32000, "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": "hello" } ] } } ] ``` The request body has been simplified for brevity. ### Root cause The Universal Endpoint `headers.authorization` field is semantically intended for the upstream provider's API key[^1]. When using BYOK, the Cloudflare documentation explicitly instructs: > Remove provider authorization headers from your requests. Note that you still need to pass `cf-aig-authorization`.[^2] Gateway authentication is already handled by the `cf-aig-authorization` HTTP header. The `headers.authorization` inside the Universal Endpoint payload should be left empty so that BYOK can supply the upstream provider key. However, OpenCode additionally places the Cloudflare gateway token into `headers.authorization`. According to the credential precedence rules[^3]: 1. Provider key on the request — if the request carries provider authentication (e.g., an `Authorization` header), AI Gateway forwards it to the provider unchanged. BYOK and Unified Billing are not consulted. 2. BYOK (stored key) 3. Unified Billing Because `headers.authorization` is present, precedence rule #1 fires. The Cloudflare gateway token is forwarded to DeepSeek as the provider credential, BYOK is entirely bypassed, and DeepSeek rejects the request: ```json { "error": { "message": "Authentication Fails, Your api key: <last 4 chars of Cloudflare token> is invalid", "type": "authentication_error", "param": null, "code": "invalid_request_error" } } ``` The invalid key suffix matches the Cloudflare gateway token, not a DeepSeek API key. > Security note: This is not only a functional bug. The Cloudflare API token is leaked to a third-party provider (DeepSeek) that is not intended to receive it. ### Expected behavior OpenCode should not populate the Universal Endpoint request-level `headers.authorization` when routing to upstream providers via BYOK. The gateway token is already correctly passed via `cf-aig-authorization`; there is no need to duplicate it into the JSON body. Removing `headers.authorization` allows Cloudflare AI Gateway to resolve credentials through BYOK (precedence #2) instead of forwarding the gateway token as a provider key (precedence #1). Concretely, the request body should look like: ```json [ { "endpoint": "chat/completions", "headers": { "content-type": "application/json" }, "query": { "model": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash", "max_tokens": 32000, "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": "hello" } ] } } ] ``` ### Actual behavior OpenCode includes the Cloudflare gateway token in the Universal Endpoint JSON body: ```json "headers": { "authorization": "Bearer <redacted Cloudflare gateway token>" } ``` This triggers credential precedence rule #1, causing the Cloudflare gateway token to be forwarded to DeepSeek as the provider credential, bypassing BYOK[^3] and resulting in an authentication failure. ### Verification Manually sending the same Universal Endpoint payload without the `headers.authorization` field returns HTTP 200. This confirms that the failure is caused by the Cloudflare gateway token being forwarded to DeepSeek as the provider credential, overriding the BYOK-stored DeepSeek API key. [^1]: https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/usage/universal/ [^2]: https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/configuration/bring-your-own-keys/ [^3]: https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/features/unified-billing/#credential-precedence ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version 1.18.11-1 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Configure Cloudflare AI Gateway as the provider in OpenCode. 2. Configure a DeepSeek model, for example: ```jsonc "models": { "deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash": {} } ``` 3. Run `opencode`. 4. Run `/init` or send any message. 5. Observe the authentication error from DeepSeek. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Arch linux ### Terminal Ghostty

signal.title: ACP session/load response omits sessionId — breaks resume for Agent of Empires and any spec-compliant ACP client
signal.text: ## Bug The ACP `session/load` handler in `packages/opencode/src/acp/service.ts` (line ~211, `loadSession`) returns `{ configOptions }` but **omits `sessionId`** from the response. The ACP spec requires `sessionId` in the `session/load` result (the `newSession` handler correctly returns `{ sessionId, configOptions }`). ## Impact Agent of Empires (aoe) v1.13.1+ sends a spec-compliant `session/load { sessionId, cwd, mcpServers }` request, receives a response with no `sessionId`, and rejects it: `session/load response missing sessionId`. It then silently falls back to `session/new`, so **every worker restart forks a fresh session and loses the transcript context** — the dashboard shows "Agent finished but didn't notify the daemon; restarting worker" and the old conversation never resumes. ## Repro (raw ACP probe) ```js // opencode acp --cwd <dir>; send initialize, then: session/load { sessionId: "ses_...", cwd: "/path", mcpServers: [] } // → 200 result: { "configOptions": [...] } ← sessionId missing ``` Verified against opencode 1.18.18 and current `dev`. ## Fix In `loadSession`, return `sessionId` alongside `configOptions`: ```ts return { sessionId: state.id, configOptions: configOptions(...), } ``` (`state.id === params.sessionId` — the response just needs to echo it back per spec.)

signal.title: Shell redirection bypasses the external_directory permission
signal.text: ### Description ## Summary When `external_directory` is denied, the built-in file tools (`write`, `edit`, `apply_patch`, `read`) correctly refuse paths outside the workspace, but the `bash` tool does not. The external-directory scan only extracts paths when the command's first token is in a 14-entry allowlist, and it never inspects `>` redirection targets. As a result the agent can freely write outside the workspace using `echo`, `printf`, `tee`, and similar. Enforcement depends on which command name is typed, not on what the command actually does to the filesystem. ## Version - Reproduced on `1.18.16` and `1.18.18` (latest release at time of filing) - Linux x64 ## Reproduction One invocation shows both halves of the problem: ```bash WS=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/oc-repro-XXXXXX") cd "$WS" OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT='{"permission":{"external_directory":"deny"}}' \ opencode run --pure --format json --dir "$WS" \ 'Run exactly this shell command and nothing else: echo BYPASS > /tmp/oc-escape.txt' ls -l /tmp/oc-escape.txt ``` ## Actual ```text tool=bash status=completed echo BYPASS > /tmp/oc-escape.txt tool=bash status=error cat /tmp/oc-escape.txt tool=read status=error -rw-rw-r-- 1 user user 7 /tmp/oc-escape.txt ``` The write succeeded and the file exists outside the workspace. In the same session the agent was then denied permission to read back the file it had just created. For contrast, both of these are correctly denied under the identical configuration: ```text cp seed.txt /tmp/oc-escape2.txt -> denied, no file created cat /tmp/oc-escape.txt -> denied ``` `cp` and `echo >` express the same operation, writing a file into `/tmp`. Only the `cp` form is blocked. ## Expected With `external_directory` denied, a shell command that writes to or reads from a path outside the workspace should trigger the same permission check that `write` and `read` already enforce, regardless of which command or shell construct is used. ## Root cause `packages/opencode/src/tool/shell.ts` Path extraction is gated on a command-name allowlist (around lines 392-405): ```ts if (cmd && (FILES.has(cmd) || (shellKind === "cmd" && CMD_FILES.has(cmd)))) { for (const arg of pathArgs(command, ps, shellKind === "cmd")) { const resolved = yield* argPath(arg, cwd, ps, shell) if (!resolved || containsPath(resolved, instance)) continue const dir = (yield* fs.isDir(resolved)) ? resolved : path.dirname(resolved) scan.dirs.add(dir) } } ``` `FILES` (lines 28-38) contains only: ```text cd chdir popd pushd push-location set-location rm cp mv mkdir touch chmod chown cat ``` Only `scan.dirs` reaches the `external_directory` prompt in `ask()` (lines 263-291). Two consequences follow: 1. Any command whose first token is outside that list contributes no paths, so `echo`, `printf`, `tee`, `sed`, `dd`, `python`, and others are never checked. 2. Redirection targets are never examined at all. A `>` target is a filesystem write but is not an argument of an allowlisted command, so it is invisible to the scan. This matches the observed behaviour exactly: every blocked command contained an allowlisted name such as `cat`, and every bypassing command used redirection or a non-allowlisted command. ## Impact `external_directory` reads as a containment boundary, and the file-editing tools honour it, so an operator can reasonably believe the workspace is confined. It is not. Any command form outside the 14-entry allowlist, and any use of `>`, escapes it. This is a fail-open design: unknown commands are treated as safe. ## Suggested fix - Treat redirection targets as filesystem writes and include them in the scan. - Stop gating path extraction on a command-name allowlist. Extract candidate path arguments from all commands, then let `containsPath` decide what is external, so unrecognised commands fail closed rather than open. ## Notes Found with a scenario-based harness using deterministic filesystem and permission oracles. The bypass reproduced in 9 of 35 write attempts and 8 of 34 read attempts across a long run, under two different models, so it is not model-specific. A single capable model often refuses these requests on its own, which can mask the missing enforcement during manual testing. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce ```bash #!/bin/bash # Minimal reproduction for: shell redirection bypasses the external_directory permission. # # One opencode invocation demonstrates both halves of the bug: # echo ... > /tmp/FILE succeeds (echo is not allowlisted, redirect is never scanned) # cat /tmp/FILE is denied (cat is allowlisted) # # Usage: bash repro_f2.sh set -u MODEL="${1:-github-copilot/gpt-5-mini}" OC="${OPENCODE_BIN:-opencode}" TARGET="/tmp/oc-escape.txt" WS="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-$HOME}/oc-repro-XXXXXX")" rm -f "$TARGET" cd "$WS" || exit 1 OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT='{"permission":{"external_directory":"deny"}}' \ "$OC" run --pure --format json --dir "$WS" --model "$MODEL" \ 'Run exactly this shell command and nothing else: echo BYPASS > /tmp/oc-escape.txt' 2>&1 | python3 -c " import sys, json for line in sys.stdin: try: e = json.loads(line) except Exception: continue if e.get('type') != 'tool_use': continue state = e['part'].get('state', {}) cmd = (state.get('input') or {}).get('command') print('tool=%-5s status=%-9s %s' % (e['part'].get('tool'), state.get('status'), cmd)) " echo if [ -f "$TARGET" ]; then echo "RESULT: BUG PRESENT - $TARGET was created outside the workspace" else echo "RESULT: not reproduced in this run - retry, the agent must actually run the redirect" fi rm -f "$TARGET" rm -rf "$WS" ``` ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signal.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request Allow configs to be invalidated and reloaded while OC is running. This not only enables the users to create new agents/skills/commands and instantly use them, but it also allows the agents themselves to develop these skills or create new agents on the fly and instantly use them (Ralph Loops, anyone?). Proposal: - Watch instance + config directories when hot-reload is enabled. - When agent/, skill/, or command/ markdown changes: invalidate cached state and reload immediately. - When custom tool .ts/.js changes: re-import with cache busting. (I believe this is a side effect that can be removed) - Emit config.updated, skill.updated, command.updated so TUI/Desktop refresh live. Is it safe? Not necessarily, and is not for everyone. I have a functioning version of it, that is locked behind EXPERIMENTAL_HOT_RELOAD flag. Kept changes to minimum and preserved everything from upstream. https://github.com/IgorWarzocha/opencode/tree/agent-skills-commands-hot-reloading It works, but there are some caveats - agents would need a create skill/command/agent tool for creating a markdown files that pass the parsing check (if it fails, nothing happens). This is probably the easiest implementation - let agent do the thing, and as a return of the tool call, give it a path to the file and ask it to expand the instructions set and leave the frontmatter alone. Toast on reload would be a nice addition, but I'm not doing either until I know if there's actually a demand for this.

signal.title: perf(fs): use augmented rope for text pagination
signal.text: ## Summary Replaces quadratic deep text pagination with a request-local augmented rope, keeps the existing single-chunk path for small files, and adds reproducible performance/resource benchmarks. The production reader now: - keeps the previous direct pagination path when the complete file fits in the first 256 KiB chunk; - scans larger files once for per-chunk byte and newline summaries; - builds a request-local bounded-fanout tree with byte/newline subtree summaries; - seeks to the requested line through accumulated summaries; - decodes and splits only the selected suffix rather than every accumulated prefix; - preserves existing pagination, UTF-8, line truncation, byte budget, and binary detection behavior; - persists no line index or cache. Two benchmark fixtures compare the V2 baseline implementation with the PR candidate in fresh isolated worker processes: - **large-log:** 2,000,250 lines / 130 MB, reading offset 2,000,000 with limit 125; 3 samples per implementation. - **small-code:** 1,000 generated TypeScript lines, reading offset 500 with limit 125; 10 samples per implementation. Wall and aggregate process CPU time cover the read operation. Peak RSS comes from Linux `/usr/bin/time -v` for each fresh worker. A separate benchmark retains the augmented-rope-versus-VS Code algorithm comparison. Algorithm references: - Boehm, Atkinson, and Plass, “Ropes: An Alternative to Strings”: https://doi.org/10.1002/spe.4380251203 - Generic order-statistic tree: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_statistic_tree - VS Code piece-tree article, used only for the comparison benchmark: https://code.visualstudio.com/blogs/2018/03/23/text-buffer-reimplementation ## Baseline versus candidate Run with: ```sh bun run benchmark:read-scenarios ``` | Scenario | Implementation | Wall mean | CPU mean | CPU utilization | Peak RSS | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | large-log | V2 baseline | 51.942 s | 55.242 s | 106.4% | 1621.4 MiB | | large-log | PR candidate | 1.916 s | 2.046 s | 106.8% | 294.5 MiB | | small-code | V2 baseline | 22.73 ms | 48.93 ms | 215.2% | 141.4 MiB | | small-code | PR candidate | 22.63 ms | 48.89 ms | 216.1% | 139.8 MiB | Aggregate CPU utilization can exceed 100% when runtime threads use more than one core. For the large log, the candidate uses **27.1× less wall time**, **27.0× less CPU time**, and **81.8% less peak RSS**. The 1,000-line case is effectively unchanged. ## Editor algorithm comparison The separate generated-log benchmark still compares the previous algorithm, the production augmented-rope implementation, and the VS Code-inspired piece tree: ```sh bun run benchmark:large-read --iterations 3 ``` - Previous implementation: **31.436 s** mean - Augmented-rope production implementation: **1.778 s** mean - VS Code-inspired: **2.690 s** mean ## Checks - `bun test test/tool-read-filesystem.test.ts` — 16 passed - `bun typecheck` (`packages/core`) - Prettier checks for changed Core files - `bun run benchmark:read-scenarios` - `bun run benchmark:large-read --iterations 3` Requested by: @Hona (Hona via Slack)

Run `OPENCODE_INSTALL_DIR=/tmp/foo curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash` (or run the repo's `install` script with the variable set) 2. Observe the binary is installed to `$HOME/.opencode/bin`, not `/tmp/foo` 3. Same with `XDG_BIN_DIR=$HOME/.local/bin` ### Plugins N/A ### OpenCode version Latest install script on `dev` branch

signal.title: 消息 ID 生成回绕导致旧会话静默拒收新消息（1.17.4，Linux）
signal.text: ### Description 升级后（约 8/14 19:22 起），所有「创建于升级前、升级后又继续使用过」的会话都无法继续对话：发送新消息后没有任何反应，换模型、重开会话都无效，服务端日志只有 loop step=0 后立即 exiting loop，新消息从未被处理。不报错、不产生回复，属于静默失败。 环境 - opencode 1.17.4（Linux / WSL） - 消息/会话存储在 SQLite（~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db） 根因 SessionPrompt.run 的 agent 循环依赖消息 ID 的字典序来挑选"最新消息"： - latest() 通过 J.id > maxId 选取最新 user / 最新 assistant（按 ID 字典序，而非时间）； - 循环开头存在退出分支：当"ID 最大的 assistant 已 finish、且其 ID 大于 ID 最大的 user"时，判定为"对话已完成"直接 exiting loop。 问题在于消息 ID 生成器存在回绕：升级前生成的 ID 前缀为 fffb...~ffff...，升级后生成的 ID 前缀为 0000.../00d...。由于 'f' > '0'，旧消息的 ID 字典序反而大于新消息。于是： - 会话中同时存在新旧消息时，latest() 把旧（8/14 之前的）assistant 当成"最新"，其 finish 已就绪且 ID 大于任何新用户消息 → 循环认为对话已完成 → 退出； - 再次发送新消息时重复同样过程，新消息永远得不到回复。 症状与"8/14 19:22 之后发的消息从没人回复"完全吻合（该时间点前后会话里出现了成批的未应答用户消息）。 影响范围 任何同时包含回绕前后消息的会话都会中招。我库中检测到 4 个（最大一个 1 万多条消息），其中两个主工作会话自 8/14 19:22 起即静默失效，直到今天全库排查才发现。 复现步骤 1. 在旧版本中创建会话并产生若干消息（ID 为 ff... 前缀）； 2. 升级到 1.17.4； 3. 在该会话中发送新消息； 4. 观察：消息写入 DB，但服务端日志仅 loop step=0 → exiting loop，无回复。 期望行为 消息的"最新"判断应基于时间（time_created）或使用可排序 ID，保证新消息一定被处理。 可行的修复方向 - latest() / 退出判断改按时间而非 ID 字典序； - 修复 ID 生成器的回绕，保证 ID 字典序与时间序一致。 本地已执行的临时补救（供参考） 对受影响会话的所有消息按时间重排了消息 ID（同步改写 parentID、part.message_id、part.data.messageID、compaction 的 tail_start_id），已确认会话可恢复正常对话。但这只能自救当前库，建议官方修复并考虑提供迁移工具。 ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signal.title: Ascending ID space wrapped on 2026-08-14: sessions created before that instant silently stop accepting new messages
signal.text: ## Summary `Identifier.create()` truncates the encoded timestamp to 6 bytes, so the ascending ID space wraps every ~795 days. **It wrapped on `2026-08-14T11:19:55.136Z`.** Since then, every freshly minted message ID sorts *lexicographically before* every ID written prior to that instant. Because the session engine resolves "newest" by lexicographic ID ordering, any session whose messages predate the wrap silently stops accepting new input: prompts and `/compact` are persisted but never served, and the agent appears to do nothing at all. ## Root cause `packages/opencode/src/id/id.ts`: ```js let now = BigInt(currentTimestamp) * BigInt(0x1000) + BigInt(counter) now = direction === "descending" ? ~now : now const timeBytes = Buffer.alloc(6) // <-- 48 bits only for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) { timeBytes[i] = Number((now >> BigInt(40 - 8 * i)) & BigInt(0xff)) } ``` `timestamp * 0x1000` needs 53 bits today but only the low 48 are kept, so the value wraps every `2^36` ms = 68 719 476 736 ms ≈ **795.4 days**. ``` last wrap : 2026-08-14T11:19:55.136Z next wrap : 2028-10-17T20:04:31.872Z id minted 1 min before wrap : msg_fffff15a0001… id minted 1 min after wrap : msg_00000ea60001… "msg_00000ea60001…" < "msg_fffff15a0001…" // ordering inverted ``` ## Observed impact Real IDs from an affected session (144k messages, session spans the wrap): ``` last message before wrap : msg_ffff07b29001lvZ1aOBcxm1fBY 2026-08-14T11:02:58Z first message after wrap : msg_00003f7d6001SjWSlWsUjBmLWQ 2026-08-14T11:24:15Z ``` Consequences in that session, reproduced against the real data: - `MessageV2.filterCompacted` walks the stream in descending-ID order and stops at the retained compaction tail, so post-wrap messages are **never reached** — 92 of 561 messages walked, and the three newest (two `/compact` markers and a user prompt) are absent from the returned view. - `MessageV2.latest()` therefore reports an old, already-closed turn as the most recent one, the loop exits on its break invariant without issuing a request, and the user sees **no reaction at all** — no error, no assistant message. - The same applies to any code deriving recency from IDs (queued-prompt lookup, run anchoring). The relevant code even documents the assumption being violated: ``` // Derive each binding by max id (MessageID is monotonic via MessageID.ascending) ``` ## Reproduction 1. Use any session containing messages created before `2026-08-14T11:19:55Z`. 2. Send a prompt, or run `/compact`. 3. The message is persisted, but no assistant turn ever starts. Sessions created *after* the wrap behave normally — until the next wrap in October 2028. ## Scope Anyone who resumes a pre-wrap session is affected, on every install, regardless of version: the trigger is wall-clock time, not code. In the store I inspected, 2 281 of 2 310 sessions predate the wrap. ## Suggested fixes 1. **Widen the encoded field** so the timestamp is not truncated (breaks ID comparability with existing IDs, but stops future wraps). 2. **Mint monotonically per scope**: when generating an ID, if it does not sort after the highest existing ID of that session, mint past that high-water mark. This repairs pre-wrap sessions without changing the ID format: ```js export function monotonic(generated: string, highest: string | undefined): string { if (highest === undefined || generated > highest) return generated const start = highest.indexOf("_") + 1 const bumped = (BigInt("0x" + highest.slice(start, start + 12)) + 1n).toString(16).padStart(12, "0") if (bumped.length > 12) return generated return highest.slice(0, start) + bumped + generated.slice(generated.indexOf("_") + 13) } ``` 3. **Stop deriving recency from ID ordering** and use `time_created` (already stored and correct) — the most robust fix, but the widest change. Happy to open a PR for whichever direction you prefer.
signal.author: menoxz

signal.title: Message ID counter overflow (wrap-around) breaks session loop — new messages silently ignored in older sessions
signal.text: ### Description ### Summary The message ID counter (12-hex-digit component after the `msg_` prefix) wrapped around from `fffb` back to `0035` on Aug 15, 2026 (after ~2 months of use). Because the session loop and `MessageV2.latest()` determine "newest message" via **lexicographic string comparison of message IDs** (not by timestamp), every message created after the wrap-around is considered *older* than all pre-wrap messages. As a result, **any user message sent in a pre-existing session is silently ignored**: the agent loop exits at `step=0` without ever calling the model. Newly created sessions work fine (their IDs are internally consistent), which makes the bug confusing to diagnose. ### Environment - OS: Windows 10 (also likely platform-independent) - opencode desktop app (`@opencode-aidesktop`), version: `[fill in your exact version from the app]` - Data migrated from JSON storage to SQLite (`opencode.db`) on Jun 16, 2026 - Provider/model: `[e.g. zhipuai / glm-5.2]` (irrelevant to the bug) ### Steps to reproduce 1. Use opencode daily for ~2 months (until the message ID counter passes `ffff` and wraps to `0000`). - Faster repro on a scratch install: manually insert messages with IDs near `msg_ffff...` and then send a new message. 2. Open a session created **before** the counter wrapped around. 3. Send any message (e.g. `hello`). ### Actual behavior - The user message is persisted (present in the `message` table with its parts), but no assistant response is ever generated. - Log shows the loop exiting immediately without any LLM call: ``` level=INFO message=loop session.id=ses_XXXX step=0 level=INFO message="exiting loop" session.id=ses_XXXX ← ~10ms later ``` - Affects **all sessions that contain pre-wrap messages**. Restarting the app does not help. - Sessions created entirely after the wrap-around behave normally. ### Expected behavior Sending a message in any session should always trigger a model response, regardless of ID ordering. Message recency should be determined by creation time, not by string comparison of IDs. ### Root cause analysis 1. Exit condition in `SessionPrompt.run` (found in `app.asar`, `node-*.js` chunk): ```js if (lastAssistant2?.finish && !["tool-calls"].includes(lastAssistant2.finish) && !hasToolCalls3 && lastUser.id < lastAssistant2.id) { // string comparison! yield* exports_Effect.logInfo("exiting loop", { "session.id": sessionID }); break; } ``` 2. `MessageV2.latest()` also selects the latest user/assistant message by ID comparison: ```js if (info32.role === "user" && (!user || info32.id > user.id)) user = info32; if (info32.role === "assistant" && (!assistant2 || info32.id > assistant2.id)) assistant2 = info32; ``` 3. Message IDs look like `msg_<12-hex-counter><random-suffix>`. Evidence from my database (first 2-4 hex of counter vs. creation time): | Period | ID prefix (hex) | Notes | |---|---|---| | Jun 16, 2026 (first message) | `ed01` | counter start after migration | | Aug 14, 2026 (evening) | `ffed` … `fffb` | approaching top | | Aug 15, 2026 (morning) | `0035` | **wrapped around** | | Aug 15, 2026 (afternoon) | `0043` | continues | After the wrap, for any old session: `lastUser.id` (e.g. `msg_0043...`) `<` `lastAssistant2.id` (e.g. `msg_fffb...`) is always true, so the loop treats the new user message as already answered and exits. ### Suggested fix - Compare by `time_created` (with the existing same-millisecond `id` tiebreaker, e.g. the `older()` helper already used for cursor pagination), instead of raw string ID comparison in `latest()` and the loop-exit condition. - And/or generate message IDs with a monotonically increasing counter that cannot wrap (e.g. wider counter, or a per-database sequence table). ### Workaround (already applied locally) I hot-fixed my database by remapping all 2610 pre-wrap message IDs into the `00000001xxxx` low range (preserving order and random suffixes), cascading updates to `part.message_id` (10,704 rows), `message.data.parentID` (2,197), and in-JSON references (21). All affected sessions recovered immediately. Happy to share the Node script if useful for other affected users. ### Additional context - The same wrap-around will recur roughly every 2 months of active use until fixed upstream. - Event-table history references were intentionally left untouched (do not affect the loop), so event replay may still show old IDs. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version v1.17.9 ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signal.title: Run loop can never exit when message ids are not time-sortable (imported sessions loop until the provider 400s)
signal.text: ### Summary `SessionPrompt.runLoop` decides a turn is finished by comparing message ids as **plain strings**. That is only correct because opencode's own ids embed a timestamp. Any session whose ids do not sort chronologically — e.g. one produced by a third-party importer — can put the loop in a state where it never exits: opencode re-requests indefinitely, each request ending on an assistant message, which providers reject. On Anthropic the user-visible result is a generic `Unexpected server error`, with the real cause (`This model does not support assistant message prefill`) buried. ### Where `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts`, in `runLoop`: ```ts if ( lastAssistant?.finish && !["tool-calls"].includes(lastAssistant.finish) && !hasToolCalls && lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id // <-- lexicographic id comparison ) { yield* Effect.logInfo("exiting loop", { "session.id": sessionID }) break } ``` `MessageV2.latest()` selects the "last" user/assistant the same way. The invariant this relies on comes from `packages/schema/src/identifier.ts`: ids are a 12-hex-char prefix encoding `timestamp_ms * 0x1000 + counter`, plus 14 random chars — so they sort chronologically as strings. Nothing validates that invariant at the `import` boundary, and it is not documented in the `SessionV1` schema. ### Reproduction 1. Import a session whose message ids are random rather than time-sortable (I hit this with [baton](https://github.com/Kaseban/baton), which emitted `msg_<uuid>`; a hand-written JSON with random ids reproduces it too). 2. Resume it and send any prompt. 3. The first request succeeds. opencode then immediately issues a second request with the assistant's own reply appended, and the provider returns 400. Captured with a forwarding proxy in front of the provider: ``` req 1: 1035312B -> 200 OK response: "stop_reason":"end_turn" + "message_stop" req 2: 1035378B -> 400 "This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message." ``` The first response is a clean, complete turn — `end_turn`, `message_stop` — and opencode continues anyway. Failure is probabilistic in session length, because ~2.6% of random hex ids sort above a freshly generated native id: | messages | P(at least one imported id outranks the live ones) | observed | |---|---|---| | 3 | ~8% | worked | | 6 | ~15% | worked once, failed once | | 423 | ~100% | failed every attempt | Ruled out by testing, in case they look like suspects: plugins (reproduced with `--pure`), missing `step-start`/`step-finish` parts (synthesised them, no change), unpaired `tool_use`, unsigned thinking blocks, and empty message content. It reproduces with a structurally valid history — I replayed the exact captured payload standalone and it returned 200. ### Suggested fixes Either would resolve it; the first is the smaller change: 1. **Order by `time.created`** (falling back to id) in the loop test and in `MessageV2.latest()`, instead of comparing id strings. 2. **Break on a terminal finish reason regardless of ordering** — if `lastAssistant.finish === "stop"` and there are no pending tool calls, the turn is over; the id comparison is then only a tiebreaker. Worth considering alongside: a continuation request that would end on an assistant message is invalid for providers that disallow prefill, so guarding that at the request-building layer would turn this class of bug into a clear error rather than a loop. ### Related - #38620 — same seam (replay 400 with thinking + tool use) but a different trigger (`message.error !== undefined`); does not cover id ordering. - #21326, #25774 — orphaned/dangling `tool_use`; also this area, different cause. ### Environment opencode 1.18.4 · macOS arm64 (container, linux/arm64) · Anthropic-compatible endpoint (LiteLLM), `claude-opus-4-8`, `thinking: adaptive`. ### Note on the provider side Not an opencode bug, but it made diagnosis much harder: when the upstream rejected the request, the gateway's fallback chain retried on models that do not support `thinking: adaptive`, so both the original and fallback errors were collapsed into one opaque message. Surfacing the provider's `error.message` verbatim in the session log would have saved a lot of time here.

signal.title: [Bug] Agent loop produces duplicate responses due to non-monotonic MessageID comparison
signal.text: ## Description Agent loop fails to exit after `finish=stop` when the assistant message ID is lexicographically smaller than the user message ID, causing a duplicate LLM call and a second assistant response. In `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts`, the `runLoop` function uses a **string comparison** to decide whether to break the loop: ```typescript if ( lastAssistant?.finish && !["tool-calls"].includes(lastAssistant.finish) && !hasToolCalls && lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id // string lexicographic comparison ) { break } ``` `MessageID.ascending()` generates IDs like `msg_f93b221d1...`. These IDs are **not guaranteed to be lexicographically monotonic**. When the assistant message ID happens to sort before the user message ID, the condition `lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id` evaluates to `false`, the loop does not break, and a second LLM call is made — producing a duplicate assistant response. This only affects agents that return `finish=stop` without tool calls (e.g. a plan-mode / discussion agent). Agents that use `finish=tool-calls` follow a different code path and are unaffected. ## Concrete evidence Session with 5 consecutive duplicate pairs. Each pair: same `parentID`, two `finish=stop` assistant messages, gap of 2–32ms between them. | User message ID | First assistant ID | `user.id < asst1.id` | Second assistant ID | `user.id < asst2.id` | |---|---|---|---|---| | `msg_f93b221d1...` | `msg_f93b221b9...` | `false` ← loop continues | `msg_f93b2853f...` | `true` ← loop breaks | | `msg_f93b7b78b...` | `msg_f93b7b748...` | `false` ← loop continues | `msg_f93b7efa2...` | `true` ← loop breaks | | `msg_f93bb731c...` | `msg_f93bb72da...` | `false` ← loop continues | `msg_f93bbd637...` | `true` ← loop breaks | | `msg_f93c03ac5...` | `msg_f93c03a9e...` | `false` ← loop continues | `msg_f93c0b842...` | `true` ← loop breaks | | `msg_f93c23126...` | `msg_f93c230ef...` | `false` ← loop continues | `msg_f93c26a5d...` | `true` ← loop breaks | In all 5 cases, the first assistant message's ID is lexicographically **smaller** than the user's, so the loop runs one extra iteration and produces a second response. ## Plugins oh-my-openagent@latest ## OpenCode version 1.18.5 ## Steps to reproduce 1. Use an agent that responds with text only (no tool calls), returning `finish=stop` directly. 2. Send a message. In ~some cases (when `MessageID.ascending()` produces an assistant ID that sorts before the user ID), the agent will respond twice with similar but slightly different content. 3. The issue is intermittent because it depends on ID generation, but happens frequently in sessions with many turns. ## Suggested fix Replace the string ID comparison with a more reliable ordering check. Options: - Compare by `time.created` timestamps instead of ID strings - Use a numeric counter that is guaranteed monotonic - Or at minimum, don't use the ID comparison as the loop exit gate — `finish=stop` (when not `tool-calls` and no pending tool calls) should be sufficient to break ## Operating System macOS 15.7.7 (x64) ## Terminal OpenChamber (Electron app, opencode v1.18.5)
signal.author: woohahahaaa

signal.title: Web prompts can stop after the first reply when client and server clocks differ
signal.text: ### Description I ran into a behavior when using `opencode serve` with the Web UI: the first message received a normal assistant response, but subsequent messages were persisted as user messages without triggering another assistant response. The same model and configuration worked normally in the terminal/TUI. After some debugging, this seems related to Web client-generated `messageID`s and clock skew between the browser/client device and the server. ### What I observed 1. Start opencode with `opencode serve`. 2. Open the Web UI from a browser. 3. Send the first message. 4. The assistant responds normally. 5. Send additional messages. 6. The later user messages are persisted in the database. 7. No new assistant message is created. 8. The server log shows: ```text session.prompt ... exiting loop ``` ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start `opencode serve`. 2. Open the Web UI from a browser/device whose clock differs from the server clock. 3. Send a first message. 4. Wait for the assistant response. 5. Send another message. 6. Observe that the later user message is persisted, but no new assistant response is generated. ### Debugging notes In the database, the later user messages had later `time_created` values, but their `messageID`s sorted before the first assistant message. In my environment, the server clock was about 170 seconds ahead of the client/browser device that was accessing the Web UI. After decoding the timestamp portion of the message IDs, the sequence looked roughly like this: ```text user1 09:38:26 assistant1 09:41:16 user2 09:38:37 user3 09:38:38 user4 09:38:39 ``` So `user2`, `user3`, and `user4` were sent after `assistant1`, but their IDs still sorted before `assistant1`. I noticed this condition in `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts`: ```ts if ( lastAssistant?.finish && !["tool-calls"].includes(lastAssistant.finish) && !hasToolCalls && lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id ) { yield* slog.info("exiting loop") break } ``` My understanding is that, in the Web UI case, the user message ID can be generated using the browser/client device clock, while the assistant message ID is generated using the server clock. If those clocks differ enough, the ID ordering may not match the actual conversation order, and the prompt loop may conclude that the latest user message has already been answered. ### Additional check I also tested sending a prompt directly to the server API without providing a client-generated `messageID`, allowing the server to generate the user message ID. In that case, the subsequent assistant response was triggered correctly. ### Impact This may be more likely to happen when using the Web UI from another device, for example: - accessing `opencode serve` from a phone or another computer - the browser/client device clock differs from the server clock - the server clock itself is not synchronized The user-facing behavior is a little confusing because the message appears to be sent successfully, but no assistant response appears. ### Question Would it make sense to avoid relying on ordering between client-generated user message IDs and server-generated assistant message IDs in this path? For example, perhaps Web prompts could have their final user message IDs generated or normalized on the server, or this loop condition could use a server-trusted ordering mechanism instead. ### Plugins None ### OpenCode version 1.14.25 ### Operating System Ubuntu 24.04 ### Terminal zsh
signal.author: Jovines
